items.x: Hunter-gatherers in the Levant settle in round stone houses and harvest wild grain with flint sickles.
Caine kills Abel in the fields, is cursed, and goes into the wilderness east of Eden.
As farming begins, the Garou start to cull the growing human herds; the Impergium lasts about three thousand years (W20 pdf 71).
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: In the reckoning of the Fallen, the angels who loved humanity rebel against Heaven at the dawn of the human race and are cast down.
Hunter-gatherers in Japan make some of the world's oldest pottery.
In the lore of Ur and Babylon, Lilith is the first woman, Adam's equal, and is cast out of Eden into the unformed world (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4).

items.t: Huts by the Sea of Galilee
items.x: Earlier hunters at Ohalo left brush huts and ground wild barley; their heirs settle the same shores.
A camp of tents and hearths in southern Chile shows people at the far end of the Americas.
Harpoon fishers live along the swollen lakes of east Africa.
Hunters on the Siberian steppe build huts of mammoth bone.
The great painted caves of France and Spain are already thousands of years old.
Garou lorekeepers read the painted beasts as the first record of the spirits humans saw.
Kithain say that in these years every child's dream crossed freely into the waking world.
The Fallen walk the young world openly and war with the loyal hosts; humans worship and fear them.
Hunters near later Beijing bury their dead with beads and red ochre.
Hunters in a Moroccan cave bury their dead with ochre and horn cores.
Late Ice Age hunters shelter in the caves of the Moravian Karst and follow reindeer and horse across the plain.
Hunters in the caves of the Zagros begin to stay through the year.
Hunters still cross the narrowing land bridge from Siberia before the sea closes it.
The cold snap called the Younger Dryas breaks; forests spread north and the great herds thin.

items.t: The ice gives up the north
items.x: Reindeer hunters follow the melting ice into Denmark and southern Sweden.
People settle by the spring at Jericho, one of the oldest continuously lived-in places.
Villagers on the Euphrates are among the first to plant rye when wild food fails.

items.t: The first sowing as a working
items.x: Verbena tell that the first seed sown on purpose was an act of will over the world.
Hunters camp by the north German lakes and cast offerings into them.
Hunters raise carved stone pillars on a hill in Anatolia, a sacred place built before farming.

items.t: The carved beasts on the hill
items.x: The foxes, vultures and boars carved at Gobekli Tepe are read by Garou lorekeepers as a caern raised in honour of the Fera.
Jomon hunters shape small clay figures with swollen bodies and blank faces.
Mammoths, horses and giant sloths die out across the Americas as hunters spread.
Uktena tales mourn the great beasts of the Americas, and blame neither humans nor the cold alone.
lk: The Shadow Lords in the Americas

items.x: In the wilderness Caine finds Lilith, who teaches the first powers of the blood and is later betrayed.
Villagers near Jericho keep figs that only grow from cuttings, the oldest tended tree.
Jomon families live through the year in sunken houses by the shore.
Bound to a crone by her blood, Caine in turn gives Zillah his blood for three nights and marries her (Book of Nod pdf 12-13).
Lilith's cult, the Bahari, keep her teaching; in their telling Caine's line turns on her for thirteen generations (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4-5).
Hunters on the Korean coast fire clay pots.
Monsoon rains spread north; lakes and rivers fill the Sahara.
Round houses stand by the Euphrates at Mureybet, with bull skulls in the walls.
Wheat, barley and lentils are first sown on purpose in the hills of the Fertile Crescent.
The dead of the first villages linger in the Shadowlands, with no city or ferryman to guide them.
Hunters with fluted spear points have spread through both Americas.
Villagers near Gobekli Tepe build a cult house with carved pillars of their own.
Rising seas cover the land bridge that joined Java, Sumatra and Borneo.

items.t: The Wan Kuei before the cycle
items.x: Kuei-jin legend holds that the dead of this age rose hungry with no court to guide them.
A band of foragers by Lake Turkana is killed with arrows and clubs, the oldest known battle.
Herders in the Zagros keep the first tame goats.
Farmers cross the sea to Cyprus with cattle, deer and goats.
Silent Strider lore says the dead of Nataruk were the first humans to fall in a Garou-driven cull in Africa.
Wild boar are bred into pigs in the hills of Anatolia and the Zagros.
The first people cross to Ireland and camp by its rivers.
Signs scratched on shell at Jiahu may be among the oldest marks of meaning in China.
Wild aurochs and mouflon are bred into cattle and sheep in Anatolia and the upper Euphrates.

items.t: The laws of the First City
items.x: Caine forbids the Second Generation to make more childer; the command is broken.
After the Time of Atrocities and the Long March, the war of Heaven and the Fallen calms into the Time of Babel (Houses of the Fallen pdf 19, 73).
People in coastal Peru grow squash and peppers.
Foragers on the north China plain begin to plant millet.
The Book of Nod tradition holds that Caine's curse kept even the First City's mortals from harming him.
A dugout canoe of pine is made in the Netherlands, the oldest boat yet found.
A woman is buried with a grinding stone in central Texas.

items.t: The wall and tower of Jericho
items.x: Jericho's people build a stone wall and round tower, among the first public works anywhere.
Painters in the Sahara mountains draw floating figures with round heads.
The Second Generation Embrace the thirteen who will be remembered as the Antediluvians.
Flax is grown in the Near East for oil and fibre.
Noddists say the Second Generation each chose four childer, against Caine's word.
Fishers on the Karelian isthmus weave a willow net with bark floats.
Caine founds Enoch and Embraces the Second Generation; mortals and the childer live under one ruler.
Rice is first farmed along the middle Yangtze in China.

items.t: Squash and gourds in the Americas
items.x: People in the Americas begin to grow squash and gourds.

items.t: The Fallen cast into the Abyss
items.x: The rebel angels are locked away in the Abyss; a few escape the binding as the Earthbound.

items.t: The antler masks of Star Carr
items.x: Hunters by a lake in Yorkshire wear red-deer antler headdresses, perhaps for rites.
People in the Oaxaca valley of Mexico grow the first tamed squash.
Fishers and hunters camp along the Nile, gathering wild grain.
Hunters roam a Britain still joined to Europe.
Hunters live on the high plain around Lake Titicaca.
Asian shapeshifter tales say the changing breeds of the east kept their own courts and their own war.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Potters press twisted cords into wet clay, the mark that names the age.
Villagers in the Zagros keep goats in mud-brick pens.
A village of mud houses at Jarmo in the Zagros farms wheat and barley.
In some tellings the Third Generation kill their own sires after the Flood; in others the Second simply vanish.
The villagers of Mehrgarh bury their dead with turquoise and shell from far away.

items.t: The paintings of Serra da Capivara
items.x: Painters in north-east Brazil cover rock shelters with dancers and hunters.
Hunters in Greece sail to Melos for obsidian, the first sea trade in the Aegean.
Villagers on the Ganges plain gather and later grow rice.
Lakes fill the Arabian interior and herders follow them.
A town of mud-brick houses entered through the roofs grows on the Konya plain, home to several thousand.
Some Noddists claim the bull horns and vulture paintings of Catalhoyuk mark a town that fed the First City.
Villagers near Amman shape tall plaster figures with staring eyes.
The houses of Catalhoyuk keep bull skulls set into plastered benches.
Cave dwellers in Peru keep beans and chili peppers.
Wraith lore holds that the dead of Catalhoyuk, buried under their own beds, stayed bound to their families.
Hunters at the Iron Gates bury their dead under trapezoid houses by the river.
Painters in central India draw hunters and animals on the shelters.
Herders begin to keep sheep for their wool as well as meat.
Villagers at Dadiwan paint the first pots of north China.
Hunters build round huts above the river Bann.
Farming families cross from Anatolia into Greece and the Balkans.
A farming village rises at Mehrgarh below the Bolan Pass, ancestor of the Indus cities.
Villagers at Jiahu in China play flutes of crane bone and scratch signs on tortoise shell.
Sixteen tribes meet and agree to end the Impergium, nearly nine thousand years before the modern nights (W20 pdf 40-41, 71).
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Garou lorekeepers tell that the Wyld, the Weaver and the Wyrm once kept the balance, before the Weaver went mad and bound the Wyrm.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.t: The rock paintings of the Sahara
items.x: Herders paint cattle, giraffes and dancers on the rocks of a green Sahara.
The people of Jericho keep their dead's skulls, rebuilt in plaster with shell eyes.
Wraith lore holds that the plastered skulls of Jericho were Fetters, keeping the first dead close to the living.
Villagers on the Huai river carve flutes from crane bone and scratch signs on tortoise shells.
Highlanders in New Guinea drain swamps to grow taro and bananas, among the first farmers anywhere.
Fishers along the Nile and the Sahara lakes make pots with wavy lines.
Farmers settle the Balikh valley in Syria.
Farmers of Thessaly build Sesklo, one of Europe's first villages.
Euthanatoi tradition places its first teachers of the wheel of life in this age.
The Fallen claim some of the first harvest spirits were Earthbound wearing new names.
Foragers in North America begin piling earth for camps and graves.
Caught in the Weaver's web, the Wyrm goes mad and splits into Beast-of-War, Eater-of-Souls and the Defiler (W20 Book of the Wyrm pdf 12-14).
The first farming villages spread into northern Mesopotamia.
After the Impergium the Fera rise against the Garou, and the Garou turn on the changing breeds; many lines are hunted near to their end (Tribebook Silent Striders pdf 16).
Mages remember the Mythic Age as a time before consensus, when gods and spirits answered common people.
Foragers in northern Thailand gather nuts, beans and peppers.
In the War of Rage, Garou packs burn the Bastet dens near the first towns.
Herders gather by a seasonal lake in the Egyptian desert.

items.t: The rock art of the Acacus
items.x: Herders paint and carve the rocks of the Acacus mountains.
A new people rebuild Jericho with rectangular houses and plaster floors.
Jars at Jiahu hold traces of a drink of rice, honey and fruit.
The rising sea covers the low land between Britain and the continent.
In Kithain legend the fae live beside mortals, and the Dreaming touches every field.
Farmers of the Starcevo culture settle the Danube and its rivers.
Potters in northern Mesopotamia make fine painted ware.
Foragers in the Tehuacan valley begin to grow squash and chili.
Bear-folk tales say the Garou killed their healers through this age.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: A wall painting at Catalhoyuk may show the twin-peaked volcano above the town.
Hunters of coastal Peru camp in the dry valleys.
Farmers spread up the Tisza onto the Hungarian plain.
A sudden cooling lasting two centuries strains the first farms of Europe and the Near East.
Two centuries of drought and cold drive villages from the uplands.
A great undersea slide off Norway sends a tsunami across the North Sea coasts.
Wraiths tell that the Storegga wave left a whole shore of the dead in the Shadowlands at once.
Farmers in southern Mesopotamia dig canals from the rivers to water their fields.
A great flood destroys Enoch; the Second Generation die or vanish, and their childer rule the ruins.
The Kuei-jin speak of the oldest age, when the courts of Heaven and the Yomi kept the Great Cycle turning.
Bands of hunters and fishers still live by the rivers of Moravia before the farmers come.
The rains make the Sahara a grassland; herders paint cattle, giraffes and dancers on the rocks of Tassili.
Farmers at Choga Mami dig the first irrigation channels.
Farmers by the Faiyum lake grow barley and keep goats.
Rice farmers from the Chinese coast settle Taiwan; their tongue will spread across the Pacific.
New Guinea gardeners grow bananas and sugar cane.

items.t: The Fall of the August Personages
items.x: Kuei-jin legend tells of a court in the east that fell before history began.
The rising sea cuts Britain from the continent.
Farmers dig ditched villages on the plain of Apulia.
Fishers by the Danube's Iron Gates carve river-stone heads with fish faces.
After the Flood, Brujah Embraces Troile, who will later destroy the sire (V20 Dark Ages pdf 45).
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: A jar at Hajji Firuz in Iran holds traces of wine.
Noddist tradition says each ruler of the Second City brought one art of the blood to its height.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Fishers and hunters settle along the Nile near later Khartoum.
A great village mound grows at Karanovo in Thrace.
Some scholars hold that the Black Sea filled quickly from the Mediterranean about now, drowning its shore villages.
Farmers move inland as the coasts change.
Farming villages spread along the edge of the Indus plain.
Linear Pottery farmers settle the loess plains of southern Moravia in long timber houses.
The first fields cut into the Moravian woods; Garou of the region mark where the farmers may go and where they may not.

items.t: The long houses and their dead
items.x: The Linear Pottery farmers of Moravia bury their dead beside the villages, crouched with pots and adzes.
The Baali begin in the Second City; their leader leads them against it and is beaten back (V20 pdf 402).
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Farmers of the Ubaid culture settle the southern marshes.
Millet farmers spread along the middle Yellow River.
Painters in eastern Spain draw hunters, archers and battles on rock shelters.
Kithain tradition places the reign of the first fae kings in Ireland in this age.
Foragers along the Bug and Dniester begin to keep pigs and plant wheat.
Farmers in the Andes grow the first potatoes.
At Talheim in Germany a whole farming community is killed and buried in one pit.
Another farming village is killed and buried in a ditch, legs broken.
Villages spread over the plain of Susa.
Long houses forty metres long stand in rows on the loess of Moravia.
Villagers at Cishan store millet in hundreds of pits.
The people of Mehrgarh grow cotton.
The Third Generation raise a new city after the Flood, each ruling a quarter with their own childer.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Eridu, held by later Sumerians to be the first city of kings, builds its first temple to the water god Enki.
Painted-pottery villages spread along the Yellow River.
Farmers in Mexico breed maize from the wild grass teosinte.
The Ratkin say they were made to keep the human herds small, and took to the first cities when the Impergium ended.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Villagers at Hemudu near the Yangtze mouth build timber houses on stilts and grow rice.
Potters of the Vinca culture scratch signs on clay that some take for an early script.
Hemudu villagers grow rice in wet fields and build their houses on stilts.
A village of round houses with a ditch grows at Banpo near later Xi'an.
The rock painters of the Sahara turn from wild beasts to cattle herds.
Foragers by the Tagus bury their dead in great mounds of shells.
Fishers on the Atacama coast make the oldest mummies in the world.
Mummy lore says the Chinchorro had their own ways of keeping the soul near the body, with no spell of life.
Wraiths of the Americas name the Chinchorro dead among the oldest wraiths still bound to their bodies.
Herders set up a ring of standing stones in the desert.
Mummy lore says the Nabta stones watched the stars that Egypt's priests would later read for the dead.
Farmers of central Europe build great round ditched enclosures, some of them in Moravia, perhaps for gatherings and rites.
Farmers build a ring of ditch and palisade at Goseck, open to the winter sunrise.
Stone tombs and standing stones rise in Brittany.
The Encyclopaedia records a War of Rage fought across Siberia.
The shrine at Eridu is rebuilt on a platform.
Villages of the Hongshan culture spread in the north-east.
Foragers in Mexico grow avocados and cotton.
Farmers of southern Moravia make clay figurines of women for their homes and shrines.
A great stone cairn with eleven passage graves rises in Brittany.
Potters at Mehrgarh use the slow wheel.
Villages of the Dawenkou culture spread across Shandong.
A grave at Varna on the Black Sea holds the oldest worked gold yet found.
The tales of the Kithain place the Mythic Age in the time when the long stone rows of Carnac were raised.
Smiths in the Balkans smelt copper; the Copper Age begins.
The Bastet keep courts among the city kings of Sumer, as their tales hold.
Each rebuilding raises Eridu's temple higher, toward the later ziggurat.

items.t: The oldest leaf of the Book of Nod
items.x: By the reckoning of the book's own scholar, its oldest fragment was written just before Sumer (Book of Nod pdf 19).
Farmers of Ukraine and Moldova build towns of thousands of houses and burn them every few generations.
Smiths in the Negev and the Jordan valley smelt copper.
Villagers at Ban Chiang bury their dead with painted pots.
Kithain say the farmers of Trypillia burned their towns to let the Dreaming out.

items.t: The quarrels of the Third Generation
items.x: The rulers of the Second City feud over power and their childer, and the city's peace frays.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Hundreds of copper crowns, maces and wands are hidden in a cave by the Dead Sea.
Farmers on the lower Danube work gold and copper.
Ubaid culture spreads from southern Mesopotamia up the rivers and along the Gulf.
Thousands of standing stones are set in rows at Carnac.
A chief at Varna is buried with a gold sceptre and a gold sheath.
Saulot, founder of the Salubri, studies in the Second City and travels east to seek the end of the Beast.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Many of the copper-working towns of the Balkans are abandoned.
Carvers in north-east China make coiled pig-dragons of jade.
Fishers at Huaca Prieta weave cotton and build a mound by the sea.
The Brujah say their founder Troile prized the Second City above all and fought its fall.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: The great standing stone at Locmariaquer is raised, twenty metres long.
The first wheels turn in Mesopotamia and on the steppe.
Steppe people north of the Black Sea begin to keep and ride horses.

items.t: The fall of the Second City
items.x: The Second City falls to war and the childer's revolt; the Antediluvians scatter across the world.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: The green Sahara turns to desert; herders move toward the Nile and the south.
Farmers of the Lengyel culture build fortified villages in southern Moravia.
The Botai people of the Kazakh steppe keep herds of horses.
Herders in the high Andes tame the llama and the alpaca.
Farming comes to Britain from the continent.
Farmers of Upper Egypt bury their dead with ivory combs and fine pots.
Herders of the Deccan build great ash mounds.

items.t: Cobs of maize in Guila Naquitz
items.x: Small cobs of maize are kept in a cave in Oaxaca.
Brujah tellers say their founder argued for the mortals of the Second City and was not heard.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.t: A city of the dead below
items.x: Wraiths say the first dead of the cities built their own towns in the Shadowlands.
Korean villagers make comb-pattern pottery and grow millet.
After the Second City, the Third Generation go their ways: some to the mountains, some to the rivers, some into the sea of mortal peoples.
The founder of the Tzimisce leaves the ruins for the mountains to the north, toward the Carpathians.
Farmers in central Europe pull the first scratch ploughs with oxen.
Villagers in China keep silkworms and weave silk.
The temple at Eridu rises on its seventh rebuilding.

items.t: The hill folk of the Alps
items.x: Herders cross the high passes of the Alps with copper axes and flint.
Nosferatu tales tell how their founder was made monstrous by Caine's anger for the deeds of the Second City.
Copper tools reach Moravian farmers through trade from the Balkans.
A timber walkway is laid across the Somerset marshes.
A palace with stored grain and seals rules a valley in eastern Anatolia.
Hierakonpolis grows into the largest town of Upper Egypt.
Uruk becomes the largest city in the world, with tens of thousands living inside its walls.
The Silent Striders are cursed by Sutekh and can no longer rest in Egypt, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Farmers on Orkney build stone houses still standing.
The first village of Harappa grows on the Ravi.
A platform of stone rises in the Casma valley.
Islanders on Malta build great stone temples.
Farmers in Ireland raise passage tombs in the Boyne valley.
Uruk builds a great temple district for Inanna.
Farmers bury their dead in long earth barrows.
Fianna lore says the first barrows of Britain were raised on caerns.
Rice farmers of the middle Yangtze build walled towns.

items.t: The potter's wheel and the plough
items.x: Sumerians use the fast potter's wheel and the ox-drawn plough.
The towns of Upper Egypt grow rich under chiefs buried with painted pots.
In the legend of the Reborn, Osiris rules the Two Lands as a god-king, with Isis beside the throne.
The Silent Striders keep their oldest home among the shrines of the Nile.
The Encyclopaedia records a council that judged quarrels among the changing breeds.
The Baden culture's villages spread through Moravia, with wheeled carts and copper.
Steppe herders bury their chiefs under earth mounds called kurgans.

items.t: The first Gangrel run with the herds
items.x: The Gangrel tell that their founder ran with the horse peoples of the steppe, far from any city.
Uruk sets up trading towns on the upper Euphrates.
The A-Group people of Lower Nubia trade with Egypt.
The passage grave of Gavrinis is carved with swirling lines.
A walled town with canals grows near the Yangtze delta.
Villagers on the Ecuador coast make the first pottery of South America and small clay women.
Hermetic tradition places the first temple magicians in the towns of Upper Egypt.
Some dead of Hierakonpolis are buried with cut throats, perhaps as offerings.
Herders from the steppe begin to push west into central Europe.
The Get of Fenris and their kin lose a great northern hold, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Uruk's officials roll carved stone seals across clay.
A pot from Poland shows the oldest picture of a wheeled wagon.
Bodies buried in the hot sand of Gebelein dry into natural mummies.
The Reborn say Egypt learned from the sand that the body could be kept for the soul.
Herders with carts move onto the eastern steppe.
A man is shot with an arrow and dies on a pass in the Alps; the ice keeps the body for five thousand years.
The bear-changers refuse to fight the Garou or to teach them; the Encyclopaedia keeps the tale.

items.t: The scattered childer reach the rivers
items.x: Deduced: Set is ruling in Egypt by about 3000 BCE (Mummy 1st pdf 64) and the Baali hold Sumerian cities, so the Antediluvians' scattering after the Second City has reached the river kingdoms by 3300 BCE.
The first tablets record grain, beer, sheep and labourers' rations.
Kings of Abydos are buried with ivory labels, the first writing of Egypt.
Lapis lazuli from Badakhshan travels west to Mesopotamia and Egypt.
Setite lore holds that Sutekh ruled from a temple in the delta before Egypt was one land.
The great temples of Gozo are rebuilt in huge stones.
A marble face of a woman is carved at Uruk.
Scribes at Uruk press signs into clay tablets to keep the temple's accounts, the start of writing.
The first hieroglyphs are written in Upper Egypt.
Set kills Osiris and scatters the body across Egypt, and takes the throne.
Isis gathers the pieces of Osiris and, with the help of the gods, works the Spell of Life; Osiris rises.
The Followers of Set tell that their founder walked among the first kings of Egypt and was worshipped as a god.
A dishonour of the War of Rage the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The passage tomb at Newgrange is built so the midwinter sunrise lights its inner chamber.
Kithain call the Boyne tombs the first hollow hills, doors of the sidhe long before the Sundering.

items.t: The War of Rage ends in Egypt
items.x: Deduced: Rage Across Egypt has Egypt united only after the War of Rage (pdf 25), so the killing is over along the Nile before Narmer, about 3200 BCE.
Smiths alloy copper with arsenic and tin.
Knowth's great mound holds the most carved stone in western Europe.
Shell-workers of Gujarat trade bangles to the Indus towns.
Fianna tales put their oldest caern at the Boyne in the age of the great tombs.
An ivory knife handle shows a battle of ships on the Nile.

items.t: The Contendings of Horus and Set
items.x: Horus and Set fight for eighty years before the gods' court.
Towns of Sumer share one set of seals and trade together.
The king of Upper Egypt takes the Delta; the Narmer Palette shows the first king of a single Egypt.
Horus, son of Osiris and Isis, wars with Set for the throne of Egypt.
Farmers on Orkney build the stone village of Skara Brae, with stone beds and dressers.
A carved alabaster vase from Uruk shows a procession bringing offerings to Inanna.
The towns of the Susa plain unite as Elam, Sumer's old rival in the east.
Shahr-i Sokhta in the Iranian desert grows rich on lapis and tin.
The first kings found Memphis at the meeting of the Two Lands.
A circular bank and ditch is dug on Salisbury Plain; the stones come later.
Ur, Uruk, Lagash, Kish and Nippur grow into rival city-states, each with its own god.
Osiris shares the Spell of Life with chosen followers, the first of the Reborn who serve Horus.
In the reckoning of the Fallen, the gods the Sumerians worship are half-remembered faces of angels from before the Fall.
Towns of the Indus valley begin building with baked brick.
The Akashic Brotherhood counts its oldest roots among hermits in the mountains above the Indus.
Garou and Fera together bind great Banes in this age, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Scribes at Susa write in their own signs.
People of the Copper Age bury some of their dead in the caves of the Moravian Karst.
As more Cainites come to Egypt, Set's rule of the land weakens (Mummy 1st pdf 64).
Egyptian scribes write on sheets made from papyrus reeds.
Island carvers make flat marble figures with folded arms.
Farmers of the Amazon build raised fields and ditched villages.
lk: The First Comers to the Amazon

items.x: Rice farming reaches the river plains of Thailand.
Bastet lore says the Simba and the Bubasti were honoured by the god-kings as the cats of Ra.
Korean fishers leave great mounds of shells along the coast.

items.t: The plough with a seed drill
items.x: Sumerian farmers fix a funnel to the plough to sow as they go.
A deep layer of river silt at Shuruppak marks a great flood, the kind later remembered in the flood stories.
Herders who bury their dead with corded beakers and stone battle-axes settle across Moravia.
The early kings of Egypt are buried at Abydos with their servants.
Uruk's walls reach nine kilometres, later credited to Gilgamesh.
Mari is built as a round planned city on the middle Euphrates.
Noddists hold that the childer of the Antediluvians hid among the en-priests of Sumer.
An early temple mound stands in the Fortaleza valley.
Queen Merneith may have ruled Egypt for her young son.
Walled towns of black polished pottery rise along the Yellow River.

items.t: The First Comers to the Amazon
items.x: The changing breeds of the great forest settle the Amazon long before the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: The First Comers to the Amazon
