items.x: The Sumerian king list names Kish as the first city to hold kingship after the flood.
The Indus towns use one set of cube weights from the mountains to the sea.
A great ring of timber posts and houses rises near Stonehenge.
Nobles are buried in flat-topped brick tombs at Saqqara.
The first king of Kish named in his own inscriptions rules about now.
Gilgamesh, later the hero of the oldest written epic, rules Uruk about now.
Egypt's Old Kingdom begins, the age of the great pyramids.
The jade-working city of Liangzhu near the Yangtze mouth is abandoned, perhaps after floods.
Weavers of the Yangtze make silk with simple looms.
A walled copper-working town rises in south-east Spain.
The Reborn say the kings of the Old Kingdom tried to copy the Spell of Life with linen and salt.
Sumerian scribes start the lists of kings who ruled after the Flood.
Imhotep builds the step pyramid for King Djoser at Saqqara, the first great stone building.
Later Hermetic masters honour Imhotep as a founder of the arts of building, healing and writing.
Egypt keeps a calendar of 365 days in three seasons tied to the Nile flood.
Ur buries its princes with golden helmets and lyres.
King Sneferu builds the Bent and Red pyramids at Dahshur.
The kings and queens of Ur are buried with gold, lyres and dozens of attendants.
The great Indus cities lay out straight streets, drains and granaries.
The ravens tell how they were scorched black in the War of Rage; the Encyclopaedia keeps the tale.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The city of Caral in the Peruvian desert raises platform mounds, the oldest city of the Americas.
A shell and lapis box shows Ur at war and at peace.
Seals with a still unread script are used from the Indus to the Gulf.
The underground tomb of Hal Saflieni is cut into the rock of Malta.
Wraith lore names the Hypogeum's sounding chambers as a place where the dead were called to speak.
Harappa builds great brick halls, perhaps for grain.
The Great Pyramid of Khufu is finished at Giza, the tallest building on earth for nearly four thousand years.
The Shemsu-heru know the pyramid fields as places where the walls between the living and the dead are thin.
A cedar boat forty metres long is buried beside the Great Pyramid.
An official's logbook records hauling limestone for the Great Pyramid, the oldest papyrus with writing.
The Sphinx is carved from the bedrock at Giza.
The great sarsen circle and the trilithons are raised at Stonehenge.
The Fianna sing that the stone circles of Britain were raised over caerns, and that the rings still answer the moon.
Bell Beaker pottery and copper daggers spread from Iberia to Britain and central Europe.
Garou and Fera keep a truce at Lagash in Sumer for a time, before the War of Rage returns.
The great stone halls of the Ness of Brodgar stand between two stone rings on Orkney.
Bell Beaker people settle in Moravia beside the Corded Ware herders.
Mohenjo-daro's builders make a large waterproof brick bath, perhaps for rites.
Deduced: Earthbound says mortal sorcerers freed them thousands of years ago (pdf 13-18), and the oldest priest-kings are Sumer's, so the first are taken to wake about 2500 BCE.
Lagash and Umma fight for generations over a border field.
Sumerian brewers make many kinds of beer, sipped through straws.
A walled city with great reservoirs stands on an island in the Rann of Kutch.
Fishers of the Supe coast build platform mounds by the sea.
A town grows at Kerma above the third cataract of the Nile.
Akashic and Chakravanti scholars both read the seated horned figure of the Indus seals as one of their own.
A great circle of stones is raised on Orkney.
Eannatum of Lagash defeats Umma and sets up a stone showing vultures over the dead.
The kings of the fifth dynasty build open temples to Ra.
Urukagina of Lagash curbs the greed of priests and officials, the first known law reform.

items.t: The War of Rage seen by ravens
items.x: The Corax's own telling of the War of Rage, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Spells for the dead king's rise to the stars are carved inside the pyramid of Unas.
The Reborn read the Pyramid Texts as a clumsy echo of the true Spell of Life.
Ebla rules northern Syria from a palace full of tablets.
A man from the Alps is buried near Stonehenge with gold and copper.
Some Tremere scholars claim the Ebla archives name a ruler who never aged.
A painted limestone scribe sits with papyrus on his lap.
Thousands of clay tablets at Ebla in Syria record a trading city's business.
The Sumerian king list names Kubaba, a tavern keeper, as the only woman to rule Kish.
A vizier's advice on good conduct is copied for a thousand years.
Sargon founds the Akkadian empire, the first to rule all Mesopotamia.
Some Ventrue claim that their line advised the first kings of Akkad; the Brujah call it a boast.
Sargon's daughter Enheduanna, high priestess at Ur, writes hymns to Inanna, the first author known by name.
The Unetice culture works bronze in Bohemia and Moravia and trades tin and amber across central Europe.
Indus traders sail to Sumer with carnelian beads; Sumerians call the land Meluhha.
Akkadian spreads as the language of rule and trade.
A walled town at Taosi has a platform that may track the sun.
Smiths in Ireland beat gold collars called lunulae.
Scribes of Ebla write word lists in two languages.
Sargon's son crushes the cities of Sumer that rise against him.
Naram-Sin of Akkad calls himself a god and king of the four quarters.
A later poem says Akkad was cursed for Naram-Sin's sack of a temple; Noddists see a Cainite feud behind it.
Pepi II rules Egypt for perhaps ninety years; the Old Kingdom weakens.
A drought lasting decades strikes from Egypt to the Indus; Akkad collapses.
The Old Kingdom breaks apart into rival provinces after low Nile floods.
The Ananasi tell of their own losses in the War of Rage.
A great stone-walled town rises on the loess at Shimao in northern China.
The Nile floods fail and Egypt's provinces starve.

items.t: The great floods of the Yellow River
items.x: Floods and drought end many of the Longshan towns.
The great city of northern Mesopotamia is left empty in the drought.
Chiefs in Brittany are buried with bronze daggers under mounds.
Mountain raiders called the Gutians overrun Akkad.
Gudea rebuilds the temples of Lagash and leaves statues of himself at prayer.
Ur-Nammu rebuilds Sumer, raises the great ziggurat of Ur and issues a law code.
The oldest surviving law code sets fines in silver for injuries.
King Shulgi of Ur sets up a road network with rest houses and standard weights.
Ur-Nammu builds the great stepped temple of Nanna.
Bronze-working towns of the El Argar culture rise in south-east Spain.
Wraith tales say the servants buried with Ur's queens served them in the Shadowlands too.
Carnelian beads from the Indus are buried in the graves of Ur.
Chinese tradition places the first dynasty, the Xia, and the flood-tamer Yu the Great about now.
The Kuei-jin say the first dynasty was founded when the dragons of the rivers were bargained with, not beaten.
Mentuhotep II reunites Egypt from Thebes.
Mentuhotep II of Thebes reunites the Two Lands.
The Minoans build the first palaces at Knossos and Phaistos.
Garou tales of the War of Rage place a hidden lair of the changing breeds under the palace hills of Crete.
Chariots with spoked wheels appear on the steppe east of the Urals.
Peoples speaking an early Greek settle the Greek mainland.
The Garou wipe out the Bunyip of the far south, a crime the Encyclopaedia records.
The Unetice dead are buried crouched on their sides with bronze pins and rings.
The fortified towns of Sintashta on the steppe bury warriors with chariots.
The Ainu people's ancestors live in the northern islands of Japan.
Kindred of the East places the Ainu in the islands by this age, with their own bond to the spirits (Kindred of the Thousand Hells pdf 44).
The Elamites sack Ur; a lament mourns the city's end.
Walled towns of the Oxus civilisation stand in the oases of Bactria.
A temple of crossed hands rises in the Andes.
The first bronze reaches Denmark and Sweden in trade for amber.
A courtier's flight and return is written, Egypt's best-loved story.
Sailors of island south-east Asia use outrigger canoes.
Bone Gnawer tales claim they followed the herds of humans into the oasis towns.
Bahrain is Dilmun, the island of trade and paradise in Sumerian song.
Amenemhat I founds the twelfth dynasty and moves the court to Itjtawy.
Merchants from Assur keep a trading colony at Kanesh in Anatolia, sending tin and cloth.
Egypt builds great forts at the second cataract.
The great Indus cities shrink as rivers shift and trade fails.
Chiefs on the chalk downs of Wessex are buried with gold and amber.
Baltic amber passes through Moravia toward the south.
Hebrew tradition places the patriarch Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan about now.
Assyrian merchants at Kanesh write home about tin, cloth and debts.
A palace town at Erlitou may be the seat of the Xia.
Minoan scribes write a script still unread.
Kithain say the Cretan bull games fed the Dreaming as no other sport has.
Spells for the dead are painted inside coffins for anyone who can pay.
An Amorite dynasty takes Babylon, then a small town.
Senusret III curbs the nobles and pushes into Nubia.
The Baali tell that their first sire drew power from things older than Caine in the swamps of southern Mesopotamia.
An Egyptian scribe works out the volume of a cut pyramid.
Egyptian scribes copy problems of fractions and areas, later gathered in the Rhind papyrus.
Fera who flee the War of Rage hide among human peoples, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The palace archive of King Zimri-Lim at Mari records spies, prophets and diplomacy.
Babylonian scribes work in base sixty and know Pythagoras' rule a thousand years early.
Babylonian scribes write the story of a flood sent by the gods and one man who survives it.
Rivers of the eastern Indus shift and the towns along them empty.
Villagers in Mesoamerica make their first pots.
Unetice smiths in Moravia cast bronze axes and rings for trade.
Noddists read the Atrahasis flood as a memory of the flood that ended Enoch.
A walled town rises at Sanxingdui in Sichuan.
The Followers of Set grow strong in the cult centres of the Delta, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Hammurabi takes the throne of Babylon and spends thirty years making it an empire.
Sobekneferu rules Egypt as the first certain woman king.
Hammurabi destroys Mari, his former ally.
Hammurabi has his laws carved on a basalt stele: an eye for an eye, set by rank.
Bronze axes, rings and ingots are buried in hoards across Moravia, as offerings or savings.
Wraiths of the Unetice dead are said to linger over the hoards buried with their names.
Mari's letters record ecstatic prophets who carry messages from the gods to the king.
Babylonian loans, sales and marriages are sealed on clay before witnesses.
The Babylonian city of Mashkan-shapir is emptied, perhaps after a change in the river.
In Baali lore their city of Mashkan-shapir falls and the elder Nergal moves to Ashur (Clanbook Baali pdf 23-24).
A bronze disc inlaid with gold sun, moon and stars is buried on a hill in Germany.
Earthquakes wreck the Cretan palaces; they are rebuilt grander than before.
The Nubian city of Kerma rules the middle Nile and rivals Egypt.
The Hittites make Hattusa their capital.
Egypt splits between Theban kings and the Hyksos of the delta.
Smiths at Erlitou cast bronze vessels in clay moulds.
A chief is buried under a timber house in a mound in Thuringia.
Fortified towns on mounds stand on the Hungarian plain.
Foreign kings called the Hyksos rule the Nile Delta, bringing the horse and chariot to Egypt.
The Hyksos kings honour Set at Avaris; the Followers of Set count this a high time of their cult.
Hunters of the lower Mississippi raise great curved earth ridges in what is now Louisiana.
The Hyksos bring the horse and chariot to Egypt.
Mummy lore says the Shemsu-heru withdrew into the tombs while the Hyksos held the delta.
The volcano of Thera blows apart, burying the town of Akrotiri in ash and sending waves across the Aegean.
Kithain tales speak of a shining island of the Mythic Age lost to fire and sea; scholars point to Thera.
The Shang dynasty rules the Yellow River plain from walled capitals.
Mycenae's kings are buried with gold masks.
A Garou moot whose vote was never counted, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Shang diviners crack ox bones and turtle shells with heat and write the questions on them, China's oldest writing.
The Kuei-jin say the Shang kings spoke with true ancestors through the cracks, and the spirits answered.
Bronze Age settlements in Moravia gain ditches and palisades.
The Kassites take Babylon and rule it for four centuries.
A surgeon's manual describes wounds and how to treat them.
The last great Indus cities are abandoned.
Villagers on the Pacific coast of Mexico build a ballcourt.
The Reborn say Horus moved openly behind the Theban kings who drove out the Hyksos.
Hazor is the greatest city of Canaan.
The Hittite king Mursili I raids down the Euphrates and sacks Babylon.
Ahmose I drives out the Hyksos; Egypt's New Kingdom begins.
The Shemsu-heru are said to have fought beside Ahmose's army against the Followers of Set in the Delta.
Egyptians begin to bury spells for the afterlife on papyrus, later called the Book of the Dead.
Deduced: Mummy's sample Reborn are born about 2600 and 1273 BCE (Mummy 1st pdf 12, 69-77), so the Reborn are many by the New Kingdom.
Ahmose of Thebes takes Avaris and expels the Hyksos.
A gold death mask is laid over a king's face at Mycenae.
Thutmose I takes Kerma and the Nile to the fourth cataract.
Peoples speaking an Indo-Aryan tongue settle north India; the hymns of the Rigveda take shape.
Egypt's kings begin to be buried in hidden tombs in the Valley of the Kings.
Central Europeans bury their dead under earth mounds, the barrows of the Bronze Age.
Bronze Age barrows crown the ridges of Moravia; the Garou of the land take some for caerns and leave others well alone.
Mycenaean builders raise walls of stones so large later Greeks thought giants had moved them.
Lapita potters from the Bismarck islands begin settling the open Pacific.
Ugarit grows rich as a port between Egypt, Cyprus and the Hittites.
Shang kings offer cattle and captives to their ancestors.
Villages of the Gulf coast grow maize and build the first platforms.
A young woman is buried in Denmark in a corded skirt, in an oak coffin.
Get of Fenris tales say the sun chariots of the north were offerings to Sun himself.
A medical book lists hundreds of remedies and spells.
The horse lords of Mitanni rule northern Syria.
Hatshepsut takes the throne of Egypt as king and rules for about twenty years.

items.t: The Reed of Thoth and the Cupbearers of Isis
items.x: Hatshepsut and Thutmose III call a gathering that founds two lodges of magicians (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
Hatshepsut's ships sail down the Red Sea to Punt and bring back incense trees and ebony.
Hatshepsut builds her terraced temple at Deir el-Bahri.
Thutmose III defeats a league of Canaanite kings at Megiddo, the first battle recorded in detail.
Mycenaean Greeks take over the palace of Knossos and its Linear B scribes.
Some Cainite legends place an elder of the beast-blooded clans in the halls under Knossos.
Thutmose III takes Egypt's armies to the Euphrates seventeen times.
The Shang build a great walled city at Zhengzhou.
The kingdom of Mitanni rules northern Mesopotamia with chariot lords.
Kings of Egypt, Babylon, Mitanni and the Hittites write to each other as brothers and trade gold for horses.
The Encyclopaedia records the Bone Gnawers' tale of being the last and lowliest tribe.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Scribes at Ugarit write an alphabet in cuneiform signs.
Within a century the two Egyptian lodges split into more than a hundred rival sects (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
Mycenaean scribes write early Greek in Linear B.
Lapita potters stamp their pots with tooth-comb patterns.
Amenhotep III raises two huge statues of himself at Thebes.
Hermetic history says the Aten cult split the temple magicians.
Babylonian diviners write down thousands of omens from sheep livers and stars.
Suppiluliuma I makes the Hittites a great power.
The Reborn remember Akhenaten's reign, which the books put at 1364 to 1347 BCE, as a time when the old rites of the dead were shut away and the Shemsu-heru hid.
Akhenaten puts the sun disc Aten above all other gods and builds a new capital at Amarna.
Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a great power.
Thinkers of the Ganges plain begin the speculation later written in the Upanishads.
Kings write to Pharaoh in Akkadian about gold, brides and war.
A ship laden with copper, tin, glass and ebony sinks off the Lycian coast.
The sculptor Thutmose carves the painted bust of Queen Nefertiti.
The boy king Tutankhamun abandons Amarna and restores the old gods.
A widowed queen of Egypt asks the Hittite king for a son to marry.
Tutankhamun dies young and is buried with a small but rich tomb that robbers miss.
Central Europeans begin to burn their dead and bury the ashes in urns in large cemeteries.
Hillforts ringed with earth and timber are built on the heights of Moravia.
Burning the dead changes nothing for the wraiths of Moravia's urnfields, who gather in the shadow of the cemeteries.
An old battle site of the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The Shang queen and general Fu Hao leads armies and is buried with hundreds of bronzes.
The Shang move their capital to Anyang.
Carvings of warriors and cut-up captives line a temple in the Casma valley.
Farmers divide the British downs into small square fields.
Wraith lore says many Egyptian dead lost their Fetters when the tombs were robbed.
The tomb builders' village keeps records of quarrels, loans and absences.
Ramesses II begins a reign of sixty-six years and carves his temples at Abu Simbel.
Ramesses II cuts his great temples into the cliffs of Nubia.
Egyptians and Hittites fight the largest chariot battle known at Kadesh; both claim victory.
Queen Puduhepa writes to Egypt as an equal of Pharaoh.
Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III sign a peace treaty, copies of which survive in both tongues.
The citadel of Troy is sacked about now, the event that may lie behind the Iliad.
Thousands fight at a river crossing in northern Germany, the oldest large battle known in Europe.
A people called Israel is first named in Canaan, on a stone of Pharaoh Merneptah in 1208.
In later hunter lore the judges and prophets of Israel are the first mortals remembered for standing against the night's creatures by faith alone.
The standard version of the Epic of Gilgamesh is written down.
Babylon honours Marduk with a twelve-day feast.
Shang kings are buried with chariots and horses.
Ramesses II's queen Nefertari is buried in the finest painted tomb in Egypt.
Setite tradition says the family of Ramesses II came from Set's own city.
Merneptah's victory stele names Israel for the first time.
Mycenae's walls are rebuilt with the Lion Gate.
Ugarit's king writes that enemy ships are burning his land.
Hattusa is abandoned and burned; the Hittite empire breaks up.
The Olmec build their first ceremonial centre at San Lorenzo and carve colossal stone heads.
The Pure Ones tell that their tribes held the lands across the ocean long before the Garou of Europe came, with their own peace among the breeds.
lk: The Shadow Lords in the Americas

items.t: The Caern of the Fallen Star
items.x: A caern raised where a star fell, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The hymns of the Rigveda reach their final form, though still learned by heart.

items.t: Bronze hoards of the Urnfield age
items.x: Moravian smiths bury hoards of sickles, axes and scrap bronze.
The palace of Pylos burns, baking its clay records hard.
Hermetic historians trace the first Greek oracles to the oak of Dodona, older than Delphi.
Villages of the Ganges plain make grey painted pots.
A shrine is built on the site that will become Chavin.
Libyan tribes press on Egypt's western delta.

items.t: The Wyrm feeds on the fall
items.x: Garou say the burning of the palaces was a feast for the Wyrm.
Trade links Iberia, Brittany, Britain and Ireland by sea.
The Hittite capital is burned and left empty.

items.t: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
items.x: Ramesses III turns back the Sea Peoples in a battle on the Nile Delta, carved on the walls of Medinet Habu.
Refugees and raiders settle the coasts of Cyprus.
Ugarit, Mycenae, Pylos and many other cities fall to raiders, drought and quakes; trade and writing vanish across the region.
The fall of the Bronze Age cities sends old Cainites into long sleep; some claim the collapse was a war among them.
Ramesses III beats the Sea Peoples in the mouths of the Nile and carves the battle at Medinet Habu.
The Hittite viceroys of Carchemish survive the fall and rule as Great Kings.
The Peleset settle Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath.
Shang kings after Wu Ding fight the Qiang in the west.
Cypriot smiths make the first everyday iron knives of the Aegean.
Small kingdoms of Luwian speakers keep the Hittite name alive in Syria.
Tomb builders at Deir el-Medina stop work when their grain rations do not come.
The citadel of Mycenae is burned once more.
The Canaanite city of Megiddo is burned.
Ramesses IV sends great quarrying parties into the Wadi Hammamat.
Farmers raise the first ramparts on the hills of southern Britain.
Wives of Ramesses III plot his murder; the trial records survive.
The Reborn say the harem plot used wax figures, and that a Setite sorcerer made them.
Shutruk-Nahhunte of Elam carries Hammurabi's law stele to Susa.
A papyrus forty metres long lists Ramesses III's gifts to the temples.
Villagers in the Valley of Mexico bury their dead with clay figures.
The Elamites sack Babylon and carry off the Code of Hammurabi and the statue of Marduk.
Tomb robbers in the Valley of the Kings are tried and confess.
Greeks from the ruined palaces move to Cyprus and the islands.
The last Shang kings cast great bronze cauldrons for the ancestors.
Urnfield ways spread through Italy.
Vedic priests gather spells and charms for healing and harm.
Chakravanti and Akashic scholars both claim the Atharvaveda's healers as forerunners.
Noddists say Elam's raids on Babylon were a war between two Antediluvian broods.
Grain in Egypt costs eight times what it did under Ramesses II.
Iranian-speaking tribes settle the Zagros and the plateau.
Refugees bury their dead in chamber tombs on the Attic coast.
Cretans move to steep hilltops such as Karphi.
Elam's greatest builder raises temples across Susa.
Ramesses IX orders the inquiry into the tomb robberies.
Assyria holds its heartland against the Arameans.
Babylon's poem of creation makes Marduk king of the gods.
Farmers carve ships, ploughs and warriors on the rocks of western Sweden.
Nebuchadnezzar I of Babylon beats Elam and brings Marduk's statue home.
Noddists say the statue of Marduk carried a Cainite's blood-bound priests with it.
A great cairn in Sweden has stones carved with chariots and lurs.
The last Shang kings ask their ancestors about hunts, war and rain.
Enkomi on Cyprus is rebuilt by newcomers from the Aegean.
The Zhou build their capital at Feng on the Wei river.
Later Zhou writers paint the last Shang king as a drunkard and a tyrant.
Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns to the Mediterranean and hunts in Lebanon.
Priests build fire altars of brick to set measures.
Assyrian law tablets set harsh rules for marriage and debt.
Libyan raiders and tomb robbers trouble Thebes.
Oasis farmers of Turkmenistan build citadels with canals.
Greece loses its palaces and writing; people live in small villages for three centuries.
Tyre, Sidon and Byblos rise as sea-trading cities.
Iron tools and weapons spread through the Levant and Anatolia.
An old wound to the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns to the Mediterranean and hunts lions and wild bulls.
The Zhou begin the divination system later written down as the Yijing.

items.t: Cold iron and the first Sundering
items.x: Deduced: cold iron is the fae's bane and the Sundering parts dream from flesh (C20 pdf 34-36), so the Sundering is taken to begin as iron spreads, about 1100 BCE in the Levant.
Aramean tribes spread over Syria and the Euphrates.
The high priests of Amun rule Upper Egypt in all but name.
Phoenician tradition dates the founding of Gadir, later Cadiz, to about now.
Fortified hilltops rise across Moravia as the Bronze Age world breaks apart.
Smiths of the Ganges plain make iron tools.
The Olmec of San Lorenzo carve colossal stone heads of their rulers.
Kithain mourn the age when iron left the forges of kings and came into every farmhouse.
Some Hermetic chronicles say Phoenician pilots kept sea charts no other people knew.
A king of Byblos is buried in a coffin carved with Phoenician letters.
Greek tradition says the Dorians came down from the north.
The first temple at Chavin is built with its stone galleries.
Rock art in the Sahara shows horses pulling chariots.
Wraiths say the dead of the burned palaces made a court of their own in the Greek Shadowlands.
Potters of the Zhou fire glazed stoneware.
Kush keeps working the gold mines Egypt once held.
The priests of Thebes rebury the royal mummies in hidden caches.
The Reborn say the reburial of the kings was done to keep their bodies from the Setites.
The Assyrian king plants trees he brought back from his wars.
The nuraghe towers of Sardinia grow into fortified villages.
The priest Wenamun sails to Byblos for cedar and is robbed and mocked.
The Zhou give out land to their kin as fiefs.
Byblos sells cedar of Lebanon to Egypt and Assyria.
Bronze Age sailors cross the Channel in sewn plank boats.
Egypt splits between the priest-kings of Thebes and kings in the Delta.
Smendes rules Lower Egypt from Tanis.
Aramean raids and drought shrink Babylonia.
Zhou nobles cast bronzes recording the king's gifts to them.
In the Hebrew telling the Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant at Aphek.
Athens is one of the few Mycenaean towns lived in through the dark age.
Greek wraith lore says the custom of the coin for the ferryman began in these years.
Olmec paintings are made deep in the caves of Juxtlahuaca.
The Philistine cities of the coast fight Israel's tribes.
Drought and Aramean raids shrink Assyria to its old heartland.
The Duke of Zhou rules for the young king and sets the rites of the dynasty.
Athenian potters paint concentric circles with a compass.
The tribes of Israel keep a shrine at Shiloh.
Egypt loses its hold on Nubia.
Olmec carvers work blue-green jade into masks and celts.
Stargazer tales say the Zhou rites kept the spirits of rivers and mountains bound to the kings.
King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king at Muye; the Zhou claim the Mandate of Heaven.
The Kuei-jin date their weakness to sunlight from the Chou, and tell that the Japanese spirit Mikaboshi advised the new dynasty (KotE pdf 12).
Small villages without pig bones spread in the highlands of Canaan.
The Zhou build an eastern capital at Luoyi.
Bronze horns called lurs are blown in pairs in Denmark.
Athenians burn their dead and bury the ash in amphorae.
Saul is made the first king of Israel.
The Philistines keep the smiths of the land to themselves.
Vedic hymns praise kings of the Bharata.
Zhou scribes record royal speeches later gathered in the Book of Documents.
A line from the southern marshes rules Babylon.

items.t: The rising of the Three Guards
items.x: Shang princes and Zhou uncles rise against the Duke of Zhou and are crushed.
Kuei-jin tellings say the Zhou rites set the order of the Middle Kingdom's courts of the dead.
Glass and amber workers trade at Frattesina on the Po.
A Korean village builds a timber palisade around its houses.
Greeks settle Smyrna on the coast of Asia Minor.
Saul and his sons die fighting the Philistines.
The high priests of Amun run Thebes as a state of the god.
Tyre and Sidon sell cloth dyed with purple from sea snails.
David makes Jerusalem the capital of Israel.
The Phoenicians write with an alphabet of 22 letters, the ancestor of Greek and Latin writing.
The Vedic hymns are gathered and the kingdoms of the Ganges plain grow.
The first fire-priests of the Iranian plateau tend their altars, later honoured as a root of the Celestial Chorus and the Ahl-i-Batin.
Hillforts multiply in central Europe as chiefs compete.
Kithain legend sets the great war of the Tuatha against the Fomorians in this age, long before the Sundering.
The Encyclopaedia's tale of a breed ordained by both sun and moon.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Large urnfield cemeteries spread across southern Moravia below the Palava hills.
Camels carry frankincense and myrrh from south Arabia north to the Levant.
Many scholars place the prophet Zarathustra between 1500 and 1000 BCE on the steppe.
The Encyclopaedia's account of Zarathustra and the first Adversary belongs here.
A chieftain and a woman are buried in a great hall at Lefkandi on Euboea.
Farmers in Korea grow rice in paddies and build stone tombs.
Farmers of the Ethiopian highlands build towns that will trade with Saba.
Maya farmers settle Cuello in Belize.
Lapita sailors reach Fiji.
Islanders on Gotland lay out stone ships around their dead.
Herders of the steppe ride horses to war and to herd.
Smiths in Ireland make gold torcs and dress-fasteners.
Garou of the steppe ride with the horse peoples.
Wraiths of the Levant say the Hebrews called the Shadowlands Sheol and feared it.
In the reckoning of the Fallen, Solomon bound Earthbound and lesser Fallen with his ring.
Rice farming reaches the island of Kyushu from Korea.
Smiths at Ban Chiang cast bronze.
Farmers settle the Jos plateau, where the Nok will rise.
The kingdom of Tartessos grows rich on silver in the south of Spain.
Urnfield farmers of Bohemia and Moravia bury their ashes with painted pots.

items.t: The first Wan Kuei of the islands
items.x: Kuei-jin tales say the first hungry dead of Japan rose among the rice-farmers from Korea.
The Reborn say Amun's priests carried the old rites to Napata when Thebes weakened.
The camel is tamed in Arabia.
Stone slabs carved with warriors, shields and chariots stand in south-west Spain.
David takes the Jebusite town of Jerusalem for his capital.
Psusennes I is buried at Tanis in a silver coffin.
Kithain tradition places the coming of the Milesians in Ireland and the retreat of the Tuatha in this age.
The god Amun gives verdicts by oracle at Thebes.

items.t: The Vedic towns of the Doab
items.x: Settlements spread along the land between the Ganges and Yamuna.
Hiram I makes Tyre the greatest Phoenician city.
Euboean traders sail again to Cyprus and the Levant.
Ashur-dan II drives the Arameans back from the Tigris.
Royal women serve as the God's Wife of Amun at Thebes.
Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem.
Tyre and Israel send ships from the Red Sea to Ophir for gold.
Long inscriptions on Zhou bronzes record land, lawsuits and gifts.
Solomon succeeds David as king in Jerusalem.
Smiths of central Europe make tall gold hats marked with the calendar.
Fallen and Earthbound alike tell stories of the king who bound spirits with a ring and a name.
Legend says Zhou King Mu drove his chariot to the Queen Mother of the West.

items.t: The Queen Mother of the West
items.x: Kuei-jin say Xiwangmu's court in the Kunlun was a real court of the dead.
Thieves strip the royal tombs of the delta.
Hebrew tradition tells of a queen of Saba who came to Solomon with spices and gold.
Zhou courts keep records of land grants on bamboo.
Shoshenq I, of Libyan descent, takes Egypt's throne and raids Judah.
The kingdom of Saba grows rich on incense in south Arabia.
Horus, with allies from the west, drives Set out of Egypt (Mummy 1st pdf 65).
Israel builds gates and fortresses at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer.
Farmers of the Lusatian culture build timber forts in the north.
The Kuru town of Hastinapura grows on the Ganges.
Kithain say the bronze horns of Denmark were blown to call the fae to the feasts.
A Libyan chief takes the throne of Egypt as Shoshenq I.
Drought in northern Mesopotamia weakens Assyria and Babylon alike.
The last king of the Tanite line hands Egypt to Libyan chiefs.
The Zhou punishments code is set down under King Mu.
The great hall of Lefkandi is covered by a mound over its two burials.
Pilgrims bring shells from Ecuador and obsidian from the south to Chavin.
After Solomon the kingdom splits into Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
The northern tribes break from Judah under Jeroboam.
Solomon's son refuses to lighten the tribes' burden.
Noddists say a Cainite feud behind the throne split Israel from Judah.
Pharaoh Shoshenq raids Judah and Israel and carries off treasure.
A fortified timber village is built on an island in a Polish lake.
Zhou King Zhao is lost with his army crossing the Han river.
The first cemeteries of Tarquinia fill with hut urns.
The amber road runs from the Baltic through Moravia to the south.
Rice farmers of the Red river delta work bronze.
Adad-nirari II begins Assyria's return to power.
Northern horsemen raid the Zhou lands.
The Etruscan hills sell iron and copper to Sardinia and the Phoenicians.
Assyria fights the Aramean states each summer.
Osorkon I gives great gifts of silver to the temples.
Akashic and Euthanatos masters begin a war in the mountains that runs, by one count, to 300 BCE (M20 pdf 123; Sorcerers Crusade pdf 68).
Kushite kings at Napata on the upper Nile build their own kingdom.
The temple centre of Chavin draws pilgrims in the high Andes.
Iron-using villages of central Italy grow into the Etruscan cities.
An old lair at Krapina tied to the spider queen, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Greek potters paint vases with bands of zigzags and meanders.
An Urnfield hillfort stands on Hostyn hill, a height later held sacred.
The Garou of Moravia keep a caern on the wooded height of Hostyn, and the hillfort's builders leave offerings there.
Assyrian armies bring battering rams and siege towers to the walls of their enemies.
Olmec power moves to La Venta, with its clay pyramid and offerings of buried jade.
Smiths around Lake Victoria smelt iron, and Bantu-speaking farmers carry it south and west.
Herders build huts on the hills by the Tiber.
Offerings of bronze figurines pile up at Olympia.
The Kuru become the first great kingdom of the Vedic peoples.
Gordion grows as the seat of the Phrygians.
A new kingdom grows at Napata by the sacred mountain of Jebel Barkal.
San Lorenzo is abandoned and its heads buried.
Woodland peoples of the Ohio valley build burial mounds.
Ventrue tales say a Cainite watched the huts of the Palatine long before Rome had a name.
lk: Rome and Italy in the High Clan Wars

items.x: Sabaeans and highlanders begin building at Yeha.
The stone god of Chavin stands in the dark heart of the temple.
Farmers in Korea raise thousands of stone dolmens.
Lapita villages spread across the Solomons and Vanuatu.
Balam tales say the jaguar-men carved on Chavin's walls were their own kin.
A ship's load of bronze weapons is lost in the harbour of Huelva.
Offerings begin at the spring of Delphi.
Assyria marches down the Euphrates collecting tribute.
Athenian potters paint bands, meanders and horses.
Assyria fields the first standing army of the Iron Age.
Herders of Mongolia raise stones carved with flying deer.
Ashurnasirpal II makes Assyria the terror of the Near East and builds a palace at Nimrud.
The kingdom of Urartu rises around Lake Van.
Ashurnasirpal II rebuilds Kalhu, later Nimrud, as his capital.
Osorkon II sends troops against Assyria.
Wraiths say Ashurnasirpal's victims formed a legion of rage in the Assyrian Shadowlands.
Highland farmers grow teff and plough with oxen.
Ashurnasirpal feeds nearly seventy thousand guests for ten days to open his capital.
Omri of Israel builds a new capital at Samaria.
Villages in Latium bury their dead with tiny model huts.
The Adena build round houses and trade copper.
Ashurnasirpal flays and impales rebels and boasts of it on his walls.
Ahab of Israel marries Jezebel of Tyre.
Noddists claim Jezebel's Baal priests served the Baali of Tyre.
The Zhou cast bronze bells tuned to two notes each.
Nomads use the short recurved bow from horseback.
A town below a cliff carved with rain gods rises in Morelos.
Damascus leads the Aramean states.
Greeks take the Phoenician letters and add vowels.
The kingdom of Urartu takes shape around Lake Van.
The Zhou kings lose their grip as their lords grow strong.
Villanovan Etruscans bury their ashes in urns shaped like huts.
Corax tales say the ravens that fed Elijah were their kin.
Villages in Greece begin to join into towns with their own shrines.
Kings of Napata are buried under mounds at el-Kurru.
Jomon villages shrink as the climate cools.
Shalmaneser III fights every year for thirty-five years.
The prophet Elijah challenges Baal's priests on Mount Carmel.
The Zhou change their bronze ritual sets toward rank.
Shalmaneser III fights a league of kings including Ahab of Israel at Qarqar.
Miners dig salt deep into the mountain at Hallstatt in the Alps, giving the Iron Age culture its name.
The first iron tools reach Moravia; the Hallstatt age begins there.
The Aramean kingdom of Damascus fights both Israel and Assyria.

items.t: Iron comes to the fae of Moravia
items.x: Deduced from the card above: iron reaches Moravia about 850 BCE, and the trods of the Moravian hills begin to close.
Lapita sailors reach Tonga and Samoa, the far edge of the Pacific for a thousand years.
Smiths of the Hallstatt world forge long iron swords.
The Hallstatt world reaches Moravia with iron and painted pots.
Priests write prose guides to the Vedic sacrifice.
Mesha of Moab throws off Israel's rule.
Horse nomads called Cimmerians roam north of the Black Sea.
La Venta raises a great clay pyramid.
Libyan chiefs rule many towns of the delta.
Garou of the Alps read the Hallstatt salt mine as a wound the Weaver made.
Wraith lore says the kings of Kush kept Egyptian ways of binding the dead to their tombs.
Hazael takes the throne of Aram and wars on Israel.
Israel and Judah fight Damascus at Ramoth-Gilead.
Herders of Mauritania build stone villages on the cliffs.
Nobles drive out King Li of Zhou; from 841 Chinese history has a year-by-year record.
Jehu kills Joram and Jezebel and pays tribute to Assyria.
Shalmaneser's obelisk shows Jehu bowing before him.
Shalmaneser III marches against Urartu.
Great pots mark Athenian graves with funerals painted on them.
Sarduri I fortifies the citadel of Van.
Assyrian armies take the Cilician plain.
A timber causeway and offering place stands in the fens.
King Mesha of Moab sets up a stone telling of his war with Israel.
The people of the Zhou capital rise and drive out King Li.
The Panchala join the Kuru as a great kingdom of the Ganges.
Hilltop forts spread across eastern France.
King Xuan restores the Zhou for a time.
Shalmaneser's son rebels and Assyria is torn for four years.
Herders of the Fezzan begin to build oasis towns.
Veii becomes one of the great Etruscan towns.
Caravans of camels carry incense up the Arabian coast.
Elissa of Tyre flees a brother king and sails west, in the tale that ends with Carthage.
Shamshi-Adad V puts down the revolt and fights Babylon.
Greek and Roman writers later tell how Elissa bought as much land as an oxhide could cover.
A temple with gold crowns rises in the northern Andes.
The towns of Euboea grow rich on sea trade.
Zhou King Xuan fights the western Rong.
Vedic priests write a long guide to the fire rite.
Phoenicians from Tyre found Carthage, in legend led by the princess Elissa, called Dido.

items.t: A new city by the sea
items.x: The Brujah tell that their elders came to Carthage soon after its founding and saw in it the chance of a city where Cainite and mortal could live side by side.
Queen Sammu-ramat, later the legendary Semiramis, rules Assyria for her young son.
Adad-nirari III takes the throne with his mother beside him.
Settlers begin a hill town above the upper Danube.
Kashi, later Varanasi, grows on the Ganges.
Adad-nirari III forces Damascus to pay tribute.
Horse lords in Tuva bury a king with 160 horses under a great timber mound.
King Zakkur of Hamath records how his god saved him from a siege.
Alara unites Kush around Napata.
Egypt is split among rival kings in Thebes and the delta.
Greek towns send out their first colonies by sea.
Teachers of the Ganges ask what the self is, and whether it is the world.
Kashta of Kush takes Upper Egypt's southern towns.
The Paracas people of the south coast weave fine cloth and bind skulls.
Smiths in China begin to cast iron.
Hermetic and Verbena scholars both trace their oldest Greek rites to the oracles of this age.
Samos builds one of the first great temples of Greece, to Hera.
A great earthquake strikes the Zhou heartland.
By Greek reckoning the first games are held at Olympia in honour of Zeus.
Greeks found a trading post on the island of Ischia.
Nomads and rebels sack the western Zhou capital; the Zhou move east.
The Zhou kings rule in name only as lords fight for power.
Kuei-jin say the fall of western Zhou split the courts of the dead along the lords' borders.
Assyrian scribes record a solar eclipse that fixes the dates of the age.
Plague and revolt shake Assyria.
By Roman tradition Romulus founds Rome on the Palatine on 21 April.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: The Iliad and the Odyssey take shape in the Greek world about now.
Greek traders found Pithekoussai on Ischia, the first Greek settlement in the west.
The first prophets whose words are written down preach in Israel.
Hesiod writes of the gods' births and the farmer's year.
Ventrue legend says the founders of Rome were watched by a Cainite and a Lupine at once.
lk: Rome and Italy in the High Clan Wars

items.x: Assyria moves whole peoples across its empire to break revolts.
Assyria becomes a standing empire that moves whole peoples to break revolts.
Urartu reaches its greatest size.
Corinthians found Syracuse on Sicily.
Midas rules Phrygia from Gordion, remembered for his gold.
Piye of Kush conquers Egypt; his line rules it as the twenty-fifth dynasty.
Assyria takes Samaria and carries off the northern tribes of Israel.
Chalcis and Eretria fight over the plain between them.
Shabaka of Kush rules Egypt and restores its temples.
Sargon II of Assyria loots the holy city of Urartu.
Spartans found Taras in southern Italy.
Sargon II falls in battle and his body is never found.
Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem; Hezekiah pays tribute and the city stands.
Chiefs of the Hallstatt culture are buried in wagon graves with gold and Greek bronzes.
The Get of Fenris tell of their kin tribes moving south into Europe about now (Tribebook Fenris pdf 21).
Maya at Nakbe and El Mirador raise stone platforms in the Peten forest.
Sixteen great states rise across north India.
A great ring of timber rises at Emain Macha.
Sennacherib brings water to Nineveh by canal and aqueduct.
Adena mounds rise over log tombs in the Ohio valley.
Scythian horsemen drive the Cimmerians south.
Garou of the steppe ride with the Scythians and take their gold as offerings.
Taharqa of Kush builds across Egypt and Nubia.
Sennacherib floods and razes Babylon.
The Messenians rise against Sparta.
Gyges takes the throne of Lydia.
The Etruscan towns grow rich and build great tombs.
Esarhaddon takes Memphis and drives the Kushite pharaoh south.
Duke Huan of Qi becomes the first hegemon of the lords.
Ashurbanipal gathers tens of thousands of tablets at Nineveh, the Gilgamesh epic among them.
Psamtik I drives out the Assyrians and unites Egypt.
Ashurbanipal's army sacks Thebes.
Japanese tradition dates the first emperor, Jimmu, to 660 BCE.
Kindred of the East keeps the traditional date for the first imperial court (KotE pdf 145).
Megarians found Byzantion on the Bosporus.
The kings of Lydia strike coins of electrum, the first true coinage.
Greek armies fight in close ranks of armoured spearmen.
The crossbow comes into use in China.
La Venta's power fades.
The Reborn say the Saite kings brought back the old rites of the pyramid age.
Ashurbanipal destroys Susa and salts the land.
Greeks from Thera found Cyrene on the Libyan coast.
King Josiah of Judah closes the shrines and keeps one temple.
Sappho writes love poems on Lesbos.
Nabopolassar frees Babylon from Assyria.
Draco writes down the laws of Athens, harsh enough to give their name to harshness.
Greeks of Thera spread across the green coast of Libya.
Tarquin the Elder becomes king of Rome.
Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh; Assyria is finished within a few years.
Necho II begins a canal from the Nile to the Red Sea.
Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish.
Greeks from Phocaea found Massalia, later Marseille.

items.t: Carthage, capital of the Phoenician world
items.x: By now Carthage leads the Phoenician cities of the west, and its Brujah court is the pride of the clan (Clanbook Brujah pdf 18).
Kuei-jin of the Azure Dragon follow Korean migrants to Japan (KotE pdf 145).
Herodotus says Phoenician sailors sent by Necho sailed round Africa in three years.
Thales of Miletus asks what the world is made of.
Mahavira teaches the Jain way of harmlessness.
The Zapotecs carve the first writing of the Americas.
A Celtic chief at the Heuneburg builds a Greek-style wall of mud brick.
Kithain bards set the Fenian stories in this age.
Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem and carries its king to Babylon.
Solon cancels debts and ends debt slavery in Athens.
Babylon builds the blue Ishtar Gate and the processional way.
Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and the first temple; the people of Judah go into exile in Babylon.
The people of Judah settle beside the canals of Babylon and keep their faith without a temple.
An eclipse halts a battle between Lydia and the Medes; Thales of Miletus is said to have predicted it.
Later Greeks tell of terraced gardens in Babylon.
Amasis takes Egypt's throne and favours the Greeks.
Peisistratos rules Athens as tyrant.
Tradition places the birth of Siddhartha Gautama about now, though many date it later.
Croesus of Lydia becomes a byword for wealth.

items.t: The first gold and silver coins
items.x: Croesus strikes coins of pure gold and pure silver.
Kong Qiu, later called Confucius, is born in the state of Lu.
Cyrus of Persia overthrows the Medes and founds the Persian empire.
In a cave of the Moravian Karst a Hallstatt chief is buried with a wagon, bronzes and dozens of others, some of them killed for the rite.

items.t: The dead of the bull cave
items.x: The cave of Byci skala holds a crowd of Hallstatt wraiths bound to their lord and to the bronzes left with them.
Tradition places Laozi, keeper of the Zhou archives, in this age.
The rites of Demeter at Eleusis draw initiates from all Greece.
Mago builds Carthage's army and fleet.
Verbena and Hermetic tales both claim the Eleusinian rite as one of theirs.
Cyrus beats Croesus and takes Lydia.
Carthage and the Etruscans drive the Greeks from Corsica.
Babylon opens its gates to Cyrus; the exiles of Judah may go home.
Siddhartha leaves his palace to seek an end to suffering.
Hermetic history says Pythagoras brought the lore of Thoth to the Greeks (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20-21).
Cyrus dies fighting the Massagetae of the steppe.
Siddhartha becomes the Buddha under a tree at Bodh Gaya.
Cambyses defeats Egypt at Pelusium.
The Reborn see Egypt pass to foreign kings for the first of many times.
Pythagoras founds his brotherhood in southern Italy.
Darius I takes the Persian throne and orders the empire into satrapies with a royal road.
Darius begins the palace city of Persepolis.
Darius builds a road from Sardis to Susa with posts and riders.
The returned exiles finish a new temple in Jerusalem.
Darius takes Gandhara and the Indus valley.
Athens drives out Peisistratos' sons.
Rome drives out its last king and becomes a republic under two consuls.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Wraith histories say the dead of Rome set up a republic of their own, the pattern for Stygia (Wraith: Renegades pdf 26-28).
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Cleisthenes reforms Athens into a democracy of citizens.
The Ahl-i-Batin date their beginning to the Night of Fana (Sorcerers Crusade pdf 69).
The Nok people of the Jos plateau work iron and model life-sized heads in fired clay.
The Zapotecs level a mountaintop above the Oaxaca valley and build a capital on it.
Tradition places Sun Tzu's Art of War in this age.
Maya villages grow into towns across the lowlands.
Kush moves its centre south to Meroe.
Iberian towns in Spain write in their own scripts.
Iron tools reach Korea from China.
Kuei-jin tales say each school of thought had its own court of the dead listening.
Wraith lore says Greek ideas of Hades shaped the first Stygian necropoli of the west.
The Greek cities of Ionia revolt against Persia.
Mages fight the Dragon River War from 496 to 480 BCE (Sorcerers Crusade pdf 69).
lk: The Warring States and the Silk Road

items.x: The common people of Rome leave the city until they get their own tribunes.
Athenians beat the Persian landing at Marathon.
A later tale says a runner carried word of Marathon to Athens and died.
Monks recite the Buddha's sayings after his death.
The state of Wu digs a canal from the Yangtze.
Leonidas and his Spartans hold the pass at Thermopylae before they are overwhelmed.
The Greek fleet destroys the Persian fleet in the strait of Salamis.
The Greeks of Sicily defeat a Carthaginian army at Himera.
Syracuse beats Carthage at Himera on the same day as Salamis.
The Greeks end the Persian invasion at Plataea.
Confucius dies in Lu, his work unfinished.
Athens leads a league of island cities against Persia.
Chinese states begin two and a half centuries of war.
Socrates is born in Athens.
Xerxes is killed in his palace.
Hippocrates of Kos teaches medicine without the gods.
The great houses of Jin and Qi break apart into rival kingdoms.
Rome's laws are written on twelve bronze tablets in the Forum.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: The La Tene style of Celtic art spreads from the upper Rhine and Danube.
Herodotus writes the first history of the Greeks and Persians.
Hanno of Carthage sails down the west coast of Africa.
The Paracas wrap their dead in great embroidered cloths.
Brujah tradition says their elders debated beside the philosophers.
Athens begins the Parthenon under Pericles.
Sophocles stages Antigone in Athens.
Athens and Sparta begin a war that lasts until 404.
Plague kills perhaps a third of Athens, Pericles with them.
The Brujah, lovers of the Greek city, watch the plague and the war break Athens.
Monks carry the Buddha's teaching along the Ganges.
Aristophanes mocks Athens' leaders on stage.
Athens sends a great fleet against Syracuse and loses it.
Persia pays Sparta to fight Athens.
The kingdoms of China arm their peasant armies with iron.
Athens yields to Sparta.
Greek mercenaries march home from Babylon to the Black Sea.
For three centuries rival cults of Hermes murder and riot against each other in Greece and Egypt (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 22).
A round temple town rises in the Valley of Mexico.
Celtic tribes settle the Po valley.
The Nok smelt iron on the Jos plateau.
Rice farmers from Korea spread through Japan with bronze and iron.
Athens condemns Socrates, who drinks hemlock.
Athens, Thebes, Corinth and Argos fight Sparta.
Gauls under Brennus defeat Rome at the Allia and sack the city.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: The Fianna sing that their Kinfolk rode with the Gauls who sacked Rome.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Plato opens his school at the Academy.
Persia dictates terms to the Greek cities.
Mozi preaches universal love and defensive war.
Plato writes of a city ruled by philosophers.
Thebes breaks Spartan power at Leuctra.
Plebeians win the right to hold the consulship.
Shang Yang remakes Qin with harsh laws and rewards for soldiers.
Philip II takes the throne of Macedon and builds a new army.
Artemisia builds a great tomb for her husband Mausolus.
Nectanebo II is the last Egyptian-born king of Egypt.
The Reborn say the last native pharaoh was a sorcerer who fled south.
Aristotle becomes tutor to the young prince of Macedon.
Rome defeats its Latin allies.
Philip beats Athens and Thebes; Greece falls under Macedon.
Philip is murdered and Alexander takes the throne at twenty.
Aristotle opens his school in Athens.
Alexander crosses into Asia and defeats the Persian satraps.
Alexander routs Darius III at Issus.
Alexander builds a mole to the island city of Tyre and takes it after seven months.
Alexander takes Egypt and founds Alexandria.
The Reborn's own histories mark Alexander's taking of Egypt and the founding of Alexandria (Mummy 2nd pdf 24).
Alexander destroys the Persian army at Gaugamela.
Alexander's army burns the palace at Persepolis.
Alexander beats King Porus at the Hydaspes; his army refuses to go further.
Pytheas of Massalia sails round Britain and hears of Thule.
Alexander dies at Babylon at thirty-two; his generals divide the empire.
Aristotle and Demosthenes die within a year of each other.
Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire across north India.
The Samnites trap a Roman army and send it under the yoke.
Rome builds its first great road, to Capua.
Seleucus takes Babylon and founds a dynasty that rules Asia.
Ptolemy I takes the title of king of Egypt.
The Reborn hold that Set corrupts the Ptolemaic kings and that Horus passes into the Underworld (Mummy 2nd pdf 24, 27).
Seleucus gives up the Indus for five hundred elephants.
The Ptolemies found the Museum and the Library of Alexandria.
Hermetic tradition counts the scholars of Alexandria among its founders in spirit.
Euclid writes the Elements of geometry at Alexandria.
The Himalayan War, begun about 900 BCE, runs to about 300 BCE by one count (Sorcerers Crusade pdf 68).
El Mirador raises La Danta, one of the largest pyramids ever built.
Kautilya's manual of statecraft is written for the Mauryas.
El Mirador grows into the greatest Maya city.
The kingdom of Gojoseon rules northern Korea.
Zeno teaches in the painted porch at Athens.
The lighthouse of Alexandria is built.
Pyrrhus of Epirus beats Rome at great cost.
Celtic raiders attack Delphi and are driven off.
Aristarchus of Samos says the earth goes round the sun.
Rome and Carthage go to war over Sicily.
Clanbook Ventrue says the clan stirred the First Punic War by way of Syracuse (pdf 19-20).
Rome's new fleet wins its first sea battle with boarding bridges.
After the slaughter at Kalinga the Maurya emperor Ashoka turns to Buddhism.
The Parni horsemen found the Parthian kingdom.
Jewish scholars in Alexandria translate their scriptures into Greek.
The Brujah of Carthage and the Ventrue of Rome start their long war.
Rome wins at the Aegates Islands and takes Sicily.
Eratosthenes measures the size of the earth.
Archimedes works out the lever and the screw in Syracuse.
Rome beats the Gauls at Telamon.
Qin Shi Huang unites China and calls himself the First Emperor.

items.t: Fu Xia and the First Emperor
items.x: The Encyclopaedia places Fu Xia at the First Emperor's court.
Hannibal leads an army with elephants over the Alps into Italy.
Hannibal surrounds and destroys a Roman army at Cannae.
The First Emperor links the northern walls into one line.
Rome takes Syracuse and Archimedes is killed.
Qin Shi Huang is buried with thousands of clay soldiers.
Kindred of the East tells that Qin Shi Huang became a Lord of the Dead (KotE pdf 142-145; Dark Kingdom of Jade pdf 34-35).
Qin Shi Huang dies seeking an elixir of life.
Modu Chanyu unites the Xiongnu of the steppe.
The Han dynasty takes power fifteen years after the Qin unification.
Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama; Carthage sues for peace.
The Xiongnu surround the first Han emperor.
Hopewell peoples build earthworks and trade from the Rockies to the Gulf.
The great stupa of Sanchi is built.
Garou of the steppe ride with the Xiongnu into China.
The Roman legion beats the Macedonian phalanx.
Priests at Memphis write a decree in hieroglyphs, demotic and Greek.
Rome beats the Seleucids at Magnesia.
Greek kings rule in Bactria and the Punjab.
Plautus and Terence fill Rome's stages.
Rome ends the kingdom of Macedon.
The Maccabees revolt against the Seleucid king.
The Maccabees rededicate the temple in Jerusalem.
Rome declares war on Carthage fifty years after the last; Clanbook Ventrue puts the clan behind it (pdf 19-20).
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Viriathus leads the Lusitanians against Rome.
Rome takes Carthage after a three-year siege, sells its people and razes the city.
Ventrue treachery ends Brujah Carthage; Malkavians help ruin it, and the Brujah never forgive Rome (V20 pdf 58; V20 Dark Ages pdf 54).
Clanbook Baali says the Brujah of Carthage dealt with the Baali, the charge Rome used against them (pdf 23-24).
Rome sacks Corinth the same year.
Han Emperor Wu takes the throne and wars on the Xiongnu.
Zhang Qian sets out to find allies against the Xiongnu.
The tribune Tiberius Gracchus is killed by senators for his land law.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Rome starves Numantia into surrender.
Han envoys reach Central Asia; silk begins to travel west.
The Parthians drive the Seleucids from Babylonia.
Gaius Gracchus and his followers are killed in Rome.
Germanic peoples beat a Roman army at Noreia.
Rome fights Jugurtha of Numidia.
The Celtic Boii hold a great walled town at Stare Hradisko in Moravia, with mints and workshops.
The Fianna count Kinfolk among the Boii of Moravia, and their caerns lie in the hills above the oppida.
The Han conquer northern Korea.
The Cimbri destroy two Roman armies at Arausio.
The Han reform the calendar.
The Boii strike gold and silver coins, the first money made in the Czech lands.
About a century before Christ, twenty mystics meet to end the feuds of the Hermes cults (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 22).
The Nazca begin scraping giant lines and figures into the desert of southern Peru.
Sima Qian writes the Records of the Grand Historian.
Farmers gather in the valley of Teotihuacan.
A kingdom grows at Aksum in the highlands.
Celtic glassmakers in Moravia make blue bracelets.
Rome's Italian allies fight for citizenship.
Mithridates of Pontus has thousands of Romans in Asia killed in a day.
Sulla takes Rome and rules as dictator.
Gladiators break out at Capua; Spartacus leads a slave army for two years.

Muhammad leaves Mecca for Medina; the Muslim calendar begins.
The Frankish merchant Samo leads the Slavs in revolt against the Avars and becomes their king.
Muhammad's followers beat the Meccans at Badr.

Li Shimin takes the Tang throne as Taizong.
Heraclius beats the Persians near Nineveh.
The Meccans fail to take Medina.
The monk Xuanzang leaves Chang'an for India to fetch the Buddhist texts.
Muhammad enters Mecca and clears the Kaaba of idols.
Songtsen Gampo builds the Tibetan empire.
Samo's Slavs defeat the Frankish king Dagobert at Wogastisburg.
Muhammad dies; Abu Bakr becomes the first caliph.
The caliph Abu Bakr brings the Arab tribes back under Medina.
Umar becomes caliph.
The Arab armies beat the eastern Romans at Yarmouk and take Syria.
The Arabs beat the Persians at Qadisiyyah.
The caliph Umar takes Jerusalem.
Christian monks from Persia build a church in Chang'an.
Arab armies conquer Egypt by 642.

The Arabs take Alexandria.
The last Persian army is beaten.
Uthman becomes caliph and orders one text of the Quran.
The Japanese court takes the land into the throne's hands on the Chinese model.

items.t: The Courts of Love take note
items.x: Philip II of France grows stronger against the English kings; the Toreador of the Grand Court watch the balance shift toward Paris.
The first Kamakura shogun dies after a fall from a horse; the Hojo family begin to rule for his heirs.
Philip II grants the scholars of Paris rights against the city's officers, the start of the university's privileges.
Hermetic masters take rooms among the Paris scholars, and the craftsmen who will become the Order of Reason do the same.
By Inca tradition Manco Capac founds Cuzco in a high Andean valley about this year.
The great mound city on the Mississippi starts to lose its people, and its palisade is rebuilt for the last time.
By the palace tradition Eweka becomes the first Oba of Benin about this year.
The Tu'i Tonga rule islands as far as Samoa and Fiji and raise the great stone trilithon on Tongatapu.
The Saudeleur lords of Pohnpei build a city of basalt logs on nearly a hundred artificial islets.

items.t: Venice agrees to carry the crusade
items.x: The Treaty of Venice binds the Fourth Crusade to pay for a fleet it cannot afford.
Leonardo of Pisa publishes the Liber Abaci, bringing Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.

items.t: The first crusader assault on Constantinople
items.x: Crusaders storm the city's sea walls and restore Isaac II and Alexios IV; the bargain cannot be paid.
A fire set during fighting burns a broad swath of Constantinople; tens of thousands lose their homes.
Hojo Tokimasa becomes regent to the shogun, and the regents rule Japan in fact.
Sumanguru Kante of the Sosso takes Koumbi Saleh, the old capital of Ghana.
Alexios Doukas Mourtzouphlos strangles Alexios IV and defies the crusaders.
The crusaders break in and loot for three days; Cainites of every clan flee or burn with their havens, and the Dream ends.
Relics, books and treasures from the sack flood into Venice, Paris and the Rhineland; mages hunt for the true ones among the fakes.
Theodore Laskaris gathers Byzantine refugees at Nicaea and founds a successor state.
The Komnenos brothers found an empire on the Black Sea coast with Georgian help.
Philip II takes Rouen and Normandy from King John.
The Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan destroys the Latin army and captures Emperor Baldwin I, who dies in prison.
Henry of Flanders becomes Latin emperor and rules the conquered lands with skill.
Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a slave general, founds the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi.

items.t: The khan's oath under the Eternal Blue Sky
items.x: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan; the courts of the Middle Kingdom take the omens of the steppe seriously.
The conqueror of northern India is murdered on the Indus; his generals divide the empire.
Innocent III names Stephen Langton Archbishop of Canterbury against King John's wishes.
The papal legate Peter of Castelnau is killed near Saint-Gilles; the pope calls a crusade against the Cathars.
The pope lays England under interdict: no masses, no church burials, for six years.
Simon de Montfort takes Carcassonne; inquirers ride with the army and learn which questions make people confess.
Pope Innocent approves the brotherhood of Francis; the Franciscans begin.
Scholars fleeing a riot at Oxford settle at Cambridge.

The Albigensian Crusade sacks Beziers on 22 July 1209. Southern France learns what a crusade at home means, and the Church learns how to hunt heresy by inquiry. Fits: Fits the heretical end times card of 1206.
items.ref: Real history (sack of Beziers, 1209).

items.x: A council at Paris forbids lecturing on Aristotle's natural philosophy; the ban is widely ignored.
Iltutmish takes the throne of Delhi and holds northern India against the Mongols.
Dunama Dibbalemi takes the throne of Kanem and sends cavalry across the central Sahara as far as the Fezzan.
Genghis Khan invades the Jin empire and wins at Badger Mouth.
King Andrew II of Hungary settles the Teutonic Order in the Burzenland to guard the passes.
Christian kings of Spain crush the Almohads; the reconquest of al-Andalus speeds up.
Bands of children and the poor march toward the sea; few come home, and some Kindred along the road grow fat.
Simon de Montfort kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret; the south loses its strongest protector.
Hungarian nobles kill Andrew II's queen for favouring her German kin.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Philip II beats Otto IV and his allies; John's hopes of retaking Normandy end, and Otto's empire collapses.
The Mongols take the Jin capital (Beijing) and burn it for a month.
The council requires yearly confession, defines transubstantiation and orders Jews and Muslims to wear distinct dress.

items.t: Rabbat in the fall of Zhongdu
items.x: Genghis Khan takes the Jin capital Zhongdu in 1215. Rabbat, already old, lives through the killing and is carried off as a Mongol captive. Fits: The book places it in the Mongol sweep through the Chin Empire in the early 13th century.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 20 (the captivity); the fall of Zhongdu, 1215, is real history; the year is a house reading.

items.x: John dies during the barons' war; the boy Henry III is crowned and William Marshal rules for him.
Pope Honorius III confirms the Order of Preachers founded by Dominic.
The great pope dies at Perugia; Kindred who shaped the Curia through him must start again.
William Marshal routs the French-backed rebels at Lincoln; Prince Louis gives up the English crown.
Crusaders gather at Acre, then turn on Egypt.
The governor of Otrar kills a Mongol trade caravan; Genghis Khan resolves on war with Khwarazm.
The crusaders take Damietta after a long siege; disease has killed most of the city.
The Mongol host enters Khwarazm; Garou of the Silk Road watch the land fill with ash and carrion spirits.
Danes conquering Estonia win at Lyndanisse; legend says the Danish flag fell from the sky.
Samarkand surrenders and is plundered; its craftsmen are carried off to Mongolia.
Pope Honorius III crowns Frederick II in Rome.
Work begins on the new cathedral at Salisbury.
A hilltop kingdom on the Limpopo trades gold and ivory to the Swahili coast and buries its rulers with gold.
Tolui's army takes Merv and kills nearly every inhabitant; chroniclers write of hundreds of thousands dead.
After a Mongol prince dies in its siege, Nishapur is razed and even its animals killed.
The crusaders, trapped by the Nile's flood, give up Damietta.
Jalal al-Din of Khwarazm escapes Genghis Khan by riding his horse into the river.
By the Maya chronicles Hunac Ceel of Mayapan overthrows the lords of Chichen Itza about this year.
King Lalibela of Ethiopia dies, leaving eleven churches cut downward into the living rock.
Andrew II grants the Hungarian nobles their rights, including the right to resist an unjust king.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Scholars leaving Bologna found a new school at Padua.
Mongol scouts under Subutai destroy the Rus princes on the Kalka; the Rus forget the warning, and the Shadow Lords do not.
Philip II of France dies after 43 years; Louis VIII takes the throne.
The pope approves the final rule of the Franciscans.
The emperor founds a school at Naples to train lawyers and officials for his kingdom.
Francis of Assisi is said to receive the wounds of Christ; the Messianic Voices count it a sign.
The Livonian crusaders take Tartu; the Get of Fenris and the Shadow Lords of the Baltic mark the last pagan groves burning.
Henry III reissues Magna Carta in its lasting form in return for a tax.
The Tran family takes the throne of Dai Viet.
Francis dies at the Portiuncula; canonised two years later.
The king dies on his way back from the Albigensian campaign; Blanche of Castile rules for the boy Louis IX.
Frederick II grants the Teutonic Order the lands it can conquer in Prussia.
Genghis Khan dies during the war on the Xi Xia, who are destroyed; the courts of the East mark the death of the scourge.
North German princes break Danish power in the Baltic.
Ugolino of Segni becomes pope and excommunicates Frederick II within months.
Excommunicated, Frederick II sails for the Holy Land anyway.
The excommunicated emperor reaches the Holy Land.
Sultan al-Kamil hands Jerusalem to Frederick II by treaty, without a battle.
The Albigensian war ends; Toulouse submits and the Inquisition arrives in the south.
A church council at Toulouse sets out how to search out heretics and bans the Bible in the common tongue.

Frederick II gets Jerusalem back by treaty in February 1229, without a battle. Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut among the city's Cainites, watches the Franks return. Fits: Same year as Camilla and Cretheus in Rome.
items.ref: Real history (Treaty of Jaffa, 1229); Gabriel Chavez from Jerusalem by Night (Dark Ages) p. 62; the year is a house reading.

items.x: Ferdinand III unites the crowns of Castile and Leon for good.
The Teutonic Knights begin their war against the pagan Prussians from Kulm.
Gregory IX sends inquisitors answerable to the pope, most of them Dominicans.
Frederick II issues a law code for the Kingdom of Sicily.
The first of many Mongol invasions of Korea begins.
Conrad of Marburg burns suspects across Germany; the shadow Inquisition in the Empire takes note of his methods.

items.t: The Korean court flees to Ganghwa
items.x: The Goryeo court moves to Ganghwa Island and holds out there for decades.

items.t: Kaifeng and the thunder crash bombs
items.x: The Jin defend Kaifeng with gunpowder bombs and fire lances; plague kills hundreds of thousands in the city.
Knights kill the inquisitor on the road; his terror ends.
The Mongols and the Song take the last Jin city; the last Jin emperor dies.
Ogedei Khan builds walls and a palace at Karakorum, the Mongol capital.
Sundiata Keita defeats Sumanguru at Kirina and founds the empire of Mali.
Ferdinand III takes Cordoba; the great mosque becomes a cathedral.
Batu and Subutai destroy Volga Bulgaria.
Razia becomes Sultan of Delhi, the only woman to rule it.
By the griots' account the clans of Mali meet and agree the laws and ranks of the new empire.
The first Rus city falls to Batu's host.
The Sword Brothers, beaten by the Lithuanians, join the Teutonic Order as its Livonian branch.
Word of the riders in the Rus lands reaches the voivodes of the Carpathians; most do not believe it.
The Mongols take Vladimir and burn the grand prince's family in the cathedral.
Grand Prince Yuri II is killed and his army destroyed.
James I of Aragon takes Valencia.
Muhammad I founds the Nasrid kingdom of Granada, the last Muslim state in Spain.
Pope and emperor go to open war in Italy.
The Mongols take Chernigov and Pereyaslavl.
Prince Alexander of Novgorod beats a Swedish force and is called Nevsky.
Batu's army storms Kiev; the mother of Rus cities is ruined, and Cainites who held it scatter.
The Rus princes submit to the Golden Horde; the Shadow Lords' quiet backing of the Mongols begins.
A Mongol column burns Krakow; legend says a trumpeter was shot mid-call from the church tower.
The Mongols destroy Duke Henry II of Silesia's army, Teutonic and Templar knights among it.
Batu and Subutai destroy the Hungarian army; King Bela IV flees to the Adriatic.

items.t: Ogedei dies and the horde turns back
items.x: Word of the great khan's death reaches the army in Hungary; the Mongols withdraw, and the Tzimisce and the Garou of the plains count their dead.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: The two cities agree to guard the road between them, the seed of the Hanseatic League.
After Mohi the Mongols burn Pest and range across Hungary all summer.
A Mongol column crosses Moravia, burning villages and failing before Olomouc.

items.t: Mohi and the burning of Pest
items.x: The Mongols beat the Hungarian army at Mohi on 11 April 1241 and burn Pest. Vencel Rikard's plan to make Buda-Pest the greatest city of the region goes up with it, for a time. Fits: Fits the Mongol invasion card of 1241.
items.ref: Real history (Battle of Mohi, 1241); Vencel Rikard from Transylvania by Night (Dark Ages) p. 105; the setback is a house reading.

items.x: Alexander Nevsky beats the Livonian Knights on frozen Lake Peipus.
Batu sets his capital at Sarai on the Volga; the Rus princes must travel there for leave to rule.
Mongol riders chase King Bela to the coast at Trogir.
The Mongols break the Seljuk sultanate of Rum.
The new pope flees to Lyon to escape Frederick II.
More than two hundred Cathars are burned below the mountain fortress; the Inquisition calls it victory, and the Inquisition is wrong to call it the end.
Khwarazmian horsemen take and wreck Jerusalem.
lk: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.x: An Egyptian and Khwarazmian army destroys the crusader host near Gaza.
The Council of Lyon declares the emperor deposed.
John of Plano Carpini sets out for the Mongol court as the pope's envoy.

items.t: The friars' mission to the Mongols
items.x: The Council of Lyon sends friars east to learn what the Mongols want.
Guyuk becomes great khan with Carpini watching.
Duke Frederick of Austria dies in battle; Austria is left without a lord.

items.t: The Sakya lama and the Mongols
items.x: Sakya Pandita submits Tibet to Godan Khan, the first tie between Tibet and the Mongols.
Ferdinand III takes Seville after a long siege.
The foundation stone of the new cathedral is laid; it will not be finished for six hundred years.
Louis IX consecrates his glass chapel for the Crown of Thorns; the Celestial Chorus calls it a true house of the One.
The Akashic Brotherhood in Tibet watches the lamas bargain with the khans and keeps its own counsel.
Louis IX takes Damietta again.
The silver town of Jihlava writes down its mining code.
The crusaders break into Mansourah and are cut down in its streets by the Mamluks under Baibars.
The French king is taken prisoner and ransomed.
Mamluk officers kill the last Ayyubid sultan of Egypt.
The stupor mundi dies in Apulia; Hohenstaufen power soon collapses.
Bela IV orders stone castles built across Hungary against the Mongols' return.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.t: The mound towns of the south
items.x: Moundville and Etowah are at their height, trading copper, shell and salt along the rivers of the south-east.
Polynesian voyagers settle the last large land on earth without people, and find the giant moa.

In February 1250 the army of Louis IX is trapped at Mansourah and broken. Tariq fights in the city's defence; later Tariq serves the Old Man of the Mountain. Fits: The book ties it to the Seventh Crusade.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 68; the battle of Mansourah, 1250, is real history.

items.x: After a bitter assembly Mongke is raised as great khan and purges Ogedei's line.
Ottokar of Bohemia takes Austria and marries the Babenberg heiress.
Florence strikes the gold florin, soon the standard coin of European trade.
Mindaugas of Lithuania is baptised and crowned, though Lithuania stays pagan.
The Flemish friar reaches the great khan's court and debates Buddhists, Muslims and Nestorians there.
Kublai conquers the kingdom of Dali in Yunnan.
Premysl Ottokar II becomes King of Bohemia, the iron and golden king.
With Conrad IV dead, the empire has no accepted ruler for almost twenty years.
The Teutonic Knights found Konigsberg, named for Ottokar of Bohemia.
The monk Nichiren preaches that the Lotus Sutra alone can save Japan.
Hulegu takes Alamut and the Nizari strongholds; Kindred in the east say the Assamites did not stir, because their Alamut is not this one.
lk: Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.x: Rhineland towns band together to keep the peace on the river roads.

Hulegu's Mongols take the Nizari castle of Alamut in December 1256. Kindred in the east note that the Assamites did not stir: whatever their Alamut is, it is not this one. Fits: Leaves the Assamite Alamut of the books untouched.
items.ref: Real history (fall of Alamut, 1256); the Kindred reading is a house rule.

items.x: Robert de Sorbon founds a college for poor theology students in Paris.
The electors choose both Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso X of Castile.
The Mongols take Baghdad, kill the caliph and throw the libraries into the Tigris; Batini carry out what they can.
English barons force Henry III to share power with a council.
Jalal ad-Din Rumi begins the Masnavi at Konya.
Hulegu has the last Abbasid caliph rolled in a carpet and trampled; the Cainites of Baghdad who lived through the sack go into the desert.
The Mongols sack Baghdad in February 1258; the libraries go into the Tigris. Batini carry out what they can before the walls fall. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (sack of Baghdad, 1258); the Batini are a house reading.

items.x: Henry III gives up his claims to Normandy and Anjou and keeps Gascony as Louis IX's vassal.
The great khan dies besieging a Song fortress; the Mongol armies in Syria and China pause.
The Goryeo crown prince submits to the Mongols.
Hulegu takes Aleppo and Damascus; the Mamluks are next.
The Mamluks under Qutuz and Baibars beat the Mongols in Galilee; the mummies of Egypt call it a reprieve for the river.
Baibars murders Qutuz on the road home and takes the throne.
Ottokar II of Bohemia beats the Hungarians and takes Styria.
Bands of penitents whip themselves through the towns of Italy; the Church is unsure whether to bless them or hunt them.
Kublai and his brother Ariq Boke are both proclaimed great khan; civil war splits the empire.

items.t: The Byzantines take back the city
items.x: Michael VIII Palaiologos's general walks into Constantinople almost without a fight; Latin rule ends, but the Dream does not return.
Baibars sets up an Abbasid survivor as caliph in Cairo to bless Mamluk rule.
The Icelandic chieftains accept the Norwegian king.
Scots and storms drive off a Norwegian fleet; the Hebrides pass to Scotland three years later.
The prince dies returning from the Horde.
Mayapan, a walled city of the Cocom lords, becomes the capital of northern Yucatan.
Simon de Montfort captures Henry III and his son Edward.
Urban IV makes the feast of Corpus Christi a feast of the whole Church.
Simon de Montfort calls knights and burgesses from towns to parliament.
Prince Edward kills Simon de Montfort and cuts the body to pieces.
Baibars takes the crusader towns of the coast one by one.
Charles of Anjou kills King Manfred and takes Sicily and Naples.

items.t: Roger Bacon writes for the pope
items.x: Roger Bacon sends Clement IV his great work on experiment and optics; the craftsmen of the future Order of Reason study it.
Baibars takes Safed from the Templars and kills the garrison.
The painter Giotto di Bondone is born near Florence.
Charles of Anjou defeats Conradin, then beheads the sixteen-year-old in Naples.
Baibars takes Antioch and kills or enslaves its people; the crusader principality ends.
Kublai adopts a new script for all the empire's languages.
The Eighth Crusade ends when the French king dies of dysentery outside Tunis.
Yekuno Amlak overthrows the Zagwe kings and claims descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.
Kublai Khan proclaims the Great Yuan and builds a new capital at Khanbaliq (Beijing).
Marco Polo leaves Venice with his father and uncle for the court of Kublai.
The Hospitallers give up their great castle to Baibars.
Korean soldiers who will not submit to the Mongols hold out on Jeju until 1273.
Edward I becomes king of England while still on crusade.
The German princes choose Rudolf of Habsburg as king, ending the interregnum.
The poet dies at Konya; the whirling dervishes of the Mevlevi order grow from his followers.
Persian engineers' counterweight trebuchets end a five-year siege; the road into southern China is open.
Aquinas dies on the way to the Council of Lyon, his Summa unfinished.

items.t: The first Mongol fleet against Japan
