items.x: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata and then sails off in a storm; the kami are said to have answered.
The Greek envoys accept union with Rome; their church at home does not.
Bonaventure dies during the council; the Messianic Voices lose a friend in the Church's councils.
The Song capital surrenders to the Mongol general Bayan.
Rudolf of Habsburg forces Ottokar II to surrender Austria and Styria.
A drought of more than twenty years begins on the Colorado Plateau, and the cliff towns start to empty.
Bishop Tempier condemns 219 philosophical propositions, many drawn from Aristotle and Averroes.
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is forced to terms.
The Mahdali family takes the throne of Kilwa, and the island city grows rich on the gold of Sofala.
Rudolf of Habsburg kills Ottokar II of Bohemia; Austria passes to the Habsburgs.
The last Song fleet is destroyed at Yamen and the boy emperor drowns; Kuei-jin speak of a turning of the age.
Dinis of Portugal plants pine forests and founds the university at Lisbon.

items.t: Black Earth Boy and the end of the Song
items.x: The last Song fleet is lost at Yamen in 1279. In those years Black Earth Boy rises to the Hundred Clouds, as the Fourth Age turns. Fits: Before the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.
items.ref: Dharma Book: Thrashing Dragons p. 18 (the rise); the year is a house reading; the battle of Yamen, 1279, is real history.

items.x: The Dominican master of natural philosophy dies at Cologne.
Guo Shoujing's astronomers produce the most exact calendar yet made.
The clans of Rapa Nui carve hundreds of stone ancestors from the crater of Rano Raraku and walk them to the coast.
A typhoon wrecks the second, far larger Mongol invasion of Japan; priests and spirits both claim the storm.
The Mamluks beat the Mongols and their Armenian and Georgian allies.
Two Mongol fleets sent against Japan, in 1274 and 1281, are wrecked by storms. Japan's priests and its spirits both claim the victory. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1274, 1281); the claim is a house reading.

items.x: Palermo rises against the French at vespers on Easter Monday; Sicily passes to Aragon.
The last native Prince of Wales dies in a skirmish; Wales is conquered.
Edward I begins Caernarfon, Conwy and Harlech to hold Wales.
The Teutonic Knights finish the conquest of the Prussians.

items.t: The stolen children are not found
items.x: No one finds Hamelin's children; changelings in the German lands keep the tale close.
One hundred and thirty children vanish from Hamelin; the town's records blame a piper, and the fae say nothing.
Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet; Pisa never recovers.
Philip IV becomes King of France.

items.t: Venice and Genoa fight at Acre
items.x: The Italian quarters of Acre are at war with each other.
The king of Scots falls from his horse in a storm; Scotland is left with a child queen in Norway.
A storm surge drowns tens of thousands along the Dutch and German coast.
A Mongol army ends the kingdom of Pagan in Burma.
The burghers of Cologne and their allies break the archbishop's power.
Tran Hung Dao destroys a Mongol fleet on staked river beds in Vietnam.
The Mamluks take Tripoli in Lebanon.
Edward I orders all Jews out of England; they will not be readmitted for over three centuries.
The child queen of Scotland dies on her way from Norway; Edward I is asked to judge between the claimants.
As Mapungubwe is left, the stone walls of Great Zimbabwe go up on the plateau to the north.
The Mamluks storm Acre and the crusader kingdom ends; Kindred of the Military Orders sail for Cyprus with the survivors.
Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear to defend each other, the start of the Swiss Confederation.
A Mongol fleet lands in Java; the Majapahit state rises from the fighting.
Edward I picks John Balliol as King of Scots.
Raden Wijaya uses the Mongols to destroy a rival, then drives them out and founds Majapahit.
The hermit pope resigns after five months; Boniface VIII follows him.
The great khan dies; his empire no longer obeys one ruler.
The Ilkhan Ghazan becomes Muslim, and the Mongols of Persia follow.
The Polos come home to Venice after twenty-four years.
Edward I takes Berwick and kills many of its people; Scotland is conquered.
Alauddin Khalji murders his uncle and takes Delhi; he will beat back several Mongol invasions.
William Wallace and Andrew Moray destroy an English army.
Francesco Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, seizes the rock of Monaco.
Edward I breaks Wallace's army.
A prisoner of Genoa, Marco Polo tells his travels to the writer Rustichello.
Ghazan's Mongols beat the Mamluks near Homs and briefly take Damascus.
Osman's frontier state in Bithynia grows; the Ottomans take their name from him.
Osman's beylik grows on the Byzantine border; Kindred of the Bosporus do not yet think it worth watching.
Boniface VIII proclaims a holy year; pilgrims crowd Rome for full pardon of sins.
Wenceslas II reforms the Bohemian coinage on Kutna Hora silver.
The last families leave Mesa Verde and the Four Corners for the Rio Grande and the Hopi mesas.
The Chimu lords of the Peruvian coast add walled palace after walled palace to their adobe capital.
Whale hunters from the west, ancestors of the Inuit, settle the north of Greenland and meet the Norse.

items.t: The great house of the Hohokam
items.x: The Hohokam of the Gila valley raise a four-storey earthen house among their canals.
The casters of Ife make lifelike heads of brass and copper for the shrines of their kings.
By Hawaiian tradition the priest Paao comes from the south with a new line of chiefs, and voyaging to Tahiti ends.
Andrew III dies; the Arpad kings of Hungary are gone.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Dante Alighieri is banished from Florence and begins the Divine Comedy in exile.
Flemish townsmen kill the French garrison of Bruges at dawn.
Flemish militia destroy the French knights at Courtrai.
Boniface VIII declares that every creature must be subject to the pope.
Osman beats a Byzantine army, his first great victory.
Philip the Fair's men seize Boniface VIII; the pope dies weeks later.
The Mamluks beat Ghazan's last invasion of Syria.
Alauddin Khalji takes the Rajput fortress of Chittor.
In the year the Quincunx is signed, mortal China lies quiet under the Yuan; the courts take it as proof the treaty works.
William Wallace is hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield.
Bertrand de Got becomes Clement V and never goes to Rome.
Robert Bruce kills a rival and is crowned King of Scots.
Philip IV expels the Jews from France and takes their goods.
Wenceslas III is murdered at Olomouc; the Bohemian royal line ends.
On Friday 13 October Philip IV has every Templar in France seized; some say Cainite counsellors or Batini with grudges guided the king.
Edward I dies on his way north to fight Bruce; Edward II takes the throne.
The Teutonic Knights seize Danzig and kill many of its people.
Albert of Habsburg is killed by his nephew.
Clement V settles in Avignon; the popes will stay for nearly seventy years, and the Kindred of Rome lose their nearest grip on the Church.
The Teutonic grand master moves to Marienburg, the largest brick castle in Europe.
The Knights of St John make Rhodes their island base.
John of Luxembourg marries the Premyslid heiress and is chosen King of Bohemia.
The council meets to decide the fate of the Templars.
Clement V dissolves the Order of the Temple and gives its lands to the Hospitallers.
The Mamluk sultan's third reign begins; Cairo reaches its height.
Musa becomes ruler of Mali after the last Mansa sails west into the Atlantic with a great fleet and does not return.
The emperor dies of fever, ending hopes of restoring imperial rule in Italy.
The last Grand Master is burned on an island in the Seine; the tale of a curse on king and pope spreads when both die that year.
Robert Bruce routs Edward II's army.
The king dies after a hunting fall, months after de Molay's death.
Mount Tarawera erupts about this year and buries the north of Aotearoa in ash soon after the first settlers arrive.

Jacques de Molay is burned in Paris on 18 March 1314. The tale that the Grand Master cursed king and pope from the fire, and that both died within the year, runs through Europe. Fits: Follows the fall of the Temple, 1307.
items.ref: Real history (1314); the curse is a legend.

items.x: Swiss peasants ambush and destroy a Habsburg army.
Years of rain ruin the harvests of northern Europe; as many as one in ten die by 1317.
De Varre founds the Solificati, the alchemists who will break away from the Order of Reason.
The Avignon pope who will condemn magic and the Spiritual Franciscans takes office.
John XXII believes enemies tried to kill him with wax images; trials for sorcery follow.
With the herds starving, Kindred across the north feed on the dying and the Masquerade frays in the poorhouses.
The throne hall of the Christian kings of Makuria on the Nile is turned into a mosque.
Four Spiritual Franciscans who would not give up their poverty are burned at Marseille.
Magnus Eriksson inherits both crowns as a child.
Scottish nobles ask the pope to recognise their independence.
Bands of young shepherds march south and massacre Jews; the authorities crush them.
Wladyslaw is crowned King of Poland at Krakow, reuniting the kingdom.
Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq takes Delhi.
Dante dies in exile at Ravenna, the Comedy complete.
Rumour claims lepers poisoned the wells for the Jews and the king of Granada; lepers are burned across France.
Louis of Bavaria captures his rival Frederick of Austria.
Coastal Flanders rises against taxes and lords for five years.
Grand Duke Gediminas invites merchants and craftsmen to Vilnius, his new capital.
Mansa Musa passes through Cairo with so much gold that its price falls for years.
The first witch trial in Ireland; Alice Kyteler escapes to England and a servant is burned in her place. Verbena in Ireland grow careful.
Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier on pilgrimage and travels for nearly thirty years.
In the year the Convention of the White Tower meets, the Order of Reason takes its name.
The Mexica settle an island in Lake Texcoco where, by their story, an eagle sat on a cactus.
Mansa Musa's generals take Gao on the Niger, and Timbuktu comes under Mali.
Orhan takes Bursa and makes it the Ottoman capital.
John XXII declares that sorcery is heresy, giving inquisitors power over it.
The deposed king dies in prison; Edward III, fourteen, takes the throne.
John of Luxembourg brings the Silesian dukes under the Bohemian crown.
An Andalusian architect brought home from the pilgrimage builds the great mud mosque of Timbuktu.
Charles IV dies without a son; Philip VI of Valois takes the crown, and Edward III's claim waits.
Philip VI crushes the Flemish rising.

items.t: Louis of Bavaria crowned in Rome
items.x: Louis IV is crowned emperor by the Roman people and sets up an antipope.
Ivan Kalita becomes Grand Prince with the Horde's blessing, and the metropolitan moves to Moscow.
Orhan beats the Byzantine emperor in Bithynia.
Mages die and the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus is destroyed in the purge of 1330; the scholars of the city never learn why their colleagues vanished.
The Wallachians under Basarab ambush and destroy a Hungarian army in the Carpathians.
The Ottomans take Nicaea.
An epidemic kills many in Hebei; some historians see the first sign of the Black Death.
Stefan Dusan takes the Serbian throne and builds the greatest Serbian state.

items.t: Ibn Battuta on the Swahili coast
items.x: The traveller visits Mogadishu, Mombasa and Kilwa and calls Kilwa one of the finest towns in the world.
Emperor Go-Daigo rises against the Kamakura shogunate.
The Ethiopian emperor Amda Seyon breaks the sultanate of Ifat and its allies in a single campaign.
Nitta Yoshisada takes Kamakura; the Hojo regents kill themselves and the shogunate ends.
Edward III's archers destroy a Scottish army.
The Arno sweeps away Florence's bridges.
Casimir III becomes King of Poland and builds the country in stone.
Giotto begins the campanile of Florence cathedral.
The governor of Madurai breaks from Delhi.
Abu Said dies without an heir; Mongol Persia falls apart.
The kings of Hungary, Poland and Bohemia meet at Visegrad and agree on trade and borders.
Ashikaga Takauji takes Kyoto; Go-Daigo flees to Yoshino, and the Northern and Southern courts begin.
Harihara and Bukka found the empire of Vijayanagara in southern India.
Philip VI confiscates Gascony; Edward III claims the French crown.
The painter who changed Italian art dies in Florence.
Ashikaga Takauji becomes shogun.
The electors declare that the man they choose is king without the pope's leave.
Graves of Christian merchants near Lake Issyk-Kul record a pestilence; Garou far to the west smell something coming.
Venice expands on the mainland at Verona's cost.
The English destroy the French fleet off Flanders.
Castile and Portugal beat the last great Marinid invasion of Spain.
Poland begins to take Galicia-Volhynia.
A civil war between John Kantakouzenos and the regency of John V begins; both sides hire Turks.
England and France fight over Brittany through rival dukes.
The traveller serves Muhammad bin Tughluq as a judge.
The priest Ivar Bardarson sails to the Western Settlement of Norse Greenland about this year and finds only loose cattle.
The worst recorded flood in central Europe sweeps the Rhine, Main and Danube.
The great Florentine banks begin to fail after Edward III defaults on his loans.
Estonian peasants rise against German lords and are crushed.
Charles of Luxembourg, already ruling Bohemia for his father, plans to make Prague a capital; the Ventrue of the Empire take interest.
A crusader league takes the harbour of Smyrna from the Turks.
Work begins on the new cathedral of St. Vitus in Prague.
The Bardi bank collapses, taking much of Florence's wealth with it.
The Bahmani nobles break the Deccan away from Delhi; the Bahmani sultanate is founded in 1347.
The leader of Ghent is murdered by a mob.
English longbowmen cut down the French knights; the blind King John of Bohemia dies in the charge.
The English capture David II of Scotland.
The Mongol army besieging Caffa in the Crimea is struck by plague; Genoese ships will carry it west.
Edward III begins an eleven-month siege of Calais.
Charles of Luxembourg is chosen King of the Romans against Louis of Bavaria.
Stefan Dusan is crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks.

appr.x: In September 1212 Frederick II confirms Bohemia as a hereditary kingdom under the Premyslids, with Moravia as its margraviate. The valley answers to a king in Prague, a margrave and, at night, to whoever holds Kranzfels.
Ventrue of the Empire send envoys east to learn who holds the Moravian march. The Tzimisce of the hills receive them coldly and send them home with gifts that are also warnings.
In the spring and summer of 1241 Mongol riders cross Moravia, burning villages and failing before walled places. The valley's families hide their own, and their Kindred, in the hills and the mine.

appr.t: The hill sept fights the riders' spirits
appr.x: The Garou of the Moravian hills meet the spirits riding with the Mongol host. They hold their caern but lose half their number, and their Kinfolk among the old families grow fewer.
The silver town of Jihlava (Iglau) sets down its mining law, which becomes the rule for workings across Moravia and Bohemia. Rothenstein's German council claims the Adit under it.

appr.t: The king falls on the Marchfeld
appr.x: On 26 August 1278 King Premysl Otakar II dies fighting Rudolf of Habsburg. Bad years follow: regents plunder the land and famine reaches the margraviate.

appr.t: Kutna Hora silver and the Prague groschen
appr.x: The great strike at Kutna Hora and the new Prague groschen of 1300 pull miners away from smaller workings. The Adit's silver is worth less and its miners drift away.
On 4 August 1306 the young King Wenceslas III is stabbed in Olomouc and the Premyslid line ends. Kindred of the march whisper that a Cainite hand guided the knife; no one proves it.
John of Luxembourg takes the Bohemian crown. German settlers keep arriving, and the towns and the old Moravian villages grow further apart.

appr.t: A citadel in the Moravian Shadowlands
appr.x: A legion of the Hierarchy raises a citadel in the Shadowlands of Moravia to hold the restless dead of the mines. It will outlast nearly every other in the east.
Dominican inquisitors work the Bohemian crown lands against Waldensian heretics. One passes through the valley, asks the parish many questions, and writes down the answers.
On 30 April 1344 Prague is raised to an archbishopric over the bishops of Olomouc and Litomysl. The parish of St. Aegidius now answers to a church of its own crown.
The last trod near the valley, at the old crossroads, opens on fewer nights each year. The fae who use it feel the cold coming.
Around 1197 the city stands at the edge of ruin, threatening to drag the Dream down with it.
The mechanical clock began with Benedictine monks around 1200 to time prayers; some say it also served Time magick.
The crusaders took Byzantium in 1204 and set up a feudal Latin Empire, also called Romania, with the emperor above vassals such as the King of Thessalonica and the Prince of Achaia.
The Toreador Methuselah Michael, the Patriarch of Constantinople, met Final Death in 1204, but that influence lingers.
Ghouls abandoned when the Trinity families burned or fled in 1204 now hunt Cainites from the Grand Bazaar.
Most Heretics expect the Third Caine to appear in 1206 and dwell on earth for thirty-three years, like Christ.
Bramber Castle in Sussex is said to hold the ghosts of three de Braose children starved by King John and of Lady Maud de Hurst, murdered in 1210.
The Hermetic sanctum at Mistridge fell in 1210, brought down by mortals led by a group calling itself the Craftmasons.
Mages have already used magic to build such weapons, and several cannon were fired in the destruction of the Mistridge Covenant in 1210.
The Craftmasons destroyed Mistridge in the winter of 1210, and the Convention of the White Tower met on 25 March 1325.
Roger Bacon's influence among the High Artisans remains immense; the Craftmasons showed their strength in 1210 when they brought down Mistridge with cannon.
A moderate Ventrue faction, the Antasians, watched over the crowning of Frederick II at Frankfurt in 1212.

After the Children's Crusade of 1212, Giselher, Ventrue prince of Cologne, barred Clan Lasombra from the city. Giselher never proved the Magisters were behind it, but used the charge against rivals anyway.
Before 1215 the vial was widely believed to have reached Cistercian monks near the start of the 12th century, though how it got there is unclear.
Given as a child to a Benedictine priory in the twelfth century, Marc ran away at sixteen and was Embraced in 1216 by Megan of Bristol, a Gangrel of the 10th Generation.

appr.t: Eye for the Weakness of Steel
appr.x: It began among the Fellowship of Our Lady, a company of Toreador and Ventrue, and it passed to their successors after the Fellowship broke apart in 1218 through infighting.
Paris is the seat of the joint Toreador and Ventrue Grand Court. Geoffrey, a Ventrue, has led it as Prince of Paris since 1222, after overthrowing Alexander, Geoffrey's own sire.
A Toreador of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1229 by Maiselle of Rochester, born in the village of Strood.

Cretheus, Fifth Generation Ventrue and childe of Mithras, ruled Rome in fact for nearly 300 years and is the only public member of the Ignoti; bending the knee to Camilla in 1229 was read as the hidden ones' blessing.
It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.
In 1230 common superstition supports belief in magic, which helps mages cast with impunity; only in later ages does belief turn against them.
A few great diseases cause most deaths in 1230; some can empty a village in weeks, others leave victims wasted husks.
In May of 1230 an eclipse darkens the sky so deeply that workers go home thinking night has come.
The Garou of 1230 count Ten Tribes.
They see this era as a time to feed on the spreading chaos and fear and to prepare for the Golden Horde, which turns west in 1235 and pulls back in 1242.
Counting from a creation date of 3761 B.C.E. and five stages of a thousand years each, Heretics expect the material world to end in 1239.
With Kin of their own among the Mongol clans, the Shadow Lords quietly backed the Tatar Yoke over Russia from about 1240 to 1480.
By the 1240s Italy is only a name on the map; loyalty comes from the cities, swollen by migrants from the countryside.

appr.t: Kupala's Eve and the Tzimisce revolt
appr.x: The Mongol invasion of 1241 broke Tzimisce holdings in the east and nearly destroyed the elder known as the Butcher of Rus. Elders tightened their grip on their thralls in response.
A diary of 1242 tells of a coterie sent by an unnamed powerful patron, chasing clues through Dublin, Edinburgh and Norwich toward London.
Most of its men-at-arms die at Gaza in 1244, and its time in the Holy Land is ending during the 13th century.
A Ventrue of the 7th Generation, Embraced in 1263 by Palamon the Copt; a few childhood memories of the mountains are all that remain from before Egypt.
Roger Bacon's London Accord of 1268 ended the war among England's artisan guilds; de Varre founded the Solificati in 1315, and they broke away from the Order of Reason in 1335.

appr.t: The Hospitallers and the Teutonic Knights
appr.x: Large endowments in Western Europe fund the Hospitallers' work in the East, a structure that lets the order outlast the loss of the Holy Land in 1291.
Around 1300 the wandering Caern of Long Voyages was thrown into an attack on a Zmei's servants in southern Russia and lost with its whole sept.
The last reliable account dates to about 1300, back when the tribe still kept its alliance with Helios and the Mound Builder Dreamspeakers.

In 1304, ten years after Kublai Khan died, ancestors from three courts (Yellow Emperor, White Tiger and Black Tortoise) met at the Shaolin monastery near Changan and signed the Treaty of the Quincunx.
King Philip the Fair had the French Templars seized in 1307 on heresy charges, with papal leave, and is widely thought to have wanted their wealth.
In 1307 Philip the Fair had the French Templars arrested for heresy; some say vampire advisors or Batini with grudges pushed the king.

appr.t: The Way of the Ancient Lawgivers
appr.x: Founded in 1312, it holds that all Kindred must return to the ways of the First City, when mortals and lesser vampires honoured the Antediluvians.
Ten years on they wrote that purpose down as the Chodona, the Wheel of the Law with eight spokes; by 1314 the Wheel stretched from Nepal to Ireland.
Pagans gathered there as a refuge from persecution, and in 1317 Sir Garland declared the land a fief named Baerwald, an open insult to Rome and the Empire.
In 1325, as that Order formally began, mathematicians made a sub-lodge, the Arithmeticians, never strong enough to be a Convention.
A Ventrue antitribu of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1327 by Leander Phipps, once a Templar in the Crusades.
The Paris University Purge of 1330 killed many mages and destroyed the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus.
The War of the Dust Witch near Great Zimbabwe, 1345 to 1350, split the Ngoma and the Madzimbabwe into separate groups; plague in 1420 set them at war, each blaming the other.

items.x: Calais yields to Edward III after eleven months; the burghers offer their lives and are spared.
Genoese galleys bring the plague to Sicily; the Second Great Maelstrom gathers as the dead cross in numbers no one has seen.
The pestilence reaches Constantinople; the emperor's son is among the dead.
lk: The great schism and the Paladins

items.x: The notary Cola di Rienzo takes power in Rome as tribune of the people.
The Deccan nobles found the Bahmani sultanate at Gulbarga.
Charles IV is crowned King of Bohemia with the new crown of St. Wenceslas.
Charles IV founds Prague New Town, one of the largest town plans in Europe.
The plague comes ashore in Provence and moves up the Rhone.
Perhaps half of Florence dies; Boccaccio sets the Decameron among young people fleeing it.
Charles IV founds the first university north of the Alps in Prague.
The plague lands at a Dorset port and reaches London by autumn.
The plague reaches Cairo; at its height thousands die a day.
The people of Damascus fast and pray together, Muslims, Christians and Jews.
Clement VI's physician keeps the pope between two great fires; the pope survives and buys Avignon outright.
The Hierarchy cannot ferry the dead fast enough; whole towns' worth of wraiths wander the Shadowlands unclaimed.
Kindred who feed on the sick sicken their herds and sometimes the Masquerade; some princes forbid feeding in plague houses.
An earthquake shakes the eastern Alps; preachers say it opened the earth for the plague.
Prague becomes the emperor's city; Kindred from the west come to court it.
Charles IV begins Karlstejn castle to keep the crown jewels and relics.
A ship drifts into Bergen with its crew dead of plague; the town soon follows.
The pestilence reaches Tunis and kills the parents and teachers of the young Ibn Khaldun.
Hundreds of Jews are burned in Strasbourg on the charge of poisoning wells, before the plague even arrives.
Processions of flagellants cross Germany; the pope condemns them in October.
The Jewish communities of the Rhineland are destroyed.
A ship brings the plague to Bergen; Norway loses perhaps half its people.
The plague reaches Moravia, lighter than in the west but bad in the towns.
Edward III forbids wages above the old rates; there are too few hands left to obey.
Hermetic healers and Chorus monks die tending the sick; the young Order of Reason studies the plague's spread.
The Jews of Basel are burned on an island in the Rhine.
Banality closes the trods to Arcadia; fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.
The king of Castile dies of plague at the siege of Gibraltar.
Pilgrims crowd Rome despite the plague.
King Ramathibodi founds Ayutthaya in Siam.
The English beat a Castilian fleet in the Channel.
With half the people dead, landlords in Tuscany cannot find tenants; wages climb.
With villages emptied, wolves come into the fields; Garou Kinfolk families are among the few still farming.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The last people leave the mound city on the Mississippi; no later nation claims to have built it.
The Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan begins in the Huai valley.
Parliament defines high treason.
The Delhi sultan who moved his capital and made copper coins worth silver dies on campaign.
The Second Great Maelstrom begins to ease; Stygia counts its lost Legions.
The Ottomans take the fortress of Tzympe on the Gallipoli peninsula, their first foothold in Europe.
The Hierarchy gathers the plague dead into new Legions as the storm passes.
The traveller rides with a salt caravan to Mali and writes down the court of Mansa Sulayman.
Boccaccio finishes the Decameron.
John Kantakouzenos gives up the throne and becomes a monk.
An earthquake shatters Gallipoli's walls; the Ottomans move in and settle the town.
In the plague years Cairo's Kindred shift and shuffle; newcomers find room where the dead left gaps.
The returned tribune is killed by a Roman mob.
Charles IV is crowned in Rome and leaves the same day, as promised.
A tavern brawl at Oxford becomes a two-day battle; dozens of students die.
The doge of Venice is beheaded for plotting to make himself lord of the city.
Stefan Dusan dies on the way to attack Constantinople; his empire breaks up.
Charles IV fixes the seven electors and the rules for choosing a king.
The Black Prince captures King John II of France.
The war between Dalou'laoshi, the Wu Lung and the Akashics begins; it will drive the Brotherhood back into Tibet by 1360.
The strongest recorded earthquake in central Europe wrecks Basel.
Another wave of plague strikes the city.
The provost of Paris merchants forces reforms on the dauphin.
The foundation stone of the stone bridge over the Vltava is laid.
The peasants of northern France rise against the nobles and are crushed within weeks.
The Paris leader is killed as he tries to open the city to Charles of Navarre.
Charles IV plans a new stone bridge across the Vltava; it is begun in 1357.
Venice runs convoys of galleys to Alexandria and Beirut each year for spices.
England gives up its claim to France in return for Aquitaine and Calais.
The Screaming Ghost Purge ends; the Akashics withdraw into Tibet.
Japanese pirates raid Korea and China throughout the 1360s.
The plague returns, killing many children born since 1348.
Murad I takes Adrianople; as Edirne it becomes the Ottoman capital.
Lithuania beats the Golden Horde and takes Kiev.
Zhu Yuanzhang destroys his chief rival's fleet in one of the largest naval battles ever fought.
John II gives Burgundy to his son Philip; the Valois dukes of Burgundy begin.

items.t: The papal court in the plague years
items.x: The Avignon popes' court thrives as plague returns; Lasombra in the Curia grow richer with each death.
Casimir the Great founds a university at Krakow.
The French king dies in London, having returned to captivity.
Rudolf IV founds a university at Vienna.
Peter I of Cyprus sacks Alexandria for a week.
The English lords of Ireland are forbidden to marry, speak or dress as the Irish do.
Astronomy is taught at Prague's new university.
The Black Prince wins for Pedro the Cruel in Castile.
Zhu Yuanzhang founds the Ming and drives the Mongols out of Khanbaliq.
The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change of dynasty.
The Yuan court flees north to the steppe; Garou of Mongolia see the old horde come back broken.

Zhu Yuanzhang drives the Mongols from Beijing and founds the Ming in 1368. The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change. Fits: After the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.
items.ref: Real history (1368); the courts' reading is a house rule.

items.x: Pedro of Castile is stabbed by his half-brother Henry, who takes the throne.
Charles V of France restarts the war and slowly takes back Aquitaine.
Timur becomes master of Transoxiana.
The Black Prince storms Limoges; chroniclers tell of thousands killed.
The Hanseatic towns force Denmark to yield; the League is at its height.
The Ottomans destroy the Serbian lords of Macedonia.
Robert II, the first Stewart, becomes King of Scots.
The Hongwu emperor forbids private sea trade; smuggling grows on the coasts.
A Castilian fleet destroys the English off La Rochelle.
A Ming army is badly beaten in Mongolia.
The poet who first called the past ages dark dies near Padua.
Crowds dance in the streets of Aachen and along the Rhine for days; priests try to cast out what moves them.
The author of the Decameron dies at Certaldo.
Jewish mapmakers of Majorca draw the Catalan Atlas, showing Mansa Musa on his throne.
The Mamluks take Sis, ending the Armenian kingdom of Cilicia.

items.t: The first king of the Mexica
items.x: Acamapichtli becomes the first tlatoani of Tenochtitlan, still a tributary of the Tepanecs.
The Chimu conquer the Lambayeque valleys and carry their goldsmiths back to Chan Chan.
Edward III's heir dies of a long sickness.
The Commons impeach the king's ministers for the first time.
Gregory XI leaves Avignon for Rome.
Richard II, ten years old, becomes king.
A Korean Buddhist text is printed with movable metal type at Cheongju.
Choe Mu-seon begins making gunpowder weapons against the pirates.
Rival popes in Rome and Avignon divide Western Christendom for forty years.
The wool workers of Florence rise and briefly take power.
The emperor dies in Prague; Wenceslas IV becomes king.
Charles's son Wenceslas takes the throne of Bohemia.
John Wycliffe denies that the bread of the mass changes; the Messianic Voices and the Order of Reason both read him closely.
Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow beats the Horde's general Mamai on the Don.
Venice breaks a Genoese siege of the lagoon and wins its long war.
The wise king of France dies; Charles VI, eleven, follows.
After Kulikovo the Shadow Lords' Mongol kin are less sure of their hold on the Rus princes.
By the Kano Chronicle King Yaji accepts Islam from Wangara traders about this time and builds a mosque.
Wat Tyler's rebels take London; that same year young Kindred across the west rise against their elders, and the Anarch Revolt begins.
The rebel leader is killed at Smithfield in front of the king.
John Ball preaches: when Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?

The Peasants' Revolt takes London in June 1381. Elders of the west see the same thing in their own childer that summer: the Anarch Revolt begins. Fits: The Anarch Revolt begins in 1381 on the approved cards.
items.ref: Real history (Peasants' Revolt, 1381); the link is a house reading.

items.x: The khan of the Horde sacks and burns Moscow.
The French crush the Flemish towns.
Philip van Artevelde leads Ghent against the Count of Flanders.
The last Burgundian king of Portugal dies and Castile claims the throne.
Timur takes Herat and razes its walls.
Wycliffe dies of a stroke; his followers, the Lollards, carry on.
Portugal beats Castile and keeps its independence.
Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agrees to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland and be baptised.
The Cortes chooses John of Aviz as king.
The Swiss destroy an Austrian army and kill its duke.
The Elector Palatine founds a university at Heidelberg.
Jogaila is baptised as Wladyslaw and crowned King of Poland; Lithuania is baptised.
England and Portugal swear an alliance that still stands.
Timur sacks Tbilisi and captures the Georgian king.
Geoffrey Chaucer begins the Canterbury Tales.
Lithuania's baptism closes the last great pagan country in Europe; Kindred who kept the old gods' shrines go deeper into the forests.
Sigismund of Luxembourg is crowned King of Hungary.
The Scots beat the English in the borders; Douglas dies winning.
Ottoman armies overrun northern Bulgaria.
After a revolt Timur has Isfahan's people killed and their heads piled in towers; the Shadowlands of Persia overflow.
Serbs and Ottomans fight at Kosovo; both Prince Lazar and Sultan Murad die.
A mob kills hundreds of Jews in Prague's Jewish town at Easter.
Preaching at Seville stirs the hatred that will explode in 1391.
Preachers in Prague call for the Church to give up its wealth.
By tradition Lukeni lua Nimi crosses the Congo river about this year and founds the kingdom of Kongo.
Massacres spread from Seville across Castile and Aragon; thousands of Jews are killed or forced to convert.
Thousands of Spanish Jews are baptised under threat; the Church will hunt their descendants for centuries.
Yi Seong-gye overthrows Goryeo and founds Joseon.
The Northern and Southern courts of Japan are joined under the Ashikaga.
The French king attacks his own escort in a forest near Le Mans; his madness returns for the rest of his life.
Healers and sorcerers are brought to cure Charles VI's madness; two are burned when they fail.

items.t: The Ball of the Burning Men
items.x: Courtiers dressed as wild men catch fire at a masked ball; the king barely escapes.
The Ottomans take the Bulgarian capital.
The Joseon king moves the capital to Hanyang (Seoul).

items.t: The Jews expelled from France again
items.x: Charles VI expels the Jews from France.
The Paris masters demand both popes resign.
Timur breaks Tokhtamysh and the Golden Horde.
Mircea the Elder of Wallachia fights the Ottomans to a standstill.
Bohemian painting and book art reach their height under Wenceslas.
The Ottomans destroy a great crusader army on the Danube.
The Bohemian lords lock up their king.
Denmark, Norway and Sweden are joined under Queen Margaret's heir.
Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici founds the Medici bank in Florence.
The Ottoman siege of the city lasts until Ankara saves it.
Timur takes Delhi and kills tens of thousands; the city is empty for months.
The founder of the Ming dies; his grandson takes the throne.
Henry Bolingbroke takes the throne as Henry IV.
The Horde crushes Lithuania's Grand Duke Vytautas.
The Prince of Yan rebels against his nephew the emperor.
Famine and plague empty Delhi after the sack.
The deposed king dies in prison, probably starved.
Owain Glyndwr is proclaimed Prince of Wales and rises against the English.
The electors depose Wenceslas IV as King of the Romans for doing nothing.
Geoffrey Chaucer dies in London.
By 1400 the Anarch Revolt has reached much of Europe; elders die in their havens, and the Assamites sell their blades to the young.
Timur takes Sivas and buries thousands of its defenders alive.
Perhaps eighteen thousand people live around the stone enclosures, trading gold for Chinese porcelain and Persian glass.
The Sunni rulers of Gao stop paying tribute to a weakened Mali.
The giant birds of Aotearoa are hunted out within a few generations, and the people turn to the sea, fern root and the kumara.
Voyagers from Aotearoa settle the Chatham Islands and in time become the Moriori.
The forest of Rapa Nui is nearly gone, and the islanders mulch their gardens with stone.
Timur takes Baghdad and builds towers of skulls.
Timur takes Damascus and carries its craftsmen to Samarkand; Ibn Khaldun meets him outside the walls.
Ghiberti wins the contest for the bronze doors of the Florence baptistery.
Timur beats and captures Sultan Bayezid; the Ottoman state falls into civil war.
The Prince of Yan takes Nanjing and becomes the Yongle emperor.
Timur takes Smyrna from the Hospitallers.
Sigismund imprisons his brother Wenceslas in Vienna.
Jan Hus begins preaching reform in Czech at Prague.
Henry IV kills Harry Hotspur.
Timur builds a vast mosque at Samarkand.
John the Fearless becomes Duke of Burgundy.
Timur dies at Otrar on his way to conquer China.
Zheng He sails with the first of seven great fleets.
Timur's son Shah Rukh takes Herat and holds the empire's heart.
Mukhtar Bey takes the domain of Cairo.
The Yongle emperor's armies invade Dai Viet.
The historian who wrote of the rise and fall of dynasties dies in Cairo.
The heir to Scotland is taken at sea by the English and kept eighteen years.
The Duke of Burgundy has the king's brother killed in a Paris street; civil war follows.
Scholars finish a vast encyclopedia of Chinese learning.

items.t: Kindred and the murder in the rue Vieille-du-Temple
items.x: Parisian Kindred whisper that the Duke of Orleans's killers had help; no one names whose.
France splits between two noble parties; Kindred of the Grand Court back both.
A wedding at Hvalsey church is the last written record of the Norse in Greenland.
The Council of Pisa elects a third pope to end the schism; none of the others steps down.
King Wenceslas gives the Czechs control of Prague university; the German masters walk out and found Leipzig.
The German masters who left Prague found a university at Leipzig.
Poland and Lithuania break the Teutonic Order.
The Yongle emperor leads the first of five campaigns into Mongolia.
The astronomical clock is set in the Old Town hall.
The Highland Lord of the Isles and the Earl of Mar fight a bloody draw.
The Teutonic Order pays heavily after Grunwald.
Bayezid's sons fight for the throne.
Joan of Arc is born at Domremy.
Hus preaches against papal indulgences; three young men are beheaded for protesting.
Mehmed I ends the Ottoman civil war.
Henry V becomes king.
Paris butchers and skinners rise and terrorise the court.
The great council meets to end the schism and judge Hus.
Lollards rise under Sir John Oldcastle and are crushed.
Zheng He's fleet brings a giraffe from Bengal to Beijing; the court calls it a qilin.
Hus is burned at Constance under a broken safe-conduct; the Church's hunters learn nothing from it.
Portugal takes Ceuta in North Africa, the start of its empire.
Henry V's archers destroy the French nobility.
Four hundred Czech nobles seal a protest against Hus's burning.
Envoys of Malindi send a giraffe to the Ming court with the treasure fleet, and the fleet later visits the Swahili coast.
Hus's friend Jerome is burned at Constance.
Venice destroys an Ottoman fleet.
Martin V is elected; the Great Schism is over.
Henry V starves Rouen into surrender.
The Burgundians take Paris and kill Armagnacs in the streets.
The Tepanecs kill the king of Texcoco, and the young prince Nezahualcoyotl flees into the hills.
Hussites throw the councillors of Prague New Town from the windows; the Hussite Wars begin.
The Duke of Burgundy is killed meeting the dauphin; Burgundy joins England.
Sejong the Great becomes King of Joseon.
Kindred of Prague watch the townsmen take the city; some find the Hussite fervour poor ground for the Masquerade.
Henry V is made heir to France and marries Charles VI's daughter.
Jan Zizka's Hussites beat the first crusade against them outside Prague.
The Ming capital moves to Beijing and the palace is finished.
Radical Hussites build a town on a hill and call it Tabor.
The Hussites demand the cup for all, free preaching, a poor clergy and punishment of sin.
By tradition the chief Mailikukahi divides Oahu into districts running from the mountain to the sea.
Zizka's war wagons break out of a crusader trap.
The Czech diet declares Sigismund unfit to rule.
Zizka exterminates the Adamites, a radical sect said to go naked and hold all things common.
Henry V and Charles VI die within weeks; the infant Henry VI is king of both realms on paper.
Murad II besieges Constantinople and fails.
Hussite armies raid into Hungary, Silesia and Saxony.
The Byzantine governor sells Thessalonica to Venice.
Zizka beats the Prague Hussites at Horice.
The English destroy a Franco-Scottish army.
The blind Hussite general dies of plague; Prokop the Bald leads after him.
Hussite armies campaign through Moravia; Catholic lords and towns hold out.
The Yongle emperor dies on campaign in Mongolia.
A university is founded at Leuven.
The Hussites destroy a German army.
Masaccio paints the Brancacci chapel.
A crusading army runs at the sound of the Hussite hymn.

items.t: Le Loi drives out the Ming
items.x: Le Loi wins Vietnam's independence and founds the Le dynasty.
The English begin the siege of Orleans.
Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan destroy Azcapotzalco and divide the tribute of the valley among themselves.
Joan of Arc lifts the siege of Orleans; the Church's hunters argue for years over what spoke to her.
Joan brings the dauphin to be crowned at Reims.
The Hussite armies take Silesian towns.
Murad II takes Thessalonica from Venice.
Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Fleece.
The Hussites raid deep into Saxony, Franconia and Bavaria.
A prince of Great Zimbabwe moves north to the Zambezi about this year and founds the Mutapa kingdom.
Joan is burned at Rouen.
The last crusade against the Hussites flees without a fight.
A church council meets that will bargain with the Hussites.
Siam sacks Angkor; the Khmer court moves south.
Nezahualcoyotl is crowned in Texcoco and gives it law courts, archives and gardens.
Joan of Arc relieves Orleans in May 1429 and is burned at Rouen on 30 May 1431. The Church's hunters argue for years over what spoke to her. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1429, 1431); the hunters are a house reading.

items.x: Jan van Eyck finishes the altarpiece begun by his brother.
Bruges is the market of northern Europe, home to the Medici and Italian banks.
Van Eyck's oils catch the light so truly that Ecstatics and the craftsmen of the Order of Reason both claim the method.
Zheng He dies on the seventh voyage; the Ming never send the fleets again.
Sigismund is crowned emperor in Rome.
Tuareg riders take Timbuktu from Mali.
Moderate Hussites destroy the radicals; Prokop dies.
Cosimo comes back from exile and rules Florence in fact.
Gil Eanes sails past the cape the Portuguese feared.
Cosimo de' Medici takes Florence in hand; Toreador and Ventrue of the city both court the bank.
Elders form the Camarilla to save themselves from the revolt and the Inquisition.
Burgundy makes peace with France; the English are alone.
The council quarrels with the pope over who rules the Church.
Gil Eanes and Afonso Baldaia sail far past the cape and find the tracks of men and camels on the shore.
The Hussites and the Church make peace at Jihlava; the Czechs keep the cup.
Florence cathedral's dome is finished.
The French retake Paris from the English.
Sigismund is accepted as King of Bohemia after the Compacts.
The last Luxembourg emperor dies; Albert of Habsburg follows.
Transylvanian peasants rise; the nobles, Saxons and Szekelys league against them.
Greek and Latin churchmen meet at Ferrara and then Florence.
A prince of Cuzco beats back the Chanka, takes the name Pachacuti and begins the Inca conquests.
The Greeks accept union with Rome at Florence; at home they reject it.
Johannes Gutenberg works on printing with movable type in Strasbourg and Mainz.
The council deposes Eugenius IV and elects the Duke of Savoy as Felix V.
Joan's comrade Gilles de Rais is tried for murdering children and hanged at Nantes.
Baldric, Lady Nightshade and Master Valorian meet in the ruins of Mistridge and agree to found an order.
Fra Angelico paints the cells of San Marco.
Frederick of Habsburg becomes King of the Romans; he will reign 53 years.
Moctezuma Ilhuicamina becomes ruler of the Mexica and carries their wars to the Gulf coast.
Ewuare becomes Oba of Benin, rebuilds the city with walls and wide streets and makes the palace guilds of brass casters.
Portuguese ships bring the first enslaved Africans to Lisbon.
The Mamluk sultan takes control of the pepper trade.
The Xiu lords rise against the Cocom and burn Mayapan; Yucatan breaks into quarrelling provinces.
Alfonso V of Aragon conquers Naples.
John Hunyadi beats the Ottomans twice in Transylvania.
King Sejong's scholars complete a new alphabet.
Skanderbeg leaves the Ottoman army and raises Albania against the sultan.
Hunyadi and Wladyslaw push deep into the Balkans.
The Ottomans destroy a crusade and kill the young King Wladyslaw of Poland and Hungary.
Augustus Giovanni diablerises the founder of the Cappadocians.
Hungary makes a ten-year peace with the Ottomans, broken within weeks.
The twelve-year-old Mehmed becomes sultan when his father steps aside.
Portuguese ships pass the desert coast and reach the green land south of the Senegal river.
The plague returns to Cairo, as it has every generation since 1347.
Portuguese sailors round Cape Verde.
The Ethiopian emperor Zara Yaqob defeats the sultan of Adal at Gomit.
Sejong publishes the new alphabet for the common people.
John Hunyadi is made regent of Hungary.
Locusts strip the fields of the Valley of Mexico.
King Sejong publishes Hangul in 1446, an alphabet made so that common people can read. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1446).

items.x: Pope Nicholas V begins collecting the books of the Vatican library.
Filippo Maria Visconti dies; Milan becomes a republic for three years.
The Ottomans beat John Hunyadi.
The Hussite lord George of Podebrady takes Prague by surprise.
Constantine XI becomes emperor of a city and little else.
The house reading has Traditions and Daedaleans arm for the wars over the Council of Nine that break out in 1450.
The Mongol Oirats capture the Ming emperor at Tumu.
The astronomer-prince of Samarkand is killed on his son's orders.
Milan briefly governs itself after the last Visconti dies.
The house reading has mages gather to raise Horizon, whose Nodes are dedicated in 1452 before the Grand Convocation.
lk: Etherspace, the Deep Umbra and the Void

items.x: Minister Yu Qian holds Beijing against the Oirats after the emperor's capture.
Charles VII begins the reconquest of Normandy.
Lake Texcoco floods Tenochtitlan, and Nezahualcoyotl designs a dike nine miles long to hold it back.

appr.x: On 7 April 1348 Charles IV founds the university in Prague. Hermetic masters and the first members of the Order of Reason both send students there to watch each other.
The Black Death reaches Moravia in 1349 and 1350, lighter than in the west but bad in the towns. The Herd thins, the parish buries in pits, and the Shadowlands fill.
At the Shattering the crossroads trod closes. The valley's fae who stay hide in mortal bodies among the old families.
Charles IV is crowned emperor in Rome in 1355. Prague is the Empire's capital, and Kindred of the west take more notice of the east.
The Anarch Revolt, begun in 1381, reaches Moravia. Young Kindred and their ghouls rise against the Tzimisce of the hills; some lords are burned in their beds, some hold.
On 6 July 1415 Jan Hus is burned at Constance. Preachers of his cause reach the valley within the year.

On 30 July 1419 the councillors of Prague New Town are thrown from the windows, and war follows until Lipany in May 1434. Moravia splits between Catholic lords and Hussite towns; the parish and the council take opposite sides.
The Craftmasons watch the Hussite war wagons and handguns closely, and some of the Hussite smiths hear from them. The Order of Hermes watches the Craftmasons.
In the war years the Church sees heresy in every town. Its hunters in Moravia find more Hussites than monsters, but now and then a monster.
When the Camarilla forms, the Tzimisce of the Moravian hills refuse it. The march is left to them, and to the families who hide them.
Through the plague years and the war the Hierarchy's Moravian citadel takes in the dead of the battlefields and grows strong.

appr.t: The Black Death and the Second Great Maelstrom
appr.x: Plague reaches Europe. The dead cross the Shroud in such numbers that the Second Great Maelstrom breaks over the Underworld.
Banality closes the ways to Arcadia. The last open trods fail and the fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.
Once a Castilian soldier fighting to retake Cadiz, Roderigo was Embraced in 1354 by Mokhadaji Ranpur, a Nagaraja of the 6th Generation.
The Screaming Ghost Purge of 1356 to 1360 set Dalou'laoshi and Wu Lung against the Akashics and drove the Brotherhood back into Tibet.
Brujah signed twice, since clan members sat on both sides of the table. Most European Kindred active when the revolt began in 1381 were dead by its end in 1493.
The Resolute Knights of St. George were founded in Syria in the 11th century and by the 1400s had houses from Ireland to India.
Mukhtar Bey has held the domain since first claiming it in 1406.
Elders of several clans bind themselves into one sect to hide the Kindred from the Inquisition.
Lady Nightshade's story begins in Harrogate, England, at Midsummer of 1435.

In 1440 the Hermetic master Baldric met Lady Nightshade of the Verbena and Master Valorian of the Chorus in the ruins of Mistridge, where fae are said to have visited them, and the three agreed to found an order.
Augustus Giovanni diablerizes Cappadocius. The Giovanni set out to destroy what is left of the clan.
Augustus Giovanni diablerized the Cappadocian founder in 1444, rising to the Third Generation and splitting the old clan from the Venetian family.
Giovanni tell of kin who helped Augustus rise against the founder, Embraced before 1444, and so perhaps of the Fourth or Fifth Generation. Accounts give anywhere from four to twelve of them.
Daedalean forces took Doissetep in 1448; the physical fortress fell and the main keep moved to a Horizon Realm.
The Second Mistridge Convocation in 1449 came under attack by Craftmasons and Artificers; the mystics won at heavy cost and helped build Horizon afterward.

items.x: French cannon break an English army; Normandy is French again.
Kentish rebels march on London against corrupt ministers.
The condottiere Francesco Sforza becomes Duke of Milan.
Mages of nine traditions build the Horizon realm; the Grand Convocation begins.
lk: Etherspace, the Deep Umbra and the Void

items.x: Gutenberg sets up his press with Fust's money in Mainz.

items.t: The voivodes and the Order of the Dragon
items.x: Kindred of the Carpathians watch the princes of the Dragon order fight the Turk and each other.
By one tradition five nations of the Haudenosaunee bury their weapons under a white pine about this time and form a league.
Pachacuti has a royal estate built on a ridge above the Urubamba.
Mehmed II becomes sultan for good and plans to take Constantinople.
A university is founded at Glasgow.
Bahlul Lodi takes the throne of Delhi.
Mehmed builds Rumeli Hisari on the Bosporus to close the strait.
Leonardo is born at Vinci near Florence.
The last emperor crowned in Rome by a pope.
The Ottomans take the city on 29 May; the last emperor dies on the walls, and the last Cainites who remember the Dream leave by sea or bargain with the new masters.
lk: The great schism and the Paladins

items.x: The French destroy the last English army in Gascony; the Hundred Years War ends.
The English king falls into a stupor for over a year.

The Ottomans take Constantinople on 29 May 1453. The last Cainites who still remember the Dream leave by sea, or stay and bargain with the new masters. Fits: Long after the Dream ends in 1204 on the approved cards.
items.ref: Real history (1453); the Cainites are a house reading.

items.x: Milan, Venice, Florence, Naples and the pope agree a balance of power in Italy.
The Prussian towns rise against the Teutonic Order and turn to Poland.
Frost and drought starve the Valley of Mexico for years; families sell themselves for maize.
The first great printed book is finished.

items.t: The Wars of the Roses begin
items.x: York and Lancaster fight at St Albans.
Corsairs make the Aegean islands unsafe as Byzantine power ends.
Gutenberg's Bible comes off the press in Mainz about 1455. The Order of Reason sees at once what books by the thousand will do to belief. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (about 1455); the mages are a house reading.

items.x: John Hunyadi breaks Mehmed II's siege of Belgrade; he dies of plague weeks later.
Pope Callixtus III orders church bells rung at noon to pray against the Turks.
Vlad III takes the Wallachian throne for the second time and rules by the stake.
Ships in Portuguese service find the empty islands of Cape Verde.
Stephen becomes Prince of Moldavia and rules for 47 years.
Ota Dokan builds a castle at Edo, the future Tokyo.
The Czech diet elects the Hussite George of Podebrady king.
Hunyadi's son Matthias is elected King of Hungary.
The Ottomans take Smederevo; Serbia is a province.
Vlad has merchants of Brasov impaled; the Tzimisce of the Carpathians wonder what they have made.
Henry VI is captured by the Yorkists.
Richard of York is killed; his head is set on York's gate in a paper crown.
The prince who sent the Portuguese down Africa's coast dies.
Catholic lords in Moravia fight George of Podebrady's Hussites.
The bloodiest battle on English soil; Edward IV takes the throne.
Mehmed II takes the last Byzantine state.
The spider king takes the French throne.
lk: France in the Age of Masks

items.x: Vlad attacks the Ottoman camp at night and leaves a field of impaled prisoners for the sultan to find.
Ivan the Great becomes Grand Prince of Moscow.
The Ottomans conquer Bosnia.
Venice and the Ottomans begin sixteen years of war.
Florence names Cosimo Father of the Fatherland.
Sunni Ali takes the throne of Songhai and builds a fleet of war canoes on the Niger.

items.t: The League of the Public Weal
items.x: French princes rebel against Louis XI.
Marsilio Ficino translates the Hermetic writings for Cosimo de' Medici; the Order of Hermes is delighted and alarmed.
The Council of Nine Mystic Traditions is founded.
lk: Etherspace, the Deep Umbra and the Void

items.x: The Teutonic Order gives western Prussia to Poland.
War between Hosokawa and Yamana burns Kyoto and starts a century of civil war.
Charles the Bold becomes Duke of Burgundy.
Charles the Bold sacks and burns Liege.
Albania's defender dies of malaria; the Ottomans take the country within a decade.
Songhai takes Timbuktu from the Tuareg, and many of its scholars are killed or flee.
Lorenzo the Magnificent leads Florence.
The heirs of Aragon and Castile marry in secret.
Catholic lords elect Matthias Corvinus King of Bohemia at Olomouc.
The founder of the Sikh faith is born.
The Ottomans take Venice's island of Negroponte.
Tupac Inca Yupanqui conquers the Chimu kingdom and carries its king to Cuzco.
The Tu'i Tonga keeps the sacred office and hands the daily rule to a brother, the first Tu'i Ha'atakalaua.
Edward IV kills the Lancastrian prince; Henry VI dies in the Tower days later.
The Hussite king dies; Vladislaus Jagiellon takes Bohemia.
Dai Viet conquers the Cham capital.
Ivan III marries the niece of the last Byzantine emperor; Moscow begins to call itself the third Rome.
Venetian envoys go to Uzun Hasan for help against the Ottomans.
Nicolaus Copernicus is born in Torun.
Mehmed II beats Uzun Hasan of the White Sheep Turkmens.
Isabella becomes Queen of Castile.
Ficino's circle at Careggi studies Plato and Hermes Trismegistus.
Caxton prints the first book in English, at Bruges.
The Ottomans take the Genoese colonies in the Crimea.
The Jews of Trent are tortured and killed after a child's death.
The Swiss beat Charles the Bold twice.
Caxton sets up the first press in England.
Vlad III is killed fighting the Ottomans; Kindred say the voivode did not stay dead.
Charles the Bold dies in the snow before Nancy; Burgundy breaks up.
The Burgundian heiress marries a Habsburg; the Netherlands pass to Austria.
Plotters kill Giuliano de' Medici in the cathedral; Lorenzo survives.
The pope allows Ferdinand and Isabella their own Inquisition; the first burnings come in 1481.
Ivan III ends the Novgorod republic.

The Spanish Inquisition is set up in 1478; Granada falls on 2 January 1492 and the Jews are expelled that year. Rafael de Corazon, a Toreador of the old Spanish wars, urges the elders to give up open ties to mortals and pass into shadow. Fits: Before the first Camarilla Conclave of 1486.
items.ref: Real history (1478, 1492); Rafael de Corazon from Children of the Inquisition p. 35; the timing is a house reading.

items.x: Matthias keeps Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia for his lifetime.
Venice makes peace with Mehmed II.

items.t: The Great Stand on the Ugra
items.x: Moscow and the Horde face each other across the Ugra; the Tatars ride away and the yoke ends.
The Ottomans take Otranto in Italy and kill hundreds who will not convert.
The Hospitallers beat off an Ottoman siege.
The conqueror dies; Bayezid II succeeds after a fight with his brother.
Six people are burned at Seville by the Spanish Inquisition.
Castile begins the ten-year conquest of Granada.
Botticelli paints the Birth of Venus about this time.
The Portuguese build a stone fort on the Gold Coast to trade for gold, and later for people.
Edward IV dies; his sons vanish in the Tower and Richard III takes the crown.
Martin Luther is born.
Tomas de Torquemada becomes Inquisitor General.
Diogo Cao anchors in the mouth of the Congo and sends envoys to the king.
Innocent VIII's bull against witchcraft in Germany gives Kramer and Sprenger the pope's backing.
Henry Tudor kills Richard III and takes the crown.
Matthias Corvinus captures Vienna and moves his court there.
A new and deadly fever kills thousands in London.
The Camarilla holds its first Conclave and proclaims the Masquerade.
lk: The Ventrue and the new trade

items.x: Kramer's Malleus Maleficarum is printed; hunters use it for two centuries.
Pico della Mirandola offers to debate nine hundred theses, many from the Kabbalah; the pope condemns thirteen.
lk: The great schism and the Paladins

items.x: Bartolomeu Dias leaves Lisbon with three ships to find the southern end of Africa.
Ahuitzotl rededicates the Great Temple with the sacrifice of thousands of captives over four days.
Bruges imprisons Maximilian of Austria.
Bartolomeu Dias rounds the southern tip of Africa in a storm.
Cyprus's Venetian queen hands the island to Venice.
Castile takes Baza after a long siege.
Matthias Corvinus dies; his library and his army scatter.
Anne of Brittany marries Charles VIII.
Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised as Joao the First of Kongo.
The last Muslim kingdom in Spain surrenders.
Spain's Jews are ordered to convert or leave; many go to the Ottomans, who welcome them.
Columbus reaches the Caribbean and claims it for Castile.
Lorenzo de' Medici dies; Savonarola's preaching grows.
Rodrigo Borgia becomes Alexander VI.
The Anarch Revolt ends; the anarchs who refuse form the Sabbat, and the Assamites are cursed.
lk: The Paths of Gold, Thorns and Screams
The Abbey of the Sacred Crown

items.x: The pope draws a line through the Atlantic between Spain and Portugal.
Seventeen ships bring settlers, horses, pigs and sickness to Hispaniola.
A general overthrows Sunni Ali's son and rules Songhai as Askia Muhammad, patron of the scholars of Timbuktu.

At the founding of the Sabbat the Malkavian seer Vasantasena, who had helped rally the clan behind the Camarilla, leaves it over its disbelief in the Antediluvians and leads a brood of anarchs into the new sect. Fits: The Convention of Thorns, 1493.
items.ref: Clanbook: Malkavian (Revised) p. 98; the year is a house reading.

items.x: The French march to Naples; the Italian Wars begin.
Spain and Portugal move the line west.
Syphilis breaks out among the armies at Naples and spreads across Europe.
The Diet of Worms bans private war in the Empire.

items.t: The new disease and the blood
items.x: Kindred learn quickly which mortals carry the French disease, and which feeding grounds to avoid.
Portugal orders the Jews out, then forces them to convert instead.
Bartholomew Columbus founds Santo Domingo, the oldest European city in the Americas still lived in.
Savonarola's followers burn mirrors, cards and paintings in Florence.
John Cabot sails from Bristol to North America.
Leonardo finishes the Last Supper in Milan.
The friar is hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria.
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut.

items.t: Vasco da Gama on the Swahili coast
items.x: The Portuguese fleet calls at Mozambique, Mombasa and Malindi, where it finds a pilot for India.
The Swiss win their freedom from the Empire in fact.
Louis XII takes Milan; Leonardo leaves the city.
The Ottoman fleet beats Venice.
Pedro Alvares Cabral lands in Brazil on the way to India.
The future emperor is born at Ghent.
Hong Kong's villages fish and farm while Canton grows into a great port.
lk: The sleeping dragons of Hong Kong

items.x: By tradition the chief Umi-a-Liloa unites the island of Hawaii about this time.
As land grows scarce the tribes of Aotearoa build terraced hill forts.
Ismail is crowned at Tabriz and makes Persia Shia.
Ismail is crowned shah at Tabriz in 1501 and makes Twelver Shia faith the law of Persia. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1501).

items.x: The Crimean Tatars destroy the last of the Golden Horde.
Frederick the Wise founds a university at Wittenberg.
Moctezuma Xocoyotzin becomes ruler of the Mexica at the height of their power.

items.t: The first enslaved Africans in the Americas
items.x: The new governor of Hispaniola brings enslaved Africans from Spain to the island.
The Borgia pope dies; Cesare Borgia's power collapses.
Leonardo begins the portrait of Lisa Gherardini.
The David is set up before the Palazzo Vecchio.
Babur, driven from Fergana, takes Kabul.
Francisco de Almeida becomes first viceroy of Portuguese India.
Ivan III dies having tripled the lands of Moscow.
A Portuguese fleet takes Kilwa and burns Mombasa.
Julius II lays the first stone of the new St. Peter's.
Mobs kill hundreds of converted Jews in Lisbon.
Waldseemuller's map names the new lands America.
The abbot Trithemius warns of a vagabond calling himself Faustus.
The pope, France and the emperor ally against Venice.
Michelangelo begins painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
Henry VIII becomes King of England.
The Portuguese destroy a Mamluk and Gujarati fleet.
An earthquake wrecks Constantinople.
The French crush Venice's army.
Afonso the First wins the throne of Kongo and makes it a Christian kingdom with its own bishop and schools.
Afonso de Albuquerque takes Goa.
Cornelius Agrippa drafts the Three Books of Occult Philosophy.
A young envoy from Fez visits Timbuktu about this year and later writes that books sell there for more than any other goods.
Albuquerque takes Malacca and its spice trade.
A Dominican friar tells the settlers of Hispaniola from the pulpit that they are in mortal sin for their cruelty to the Taino.
The French win and lose their general Gaston de Foix.
Selim I takes the Ottoman throne.
James IV of Scotland is killed with much of his nobility.
Machiavelli writes The Prince in exile.
Balboa crosses the isthmus of Panama and wades into the South Sea to claim it for Castile.
Ottoman guns break Shah Ismail's army.
A crusade turns into a peasant war in Hungary; Gyorgy Dozsa is burned on an iron throne.
The Unity of Brethren grow in Moravia despite the king's ban.
Francis I beats the Swiss and takes Milan.
The Habsburgs and Jagiellons agree marriages that will bring Bohemia and Hungary to Austria.
The Unity of Brethren keep their faith in Moravia; inquirers from Prague find them hard to catch.
Selim destroys the Mamluk army in Syria.
Thomas More publishes Utopia.
Charles of Habsburg inherits Spain.
Selim ends the Mamluk state; Mukhtar Bey spreads influence beyond Egypt under the new rulers.
Luther publishes the theses against indulgences.
The last Lodi sultan takes Delhi.

Selim I takes Cairo in January 1517 and ends the Mamluk state. Mukhtar Bey, who has held the city since 1406, spreads influence beyond Egypt under the new rulers. Fits: Follows Mukhtar Bey's claim of 1406.
items.ref: Real history (1517); Cairo by Night pp. 44, 74.

items.x: On 31 October 1517 Martin Luther posts the theses at Wittenberg. Western Christendom splits. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1517).

items.x: Hundreds dance in Strasbourg's streets for weeks; some die.
Charles of Spain is chosen emperor, ruling half of Europe.
Leonardo dies in France.
Magellan leaves Spain to sail round the world.
Hernan Cortes lands on the Gulf coast with some five hundred soldiers, marches inland and enters Tenochtitlan as a guest.
Christian II of Denmark executes Swedish nobles after his coronation.
Suleiman becomes sultan.

items.pl: Field of the Cloth of Gold
items.t: The Field of the Cloth of Gold
items.x: Henry VIII and Francis I meet in tents of gold near Calais.
The painter dies in Rome; Toreador of the city call it a loss to the blood itself.

items.t: Smallpox and the Night of Sorrows
items.x: The Mexica drive the Spaniards out with great loss, and smallpox then kills a large part of the city.
Luther refuses to recant and is outlawed.
Suleiman takes Belgrade.
Magellan dies fighting on Mactan in the Philippines.
After a siege of three months Cortes and his Tlaxcalan allies take the ruined city.
The house reading has the plagues and the siege fill the lands of the dead beyond anything their keepers can bear; the wraiths' books tell of a Dark Kingdom of the Americas broken in these years.
After ninety-nine days on the Pacific the fleet reaches Guam; a quarrel over a boat ends with houses burned.
The last ship of Magellan's fleet comes home.
The Hospitallers surrender Rhodes after six months.
Lutheran preachers reach Bohemia and Moravia.
Gustav Vasa is elected King of Sweden; the Kalmar Union ends.
Zurich adopts Zwingli's reform.
Peasants rise across southern Germany.
The princes crush Thomas Muntzer's peasants.
Charles V's army captures Francis I.
The grand master of the Teutonic Order becomes Duke of Prussia.
Babur founds the Mughal empire.
Suleiman destroys the Hungarian army; King Louis II drowns fleeing.
Ferdinand of Habsburg is elected King of Bohemia.
The king of Kongo writes to the king of Portugal that slave traders are carrying off even nobles and asks that the trade be stopped.
Jorge de Meneses winters on the north-west coast of New Guinea.
Imperial troops sack Rome for weeks; the pope is besieged in Castel Sant'Angelo.
Paracelsus burns Avicenna's canon at Basel and lectures in German.
The Inca emperor dies of a sickness that runs ahead of the Spaniards, and two sons fight over the empire.
Anabaptist communities settle in southern Moravia.
Augustus Giovanni's clan comes to its arrangement with the Camarilla.
Suleiman besieges Vienna and fails.
Luther and Zwingli fail to agree.
The imam Ahmad of Adal breaks the Ethiopian army with Ottoman firearms and overruns the highlands.
The Lutherans set out their faith.
Charles V gives Malta to the Hospitallers.
Babur dies; Humayun takes the throne.
Paracelsus's chemistry splits the alchemists: some go to the Hermetics, some to the Order of Reason.
Zwingli is killed in battle.
An earthquake damages Lisbon.
Ferdinand I rebuilds Prague castle in the new style.
By the church's account a Nahua convert sees the Virgin on the hill of Tepeyac outside Mexico City.
Suleiman's second march on Vienna stalls at Koszeg.
Pizarro seizes the Inca Atahualpa in the square of Cajamarca and kills thousands of the escort.
Henry VIII breaks with Rome to marry Anne Boleyn.
Atahualpa fills a room with gold for a ransom and is strangled anyway; the Spaniards take Cuzco.
Anabaptists seize Munster and proclaim the kingdom of God.
Ignatius of Loyola and companions take vows at Montmartre.
Suleiman takes Baghdad from Persia.
The bishop's army retakes Munster; the leaders' bodies are hung in cages on the church tower.
Charles V takes Tunis from Barbarossa.
More is beheaded for refusing to accept Henry as head of the Church.

items.t: Kindred in the kingdom of God
items.x: Kindred in Munster find the prophets' kingdom an easy place to hunt and a hard one to hide in.
Pizarro founds the City of the Kings near the coast.
Jacques Cartier sails up the river to the Iroquoian town of Hochelaga, where Montreal will stand.
Anne Boleyn dies in the Tower on 19 May; the Restless say the queen serves the Quiet Lord as an Anacreon of southern England.
Henry VIII begins closing England's monasteries.
John Calvin publishes the Institutes of the Christian Religion.
Anne Boleyn is beheaded in the Tower on 19 May 1536. The living say the queen haunts it; the Restless say the queen serves the Quiet Lord as an Anacreon of southern England. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1536); Love Beyond Death p. 68 (the Restless' account).

items.x: The north rises against the closing of the monasteries.
Barbarossa beats the Holy League's fleet.
The pope approves the Society of Jesus.
Sher Shah Suri drives Humayun out of India.
Coronado marches from Mexico to the Zuni towns and the plains in search of golden cities and finds none.
Suleiman takes Buda; Hungary is split three ways.
Paul III sets up the Holy Office in Rome.
A great fire burns Prague's Lesser Town and castle.
Charles V forbids the enslaving of the native peoples of the Indies; the settlers resist.
De revolutionibus puts the sun at the centre; its author dies that year.
Vesalius publishes the Fabric of the Human Body.
Portuguese traders bring arquebuses to Japan.
Ethiopian and Portuguese musketeers kill Ahmad Gran, and the invasion collapses.
The Catholic Church meets to answer the reformers.
A silver mountain found in Peru sends its silver through Seville; prices across Europe begin to climb.
Sher Shah Suri dies in a gunpowder explosion.
A bleeding fever kills perhaps most of the native people of highland Mexico in three years.
Silver is found at Potosi, and within a generation a city larger than Paris stands at four thousand metres.
Luther dies where he was born.
Charles V crushes the Protestant princes.
Ivan IV is crowned the first tsar of Russia.
Ferdinand crushes a revolt of Bohemian towns and nobles.
The Jesuit Francis Xavier lands in Japan.
The Portuguese crown founds Salvador as the capital of Brazil.
Las Casas and Sepulveda argue whether the native peoples of America may be enslaved.
The Black Hand sets its ranks and marks.
lk: The Ventrue and the new trade

items.x: The Mongol Altan Khan burns the suburbs of Beijing.
The Ottomans take Tripoli from the Knights of Malta.
Ivan IV takes the khanate of Kazan.
Mary I takes the throne and restores the old Church.
Calvin's Geneva burns Michael Servetus.
Each prince of the Empire chooses the faith of his land.
Bishops Latimer and Ridley are burned at Oxford.
Humayun takes back Delhi.
The deadliest earthquake recorded kills perhaps 830,000 in China.
The young Akbar's army wins northern India.
Charles V gives up his crowns; Philip II takes Spain and the Netherlands.
Antwerp printers flood Europe with books; the Order of Reason backs the printers of almanacs.
France takes Calais, England's last French town.
Elizabeth becomes Queen of England.
Ivan IV invades Livonia.
The Italian Wars end.

items.t: Henry II killed at a joust
items.x: A lance splinter kills the French king.
Huguenot plotters try to seize the young king.
Oda Nobunaga destroys a much larger army.

items.t: The Toreador and the wars of religion
items.x: The Grand Court's Kindred back Catholic and Huguenot nobles as it suits them.
lk: France in the Age of Masks

items.x: Philip II moves the court to Madrid.
Soldiers kill Huguenots at worship; the French Wars of Religion begin.
Friar Diego de Landa burns the Maya books and images of Yucatan.
John Hawkins carries captives from the Guinea coast to Hispaniola, the first English slaving voyage.
The council closes, having reshaped the Catholic Church.
Galileo Galilei is born at Pisa.
William Shakespeare is born.
John Dee publishes the Hieroglyphic Monad; the Hermetic houses of England court him.
The Knights hold Malta against the Ottomans.
The Deccan sultans destroy Vijayanagara.
Spain begins its rule of the Philippines.
The Spanish found Saint Augustine in Florida and kill the French Protestants settled nearby.
A ship finds the way back east across the Pacific, and for two and a half centuries a galleon carries silver to Manila and silk to Acapulco.
Calvinists strip the churches of the Netherlands of images.
Suleiman dies during the siege; Zrinyi's defenders die in a last sally.
The Duke of Alba arrives to crush the Netherlands.
William of Orange leads the Dutch revolt.
Invaders from the east sack the capital of Kongo, and the king regains it only with Portuguese guns.
A Spanish fleet from Peru finds the Solomon Islands and names them for the gold it hopes is there.
Poland and Lithuania become one commonwealth.
Mercator publishes his world map.
Akbar builds a new capital near Agra.
Ivan IV's men kill thousands in Novgorod.
The Ottomans invade Venetian Cyprus.
Tribunals of the Holy Office are set up in Lima and then in Mexico City.
Famagusta falls; its commander is flayed alive.
The Holy League destroys the Ottoman fleet.
The Crimean khan burns Moscow.
Nagasaki is opened to Portuguese trade.
Idris Alooma becomes ruler of Bornu about this year and arms his horsemen with Turkish muskets.
Thousands of Huguenots are killed in Paris and the provinces.
Russia destroys a Crimean army south of Moscow.
Tycho Brahe sees a new star in Cassiopeia.
The Spaniards take the mountain refuge of Vilcabamba and behead Tupac Amaru in the square of Cuzco.
Nobunaga drives out the last Ashikaga shogun.
The Dutch flood their own land to lift the Spanish siege.
Nobunaga's musketeers destroy the Takeda cavalry.
Akbar invites scholars of every faith to debate at his court.
Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda, which will send more captives across the Atlantic than any other port.
Unpaid Spanish troops sack Antwerp.
Rudolf II becomes emperor.
Tycho Brahe builds an observatory on Hven; the Order of Reason funds measurements, the Hermetics read omens in them.
The bleeding fever returns to New Spain and kills about two million.
Francis Drake leaves on his voyage round the world.

items.t: The Battle of the Three Kings
items.x: King Sebastian of Portugal vanishes in a disaster in Morocco.
The northern Dutch provinces bind together.
Akbar claims the right to judge disputes of Islamic law.
Philip II becomes King of Portugal.
Rudolf's alchemists and astrologers draw Tremere and Toreador to Prague.
The Dutch renounce Philip II.
Ten days are dropped from October in Catholic lands.
Nobunaga is betrayed and dies in the burning temple.
Rudolf II makes Prague the imperial capital.
John Dee and Edward Kelley come to Bohemia to speak with angels.
The leader of the Dutch revolt is murdered.
Ivan IV dies over a chessboard.
Parma takes Antwerp; trade moves to Amsterdam.
English settlers land on Roanoke Island off the Carolina coast.
Toyotomi Hideyoshi becomes chancellor of Japan.
Elizabeth signs her cousin's death warrant.
Abbas the Great takes the Persian throne.
Hundreds are burned in the Trier trials over a decade.
The Spanish fleet is beaten off and wrecked by storms.
A friar stabs the French king; Henry of Navarre is heir.
A judge who doubted the witch trials is himself burned at Trier.
Hideyoshi takes Odawara; all Japan is his.
The tale of the rabbi who made a man of clay runs through the crown lands; mages argue whether it is a story or a working.
A relief ship finds the settlement of Roanoke empty and the word CROATOAN cut into a post.
The house reading follows the Garou's own story: in these years the Croatan tribe gives itself whole to bind a great Wyrm spirit, and the Pure Ones are two tribes where there were three.
Rudolf fills his rooms with clocks, stones, paintings and marvels.
A Moroccan army with firearms crosses the Sahara and destroys Songhai at Tondibi.
Hideyoshi's army lands at Busan.
Admiral Yi Sun-sin's turtle ships destroy a Japanese fleet.
Henry IV becomes Catholic.
The Long Turkish War begins.
The Portuguese build Fort Jesus to hold Mombasa.
Hugh O'Neill rises against English rule.
The Moroccans carry the scholar Ahmad Baba and his library from Timbuktu to Marrakesh.
Michael the Brave beats the Ottomans.
A witch judge of Lorraine publishes his book on demons, boasting of hundreds burned.
The Spaniards reach the Marquesas, kill about two hundred islanders and fail to found a colony at Santa Cruz.
The Ottomans win a great battle in Hungary.
Twenty-six Christians are crucified at Nagasaki.
James VI of Scotland writes against witches.
Admiral Yi dies winning the last sea battle; Japan leaves Korea.
Henry IV grants the Huguenots toleration.
Shah Abbas makes Isfahan his capital.
Tsar Fyodor dies; Boris Godunov is chosen tsar.
Shah Abbas makes Isfahan the capital in 1598. Batini schools gather in the new city. Fits: The Batini train Qutbs in Isfahan in 1979 on the approved cards.
items.ref: Real history (1598); the Batini are a house reading.

items.x: Shakespeare's company builds the Globe.
Tycho Brahe becomes imperial mathematician to Rudolf.
The Roman Inquisition burns Bruno in the Campo de' Fiori.
Tokugawa Ieyasu wins Japan.
Elizabeth charters the English East India Company.
The worst storm yet cuts Stygia off.
lk: The Ventrue and the new trade

items.x: Johannes Kepler comes to Prague to work with Tycho Brahe.
A volcano in southern Peru explodes; the ash darkens the sky, and the next years bring cold summers and famine as far as Russia.

appr.x: George of Podebrady is elected King of Bohemia on 2 March 1458. Rome calls him a heretic, and the Catholic lords of Moravia turn to Hungary.
Matthias Corvinus is chosen king in Olomouc in 1469 and holds Moravia until the Peace of Olomouc in 1479. Hungarian soldiers are quartered in the towns.
After the Convention of Thorns most Tzimisce join the Sabbat. Some in Moravia refuse both sects and keep the old ways, hidden by the families who have always fed and sheltered them.
After Mohacs, Ferdinand of Habsburg is chosen King of Bohemia in 1526. Vienna is now the crown's seat, and the march looks south.
