Anabaptist communities settle in southern Moravia under the protection of local lords, living in shared households. They stay until they are driven out in 1622.

appr.t: The caern and the deep shafts
appr.x: New shafts below the Adit cut into ground the hill sept guards. The Garou drive the miners out twice; the third time they lose the caern's outer stone.
Emperor Rudolf II moves the court to Prague in 1583. Alchemists, astrologers and astronomers gather there, and both the Traditions and the Order of Reason send people to court.
The tale of the rabbi of Prague who made a man of clay is told across the crown lands. Mages argue whether it is a story or a working.
The Third Great Maelstrom batters Stygia. The Moravian citadel is cut off but stands, and its legion rules the eastern Shadowlands alone for a time.
After the defeat of the Craftmasons in the Battle of Flames in 1450, the Primi of the Traditions resolved to build a Realm far from Earth as their meeting place.
Tezghul the Insane and Lithuanian demon-worshippers ravaged the Baltic from Kupala Alka from 1450 to 1453, and in 1452 the Daedaleans swore an Oath of Fire against vampires and magi.
At a minor Tribunal in the Gediz Caves in 1452 the Nodes, still called the Columns of Power, were formally dedicated; among them were Stonehenge and Glastonbury Tor.
Founded in 1456, the cult recruits no one openly and works to keep other Kindred weak and misled before Gehenna.

appr.t: France in the Age of Masks
appr.x: Louis XI takes the throne in 1461 and drags France into plots and near revolt; Charles VIII invades Italy to claim Naples, starting some 50 years of war that wins nothing lasting.
After nine years of talks the mystic mages found the Council of Nine Traditions against the Order of Reason.
A Nosferatu antitribu of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1467 by Boronisk, once an officer in the army of Ivan the Great.
The sect holds its first Conclave and names its first Justicars.
The Anarch Revolt ends at Thorns. The anarchs who refuse the treaty go on to found the Sabbat; the Assamites are cursed.

Jamal, a warrior, held the Black Throne from 1494 to 1998. Ur-Shulgi says Jamal refused to renounce Allah and was destroyed for it; many schismatics call Jamal a martyr. Ur-Shulgi does not take the title, giving it to Haqim alone.
For about 1500 years Hong Kong was a backwater ruled from Canton, its villages farming and fishing while Canton grew into a great trading city.
Voragg has served the Wyrm for centuries, mostly while bound in a rock deep under the Rocky Mountains, where a Wendigo tribe sealed it after it troubled them in the late 1500s.

By 1519 more than forty conquered provinces paid tribute to the emperor, who would soon need a Flower War, a battle fought only to take captives for sacrifice, if no new states could be found to conquer.
Within decades other clans called the Necromancers Devil Kindred. To avoid a united front against them, the Giovanni swore in 1528 to stay forever outside Kindred affairs.
It was founded in the 1530s, in the wake of the Reformation, by the French Toreador Louvel Tarneau.
The crescent tattoo of the Hand has been in use since at least about 1550.
Founded in 1550, it believes a single Book of Nod stanza about the last daughter of Eve is the key: control or destroy that daughter and Gehenna is averted.
During the witch-hunts of the 1560s refugees flooded Horizon, and Doissetep, once called its sister Chantry, broke with it over a failed plan for European universities.

appr.t: France in the Age of Masks
appr.x: Catherine di Medici rules as regent for the young kings from 1560 to 1589, and the strife between Catholic nobles and Huguenots peaks in the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572.
The last mortal record of one is a Warsaw church entry from 1587. Survivors now lurk in rural Chantries and unsettled Realms, where they plague mages in their sanctuaries.

appr.t: The Croatan give themselves at Roanoke
appr.x: The whole tribe dies to stop a great servant of the Wyrm. No living Croatan remains.
After the Looting, the Breaking of the Guilds and the Flaying of Obsidian, the worst storm yet cuts Stygia off. The Shroud thickens.
Polonia is of the 7th generation, Embraced in 1600 by Anton de Concepcion.
Archons, the justicars' agents, are usually picked from promising ancillae and young elders. They existed long before the title, which came into use in the late 1600s, probably from the Brujah.

By the middle of the 1600s, tales of torture and of children shaped into living mounds of bone and flesh reached Camarilla ears in France. The Toreador investigated, found signs of unsanctioned emigration, and put pawns in key posts to take hold of the colony.
Once Father Raymond, a convert born in the West Indies, recruited from a Norman monastery for Pierre de l'Ancre's witch hunts in Labourd in the early 1600s.

items.x: Tycho Brahe dies in Prague; Kepler inherits his observations.
The English break the Irish and Spanish at Kinsale.
Three years of failed harvests kill perhaps a third of Russia.
The VOC is founded and sells shares to the public.
James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England.
Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun and rules from Edo.
Izumo no Okuni performs the first kabuki in Kyoto.
The alchemists' lane of Prague castle hides more than mortal adepts; the Tremere keep a close eye on Rudolf's circle.
Guy Fawkes is caught under Parliament with barrels of powder.
A pretender claiming to be Ivan's son takes Moscow.
Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quixote.
Akbar dies at Agra after nearly fifty years; his son Jahangir takes the Mughal throne.
The Long Turkish War ends at Zsitvatorok; the emperor stops paying tribute and the border in Hungary holds.
Willem Janszoon of the Dutch company charts the west of Cape York, and Torres sails the strait to its north the same year.
The Spanish navigator Quiros lands in Vanuatu and believes that the great southern continent has been found.
The Gaelic lords of Ulster flee to the continent.
English settlers build a fort on the James River; most die of hunger and fever within three years.
A spectacle-maker asks for a patent on a looking glass that sees far.
Samuel de Champlain builds a trading post where the Saint Lawrence narrows.
Rudolf II grants the Bohemian estates freedom of worship, a promise the Habsburgs will break within twenty years.
Kepler publishes the New Astronomy in Prague, showing that Mars moves in an ellipse.
Spain begins expelling the Moriscos, some three hundred thousand descendants of its Muslims, over five years.
Ravaillac stabs the French king in his carriage.
A Polish army takes Moscow and a Polish prince is offered the Russian throne in the Time of Troubles.
Galileo publishes the moons of Jupiter; the Order of Reason calls it proof, the Celestial Chorus a trespass.
The Spanish make Santa Fe the capital of New Mexico, among the Pueblo towns.
Galileo publishes the moons of Jupiter in March 1610. The Order of Reason calls it proof; the Celestial Chorus calls it a trespass. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1610); the mages are a house reading.

items.x: The authorised English Bible is printed, and its language shapes English for centuries.
Matthias forces his brother Rudolf to give up the Bohemian crown; Rudolf is left with his collections in the castle.
Rudolf II dies in Prague; his court of alchemists and artists scatters and his treasures begin to drift away.
A Russian militia drives the Poles out of Moscow.
Ten people are hanged as witches at Lancaster.
The assembly of the land chooses sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov as tsar, ending the Time of Troubles.
A cannon shot during Henry VIII sets the Globe alight.
The shogun orders all missionaries out of Japan and the churches pulled down; Japanese Christians go into hiding.
The French Estates meet for the last time until 1789.
The Tokugawa storm Osaka castle and destroy the Toyotomi family; Japan has one master.
Shakespeare and Cervantes die in the same spring.
The Church puts Copernicus's book on the Index until it is corrected, and warns Galileo not to teach it as truth.
Nurhaci proclaims the Later Jin, the start of the Qing.

items.t: The great dying on the coast
items.x: A sickness brought by ships empties the Wampanoag and Massachusett villages of the New England coast in three years.
Dirk Hartog lands on the west coast of Australia and nails an inscribed pewter plate to a post.
The emperor's regents are thrown from a window of Prague castle; the Thirty Years War begins.
The Bohemian estates raise an army, take over the government and send envoys to every Protestant prince.

items.t: The Kindred and the long war
items.x: The Thirty Years War opens; princes of the Camarilla and Sabbat both fatten on the armies.
The Bohemians choose Frederick of the Palatinate as king.
The Dutch take Jakarta and name it Batavia.

items.t: Africans and an assembly in Virginia
items.x: A privateer sells some twenty captive Angolans at Point Comfort in the same summer that Virginia's first assembly meets.
The Bohemian army is routed outside Prague in an hour; the Winter King flees and Bohemia's independence ends for three centuries.
English separatists sail on the Mayflower for America to worship as they choose.
Separatists from the Mayflower settle in an emptied Wampanoag village.
Twenty-seven leaders of the revolt are executed in Prague.
The war between Spain and the Dutch resumes.
The Hutterite communities are driven out of Moravia; many go to Hungary and Transylvania.
The Dutch torture and kill English traders on Ambon.
Shah Abbas takes Baghdad from the Ottomans and holds it fifteen years.
Cardinal Richelieu becomes chief minister of France and sets about breaking the Huguenots and the Habsburgs.
Njinga takes the throne of Ndongo and fights the Portuguese for forty years, by turns as their ally and their enemy.
Charles I becomes king of England and soon quarrels with Parliament over money and religion.
Wallenstein beats Mansfeld's Protestant army at the Dessau bridge on the Elbe.
Packs of wolves, and worse, return to the empty villages of Germany; the Get of Fenris hunt the Wyrm's creatures in the ruins.
The Dutch West India Company builds a fort and a town at the tip of Manhattan.
Bohemia becomes Catholic by law; Protestants must convert or leave.
Richelieu besieges the Huguenot port; it starves into surrender.
The Renewed Land Ordinance comes to Moravia; Protestants must convert or leave, and many lords go into exile.
The teacher and bishop of the Unity of Brethren, Jan Amos Comenius, leaves for exile in Poland and never returns.
The emperor orders all church lands taken since 1552 given back; the Protestant princes are driven toward Sweden.
The prince-bishop of Bamberg burns hundreds as witches.
A Dutch ship is wrecked on reefs off western Australia, and mutineers murder more than a hundred of the survivors.
Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden lands in Pomerania and enters the war on the Protestant side.
Plague kills perhaps half of Milan; the city hunts for anointers said to spread it with ointment.
The Dutch take Pernambuco and its sugar mills and hold them for twenty-four years.
Tilly's army storms Magdeburg; twenty thousand die in the sack and fire, and the city is a byword for horror.
Gustavus Adolphus destroys Tilly's army at Breitenfeld and the road into southern Germany is open.
Shah Jahan's wife dies; he begins the Taj Mahal.
Vesuvius erupts after centuries of quiet and kills several thousand people around Naples.
The twenty thousand dead of Magdeburg cross in a night; the Hierarchy names the place a Haunt.
Gustavus Adolphus dies leading a cavalry charge in the fog at Lutzen, though the Swedes win the field.
Galileo publishes his Dialogue on the two world systems.
Emperor Fasilides restores the Ethiopian church and drives out the Catholic mission.
The Roman Inquisition forces Galileo to recant his teaching that the earth moves; he spends his last years under house arrest.
The emperor's general Wallenstein, suspected of treason, is killed by his own officers at Cheb.
The Swedes and their allies are destroyed at Nordlingen; France prepares to enter the war openly.
The emperor makes peace with Saxony and most Lutheran princes; the war goes on, now a contest of France and the Habsburgs.
Richelieu founds the Academie francaise to guard the French language.
Hong Taiji renames his Later Jin state the Great Qing and his people the Manchu.
The colony of Massachusetts Bay founds a college to train ministers.
Fasilides founds a capital at Gondar and builds a stone castle there.
Descartes publishes the Discourse on Method: I think, therefore I am.
The price of tulip bulbs in Holland collapses overnight, ruining speculators.
Christian peasants of Shimabara and Amakusa rise against taxes and persecution in Kyushu.
Colonists and their Narragansett and Mohegan allies burn a Pequot fort at Mystic with several hundred people inside.
Sultan Murad IV takes Baghdad back from Persia and kills much of its garrison.
The Shimabara rebels are killed to the last.
Japan expels the Portuguese and closes its ports.
The Ottomans and Persia sign the Treaty of Zuhab, fixing a border that lasts nearly to modern times.
Portugal rises, crowns the Duke of Braganza and breaks from sixty years of Spanish rule.
The reapers of Catalonia kill the viceroy and rise against Madrid; the war lasts twelve years.
Irish Catholics rise against English and Scottish settlers; thousands die and the tales grow in the telling.
King and Parliament raise armies and fight at Edgehill; the English Civil War has begun.
Swedish troops take Olomouc and hold it as their base in Moravia until 1650.
Richelieu dies; Cardinal Mazarin takes his place at the young king's side.
French missionaries found a settlement on the island of Montreal.
Abel Tasman sights Tasmania and then Aotearoa, where Maori canoes kill four of the crew.
The French destroy the famed Spanish infantry at Rocroi.
The four-year-old Louis XIV becomes king of France, with his mother and Mazarin to rule for him.
Li Zicheng takes Beijing; the last Ming emperor hangs himself.
Wu Sangui opens the pass; the Manchus take China.
Cromwell's cavalry win the north for Parliament at Marston Moor.
Rebels take Beijing in 1644 and the last Ming emperor dies; the Manchu Qing take the city weeks later. The courts of the Middle Kingdom read the omens and wait. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1644); the courts are a house reading.

items.x: The Swedes besiege Brno for months and fail; the town is honoured for it ever after.
Parliament's New Model Army destroys the king's army.
Qing troops kill much of the population of Yangzhou in ten days after it resists them.
Matthew Hopkins hangs about a hundred people as witches in East Anglia.
The Ottomans invade Venetian Crete; the war lasts a generation.
The fisherman Masaniello leads Naples against Spanish taxes.
The Thirty Years War ends; the Dutch are free.
Swedish troops take Prague castle and loot Rudolf's collections.
The Cossacks rise against Poland; tens of thousands of Jews are killed.
Paris rises against Mazarin and the court flees the city; the Fronde lasts five years.
The mad Sultan Ibrahim is deposed and strangled; his seven-year-old son takes the throne.
The Peace of Westphalia settles the mortal borders; elders of both sects redraw their own.
Charles I is beheaded outside his own Banqueting House in Whitehall.
Cromwell's army storms Drogheda and kills the garrison and many townspeople.
Russia's law code binds peasants to the land.
The Haudenosaunee, armed with Dutch guns, break the Wendat towns already thinned by smallpox.
The Swedish garrison marches out of Olomouc after eight years, leaving a ruined town.
Thomas Hobbes publishes Leviathan: without a strong sovereign, life is nasty, brutish and short.
Cromwell beats Charles II, who escapes by hiding in an oak.
Patriarch Nikon's reforms of Russian worship split the church; the Old Believers refuse them.
England and the Dutch Republic go to war at sea over trade.
Jan van Riebeeck lands at Table Bay to grow food for the Dutch East India Company's ships.
The Taj Mahal is finished at Agra as Shah Jahan's tomb for his wife.
Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of England, Scotland and Ireland.
At Pereyaslav the Cossacks of Ukraine swear loyalty to the tsar.
Sweden invades Poland; the years of war that follow are remembered as the Deluge.
An English fleet takes Jamaica from Spain; freed and escaped Africans hold the mountains as the Maroons.
Plague kills perhaps half of Naples in a single summer.
Mehmed Koprulu becomes grand vizier and saves the empire.
Oliver Cromwell dies; his son cannot hold power.
Aurangzeb imprisons his father and takes the throne.
France and Spain make peace at the Pyrenees; Louis XIV will marry the Spanish infanta.
The French build a fort on an island in the mouth of the Senegal.
Charles II returns to London and the monarchy is restored.
The Royal Society is founded in London for the advancement of natural knowledge by experiment.
Mazarin dies and Louis XIV announces that he will rule without a chief minister.
The Kangxi emperor takes the Qing throne as a child; he will rule sixty-one years.
The Ming loyalist Koxinga drives the Dutch from Taiwan.
Ottoman Tatars raid Moravia and carry off thousands.
Imperial and French troops beat an Ottoman army at Szentgotthard.
The Dutch governor surrenders the town to an English fleet without a shot.
Plague kills perhaps a hundred thousand Londoners, a quarter of the city.
Prince Mithras's Kindred hunt among the dying while the court flees to Oxford.
A Portuguese army kills the king of Kongo in battle and carries his head to Luanda; the kingdom breaks into civil war.
London burns for four days; Kindred lose havens in the City, and some say a few of them lit the fire.
The messianic claimant Sabbatai Zevi converts to Islam before the sultan.

items.t: The Royal Society and the Order
items.x: The Order of Reason sends members into the new Royal Society.
London burns from 2 to 6 September 1666. Prince Mithras's Kindred lose havens in the City, and some say a few of them lit the fire. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1666); the Kindred are a house reading.

items.x: The Dutch sail up the Medway and burn the English fleet at its moorings.
Venice gives up Candia and Crete to the Ottomans after twenty-one years of siege.
The Cossack Stenka Razin leads a great revolt along the Volga before being captured and quartered in Moscow.
France invades the Dutch Republic; the Dutch open the dikes.
A mob in The Hague kills the Dutch leaders Johan and Cornelis de Witt and mutilates their bodies.
An English company with a royal charter takes over the forts of the Gold Coast and brands its captives with its initials.
Three southern generals rebel against the Kangxi emperor; the war lasts eight years.
The Great Elector of Brandenburg beats the Swedes at Fehrbellin.
Charles II founds the Royal Observatory at Greenwich.
Metacom of the Wampanoag leads the last great rising of New England's peoples; a dozen towns burn and the survivors are sold to the Caribbean.
Spinoza dies at The Hague; his Ethics is published after his death and shocks Europe.
Witch trials in northern Moravia begin; about a hundred people burn before 1696.
Plague kills tens of thousands in Vienna; the Plague Column on the Graben is vowed in thanks.
Bohemian peasants rise against forced labour after plague and are put down.
Fortune-tellers and poisoners at court are burned; the king's mistress is implicated.
The Pueblo towns rise on one day under Popé, kill the friars and drive the Spanish out of New Mexico for twelve years.
Louis XIV seizes the free city of Strasbourg in peacetime.
Louis XIV moves the court to Versailles, where the nobility can be watched.
Peter and his brother Ivan are crowned joint tsars.

items.t: La Salle at the river's mouth
items.x: La Salle reaches the Gulf by the Mississippi and claims the whole valley for France.
Jan Sobieski breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna.
The Ottoman siege brings Assamite and Setite agents to the walls; Vienna's Tremere hold their chantry.
The emperor, Poland and Venice ally against the Ottomans.
Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes; two hundred thousand Huguenots flee France.
Imperial troops take Buda back from the Ottomans after 145 years.
Newton publishes the laws of motion and gravity.
A Venetian shell ignites the Ottoman powder store in the Parthenon.
William of Orange lands in England; James II flees, and the crown passes without a war.
An English buccaneer careens a ship on the north-west coast of Australia and later writes a book about it.
The English Bill of Rights limits the crown and guarantees Parliament.
Russia and China fix their border at Nerchinsk, the first treaty between them.
William III beats James II at the Boyne in Ireland.
Tens of thousands of Serbs flee north into Habsburg Hungary as the Ottomans return.
The title of justicar comes into use in the Camarilla in the late 1600s.
An eclipse on 23 August is marked by Lasombra across Europe.
Nineteen people are hanged for witchcraft in Massachusetts on the word of afflicted girls.
The house reading has almost none of the accused hold any power; the hunters' and mages' books both treat Salem as a warning about fear, and each blames the other's kind.
An earthquake drops most of the pirate port of Jamaica into the harbour.
An earthquake destroys towns across eastern Sicily and kills about sixty thousand.
Gold is found in the hills behind Rio, and half a million people cross the ocean in the rush that follows.
The Rozvi ruler Changamire Dombo drives the Portuguese from the plateau south of the Zambezi.
The Bank of England is founded to lend money to the crown for war.
The last leader of the great settlement of escaped slaves in Brazil, Zumbi, is hunted down and killed.
Peter the Great takes the Ottoman fortress of Azov with his new fleet.
Prince Eugene of Savoy destroys an Ottoman army crossing the Tisza at Zenta.
Tsar Peter travels west in disguise and works in Dutch shipyards.
The Spanish take Tayasal on its lake in the Peten, the last independent Maya city.
Peter executes over a thousand rebel musketeers and hangs bodies outside his sister's window.
After a siege of nearly three years the Omanis take Fort Jesus, and the Swahili coast north of Mozambique passes from Portugal to Oman.
At Karlowitz the Ottomans give up Hungary and Transylvania; their retreat from Europe begins.
Charles XII of Sweden crushes a much larger Russian army at Narva in a snowstorm.
The last Spanish Habsburg dies, leaving Spain to a French prince and Europe to war.
The Elector of Brandenburg crowns himself King in Prussia at Konigsberg.
Osei Tutu defeats Denkyira at Feyiase, and the Asante union takes the Golden Stool as the seat of its soul.
Masterless samurai avenge their lord and are ordered to kill themselves.
Peter founds a city on the Neva marshes.
Francis II Rakoczi leads Hungary in a war of independence against the Habsburgs that lasts eight years.
Marlborough and Prince Eugene destroy a French and Bavarian army at Blenheim.
An English and Dutch fleet takes Gibraltar from Spain; Britain keeps it.
A young Kongo noblewoman who preached that Saint Anthony spoke through the dead and that Christ was Kongolese is burned as a heretic.
The Acts of Union join England and Scotland as Great Britain.
Aurangzeb dies after fifty years; Mughal power begins to break apart.
The last eruption of Fuji covers Edo in ash.
Peter destroys Charles XII's army at Poltava; Russia becomes the power of the north.
The coldest winter in five centuries kills crops and people.
The first European hard porcelain is made at Meissen.
The Ottomans trap Peter's army on the Pruth and make the tsar give back Azov.
Plague returns to Moravia; columns of thanks follow.
Enslaved Africans set fires and kill nine colonists; twenty-one are executed.
The Peace of Utrecht ends the War of the Spanish Succession.
Charles VI issues the Pragmatic Sanction so his daughter can inherit the Habsburg lands.
The Elector of Hanover becomes George I of Great Britain.
Louis XIV dies after seventy-two years on the throne.
A Jacobite rising in Scotland for James Stuart fails.
Prince Eugene destroys an Ottoman army at Petrovaradin.
Prince Eugene takes Belgrade from the Ottomans.
Four London lodges of Freemasons form the first Grand Lodge.

Peter the Great sends young Russians west to learn shipbuilding and statecraft. Alexis Danpai, of a family the tsar favours, is among them. Fits: The book has Alexis born at the start of the 18th century.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 56; the year is a house reading.

items.x: The French found a town in a bend of the Mississippi.
A naval party kills the pirate Edward Teach off the Carolina coast.
Plague brought by a merchant ship kills half of Marseille.
Shares in the South Sea Company collapse and ruin thousands in Britain.
Peter the Great takes the title of Emperor of All Russia.
Afghan rebels take Isfahan after a long siege and famine; the Safavid state collapses.
Jacob Roggeveen lands on Easter Day; the visit ends with a dozen islanders shot.
Peter the Great dies; his wife Catherine takes the throne.
An imperial official reports that a dead peasant of Kisiljevo in Serbia rose to drink the blood of his neighbours.
Fulani clerics found a Muslim state in the highlands of Guinea.
Jonathan Swift publishes Gulliver's Travels.
Isaac Newton dies and is buried in Westminster Abbey.
Newton's death leaves the Order of Reason without its greatest Sleeper ally; some of its members think Newton was more than a Sleeper.
King Agaja of Dahomey conquers Ouidah and takes the slave trade of the coast into the crown's hands.
An Austrian army surgeon's report on vampires in Serbia is printed across Europe; the Masquerade strains.
The Medvedja report is reprinted across Europe; learned men argue over vampires.
War breaks out over the Polish throne between Russia, Austria and France.
The Qianlong emperor takes the Qing throne; his reign is China's last great age.
Nader is crowned shah of Persia, ending the Safavid line.
The San Carlo opera house of Naples opens, the oldest working opera house in Europe.
Nader Shah sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.
The Ottomans take back Belgrade at the peace of 1739.
Enslaved Kongolese soldiers in South Carolina march for Spanish Florida under a banner and are cut down.
Frederick II of Prussia seizes Silesia from Austria; the War of the Austrian Succession begins.
Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands at twenty-three and must fight to hold them.
Frederick's Prussia rises; the Ventrue of Berlin grow with it.
French and Bavarian troops take Prague by night; the Elector of Bavaria is crowned King of Bohemia.
Prussian troops invade Moravia and besiege Brno and its Spilberk fortress, and fail.
Handel's Messiah is first performed in Dublin.
Charles Edward Stuart lands in Scotland and raises the clans.
The Jacobite army is destroyed at Culloden; the Highlands are broken.
Dom Augustin Calmet publishes his learned treatise on ghosts and vampires.
An earthquake wrecks Lima, and the wave that follows wipes out its port.
The peace of Aix-la-Chapelle leaves Silesia to Prussia.
Excavations begin at Pompeii, buried by Vesuvius in the year 79.
Diderot and d'Alembert begin the Encyclopedie.
Maria Theresa forbids the digging up and burning of corpses as vampires.
An earthquake, fire and sea wave destroy Lisbon.
Tens of thousands die in a morning; the Shadowlands of Lisbon shake with a small storm.
Frederick invades Saxony and the Seven Years War begins.
Austria beats Frederick at Kolin in Bohemia.
The East India Company wins Bengal at Plassey.
Frederick crushes the French at Rossbach and the Austrians at Leuthen within a month.
The East India Company wins at Plassey on 23 June 1757. The Order of Reason's merchants follow the Company into Bengal. Fits: Fits the Mage history from 1756 card.
items.ref: Real history (1757); the mages are a house reading.

items.x: Frederick besieges Olomouc and fails when his supply convoy is destroyed.
Russians and Austrians destroy Frederick's army at Kunersdorf.
A British army climbs the cliffs and takes Quebec; both generals die.
George III becomes king of Great Britain.
The Afghans destroy the Maratha army at the third battle of Panipat.
Catherine takes the throne; Peter III is killed.
Rousseau publishes The Social Contract: man is born free, and everywhere in chains.
The Peace of Paris gives Britain Canada and India's trade.
The peoples of the Great Lakes rise against the British forts, and the crown forbids settlement beyond the mountains.
Hargreaves's spinning jenny multiplies a spinner's work.
The Company beats the Mughal emperor at Buxar and takes the revenue of Bengal.
James Watt improves the steam engine with a separate condenser.
Spain expels the Jesuits from its empire, and the Guarani missions fall apart.
Samuel Wallis's ship is the first from Europe to reach Tahiti.
Catherine the Great goes to war with the Ottomans.
Famine kills perhaps ten million people in Bengal under Company rule.
Franciscans and soldiers found the first of twenty-one missions on the coast of Upper California.
A warlord has the Ethiopian emperor strangled, and for eighty years the emperors are puppets of regional lords.
James Cook observes the transit of Venus from Tahiti, then charts Aotearoa with the help of the Tahitian navigator Tupaia.
Russia burns the Ottoman fleet at Chesma.

items.t: The Order of Reason and the machines
items.x: The craftsmen's guilds of the Order of Reason back the new engines of Britain.
Cook lands at Botany Bay, sails north and claims the east of Australia for Britain.
Plague in Moscow kills tens of thousands and sets off a riot that kills the archbishop.
Russia, Prussia and Austria take a third of Poland's lands.
A Cossack claiming to be Peter III rises.
The pope dissolves the Jesuits under pressure from the Catholic kings.
Colonists dressed as Mohawks throw a cargo of East India tea into Boston harbour.
At Kuchuk Kainarji Russia wins the north shore of the Black Sea.
Louis XVI becomes king of France at nineteen.
Bohemian peasants march on Prague against forced labour.
Militia and British regulars exchange fire in Massachusetts.
Adam Weishaupt founds the Order of the Illuminati in Bavaria.
Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations.
The Bavarian Illuminati draw on Freemasonry; the Order of Reason watches a secret society it did not found.
Thirteen colonies declare themselves free of the British crown.
Austria and Prussia face each other in Bohemia without fighting a battle; the soldiers dig potatoes.
Cook's ships reach the Hawaiian islands in the season of the god Lono.
Dutch farmers and the Xhosa fight over cattle and pasture, the first of nine wars in a century.
Cook is killed on the beach at Kealakekua in a quarrel over a stolen boat.
Anti-Catholic mobs burn London for a week in the Gordon Riots.
A descendant of the Incas leads the greatest revolt Spain's empire has seen and is pulled apart by horses in Cuzco the next year.
Joseph II ends personal serfdom and grants toleration to Protestants.
Kant publishes the Critique of Pure Reason.
William Herschel finds a new planet, Uranus.
A British army surrenders to American and French forces in Virginia.
The Montgolfier brothers fly hot-air balloons in Paris.
The Laki eruption in Iceland poisons Europe's air through a hot summer and a hard winter.
Russia annexes the Crimean khanate.
Romanian peasants rise in Transylvania under Horea; Horea is broken on the wheel.
Bavaria bans the secret societies; the Illuminati break up.
Mozart's Marriage of Figaro is a triumph in Prague.
Mozart's Don Giovanni opens in Prague.
Delegates in Philadelphia write a federal constitution that counts an enslaved person as three fifths of a free one.
Poor black Londoners are settled on the coast of Sierra Leone; freed loyalists from Nova Scotia follow and found Freetown.
A great hailstorm destroys France's harvests and bread prices soar.
Eleven ships land more than seven hundred convicts at Sydney Cove on the country of the Eora.
Paris takes the Bastille on 14 July.
The Assembly declares the rights of man and of the citizen.
Brujah idealists back the Revolution; Toreador of the court flee or die.
Smallpox kills perhaps half of the Aboriginal people around the harbour.
Mutineers put Captain Bligh in an open boat; nine of them later hide on Pitcairn Island with Tahitian companions.
Joseph II dies, his reforms undone.
Louis XVI is caught fleeing Paris at Varennes.
Mozart dies in Vienna at thirty-five.
After a ceremony in the woods the enslaved of the northern plain of Saint-Domingue rise and burn the sugar estates.

items.t: The dead walk with the living
items.x: The house reading has the lwa and the dead of the plantations counted among the rebels by both sides; the island's Shadowlands stay restless for two centuries.
The French revolutionary army holds the Prussians at Valmy.
Mobs kill over a thousand prisoners in the Paris jails.
Louis XVI is guillotined on 21 January.
The Committee of Public Safety's Terror kills thousands.
Western France rises for king and Church and is crushed with mass killings.
In the Revolution the Brujah Critias Embraces Germaine.
In the Revolution the Brujah Critias Embraces Germaine; the Countess d'Adhemar, a Toreador childe of Madame Guil, is the lover Critias keeps. Fits: Fits the 1774 Germaine card.
items.ref: Dread Names, Red List p. 49; the year is a house reading inside the Revolution.

items.x: Robespierre falls and is guillotined.
Kosciuszko leads a Polish rising and is beaten.
Kindred use the Terror to settle debts; the guillotine kills a few ghouls.
Russia, Prussia and Austria divide what is left of Poland.
A British fleet takes the Cape from the Dutch to keep it from France.
Kamehameha's army drives the defenders of Oahu over the cliffs at Nuuanu.
Edward Jenner tries vaccination with cowpox.
Bonaparte conquers northern Italy.
A Scottish surgeon reaches the Niger at Segou and sees that it flows east.
Bonaparte ends the Venetian Republic after a thousand years.
The first party of the London Missionary Society lands at Tahiti.
Napoleon lands in Egypt and wins at the Pyramids.
Nelson destroys the French fleet at Aboukir Bay.
Ireland rises with French help and is crushed.
Napoleon's scholars dig in Egypt; the mummies watch strangers dig.
Napoleon lands in Egypt in July 1798 and wins at the Pyramids; his scholars find the Rosetta Stone in 1799. The mummies watch strangers dig. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1798, 1799); the mummies are a house reading.

items.x: French soldiers find the Rosetta Stone.
Bonaparte seizes power as First Consul.
Bonaparte beats Austria at Marengo.
Ireland joins Great Britain in the United Kingdom.
Tsar Paul I is murdered by officers; Alexander I becomes tsar.
France, having lost an army in Saint-Domingue, sells the Mississippi valley to the United States.
Napoleon crowns himself emperor in Notre-Dame.
Serbia rises against the Ottomans under Karadjordje.
Dessalines declares the independence of Haiti, the first state founded by people who freed themselves from slavery.
An army expedition sets out up the Missouri to find a way to the Pacific.

items.t: The jihad of Usman dan Fodio
items.x: A Fulani scholar raises the Hausa lands against their kings and founds the Sokoto caliphate.
Irish convicts rise near Sydney under the cry of death or liberty and are cut down.
Nelson dies winning at Trafalgar.
Napoleon wins near Brno; the dead flood the Moravian Shadowlands.
Francis II gives up the crown and the Holy Roman Empire ends.
Napoleon crushes Prussia at Jena and Auerstedt.
At Tilsit Napoleon and Alexander divide Europe between them.
Madrid rises against the French; the Peninsular War follows.
The Portuguese court, fleeing Napoleon, lands in Brazil and rules its empire from Rio.
Officers of the New South Wales Corps arrest Governor Bligh.
Napoleon beats Austria at Wagram.
Samuel Hahnemann publishes the method of homeopathy.
The priest Miguel Hidalgo rings the church bell and calls his parish to rise against Spanish rule.
The last independent island submits, and Kamehameha rules all Hawaii.
Three great earthquakes shake the Mississippi valley; the river runs backward and church bells ring in Boston.
An American army burns Prophetstown, the centre of Tecumseh's league of nations.
Borodino is the bloodiest day of the Napoleonic wars.
Napoleon enters Moscow and finds it burning.
The Grande Armee dies in the Russian snow; few cross the Berezina.
Half a million die in Russia; Stygia takes the dead of the retreat.
Napoleon is beaten at Leipzig in the Battle of the Nations.
The Congress of Vienna redraws Europe.
British troops burn the Capitol and the President's house.
Napoleon is beaten at Waterloo and sent to St Helena.
Tambora in the East Indies erupts, the greatest eruption in recorded history.
Kindred of Vienna host the Congress's diplomats and take their share.
In the year without a summer Mary Shelley conceives Frankenstein by a lake near Geneva.
Byron, the Shelleys and Polidori write ghost stories by a lake; Toreador take note of the Vampyre.
Shaka takes the Zulu chieftaincy and remakes its regiments; the wars and migrations that follow empty and remake southern Africa.
Cholera spreads from Bengal across Asia.
Mary Shelley's Frankenstein is published.
Northern Maori armed with muskets raid the length of Aotearoa; tens of thousands die or are enslaved in twenty years.
John Polidori publishes The Vampyre, the first modern vampire tale.
Cavalry charge a crowd demanding reform at Peterloo in Manchester.
Bolivar crosses the Andes and frees New Granada in one battle.
After Kamehameha's death the royal women eat with the young king in public, and the old religious law ends.
Greece rises against the Ottomans.
A royalist general changes sides, and the army of the Three Guarantees enters Mexico City.
The Ottomans kill or enslave tens of thousands on Chios.
Champollion reads the hieroglyphs.
Champollion reads the hieroglyphs; the mummies' names can be read again.
The Portuguese prince Pedro declares Brazil independent and is crowned its emperor.
Freed black Americans sent by a colonisation society land at Cape Mesurado.
Champollion reads the hieroglyphs in 1822. For the first time since antiquity, the living can read the mummies' names. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1822); the mummies are a house reading.

items.x: The United States warns Europe against new colonies in the Americas.
Lord Byron dies of fever at Missolonghi.
Sucre defeats the last Spanish army in South America.
The governor of the Gold Coast is killed fighting the Asante, and his skull is kept in Kumasi.
The Stockton and Darlington railway opens.
Officers rise in St Petersburg and are crushed.
A canal joins the Hudson to the Great Lakes and makes New York the port of a continent.
Sultan Mahmud II destroys the Janissaries.
The allied fleets sink the Ottoman fleet at Navarino.
Shaka's half-brothers stab him to death, and Dingane takes the kingship.
The queen of the Merina takes the throne, closes the island to Europeans and persecutes its Christians.
The Ottomans accept an independent Greece.
Paris overthrows Charles X in the July Revolution.
Poland rises against Russia.
Belgium breaks away from the Netherlands.

items.t: The Kindred of the July Revolution
items.x: Barricades go up in Paris; anarchs join the crowds.
Congress empowers the president to move the nations of the south-east beyond the Mississippi.
A French army lands and takes Algiers, the beginning of a hundred and thirty years of rule.
Two thousand settlers and soldiers sweep across Tasmania to drive its Aboriginal people into a peninsula; the survivors are later exiled to an island.
The house reading puts in these decades the first killings of the Bunyip by Garou who came with the settlers, the war that the tribes later mourn.
Cholera reaches Europe.
Cholera kills hundreds of thousands; the Shadowlands of Europe's cities fill.
An enslaved preacher leads a rising in Virginia; about sixty white people are killed, and far more black people in the reprisals.
The Reform Act widens Britain's vote.
Republicans rise in Paris during the cholera year.
Said of Oman moves the court to Zanzibar, plants cloves and makes it the market for the ivory and slaves of the interior.
Britain abolishes slavery in its empire.
Emperor Francis I dies; the simple-minded Ferdinand succeeds.
Muslim Africans, enslaved and free, rise in Bahia at the end of Ramadan.
Dutch-speaking farmers leave the British Cape with their wagons and servants for the interior.
A grazier from Tasmania claims to buy the land where Melbourne stands from Kulin elders; the governor voids the deal.
Northern Maori chiefs sign a declaration of the independence of New Zealand.
The woollen mills of Brno grow; it is called the Moravian Manchester.
Mexican troops storm a mission held by Texan rebels; six weeks later the rebels win at San Jacinto.
A colony without convicts is proclaimed at Adelaide.

appr.x: On 23 May 1618 the Bohemian estates throw the emperor's regents from a window of Prague Castle. The Thirty Years War begins.
The Bohemian estates lose at White Mountain on 8 November 1620. Protestant lords are executed in 1621, the Anabaptists are expelled in 1622, and the Renewed Land Ordinance follows (Moravia, 1628).
Swedish troops take Olomouc in June 1642 and hold it until 1650. Foragers reach the valley; the families hide their stores, their daughters and sons, and their Kindred.
The Swedes besiege Brno in 1645 and fail. The town is remembered for it for centuries.
From 1678 to 1696 witch trials in northern Moravia send about a hundred people to the fire. Kindred and fae keep very still while the inquisitor works.
Plague spreads from Vienna through the crown lands in 1679 and 1680. Plague columns go up in the squares afterwards.
Frederick of Prussia invades Moravia in 1742 and besieges Brno, and comes back against Olomouc in 1758. Each time the countryside pays.
Joseph II ends personal serfdom and grants toleration to Protestants in 1781, and soon after closes many monasteries. Peasants may now leave the land; some leave the valley.
Brno's cloth mills grow, and the Order of Reason takes an interest in Moravian manufacture. The valley's weavers feel it first in their prices.
On 2 December 1805 Napoleon beats the Austrian and Russian armies at Austerlitz (Slavkov), east of Brno. Thousands of the dead go into the Moravian Shadowlands in one day.
The Moravian citadel takes in the soldiers of Austerlitz and forms a new legion from them. The Hierarchy in the east is stronger for it.
A Nosferatu of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1614 by Stanford Warwick, who found Maryann burned yet alive in a tavern after a Ventrue purge of the sire's servants.
Jeremy MacNeil is a Brujah of the Eighth Generation, born in 1631 and Embraced in 1657.

During an eclipse on 23 August 1691, tendrils of shadow impaled Lasombra in their crypts, and three died. Goratrix and the Tremere antitribu later claimed to have destroyed Tezcatlipoca with a ritual using the black ichor from the wounds; they showed no proof, but Tezcatlipoca was never seen again.

Through the 1700s the Lasombra and Tzimisce fought a war of pawns inside the colonial Church, Lasombra backing Spanish-born priests and the Tzimisce stirring up creole ones, until armed priests clashed and the army stepped in.
Racism and sexism took hold in the Circle in the 1700s, demeaning its women and its non-European forebears, now called the Aesculapians.
Doran crossed to North America and in the early 1700s went south rather than north to Canada, settling in the Louisiana territory.
Ever since Spanish monks came early in the 1700s, Old World undead have ruled the New World's mortals by murder and deceit, hidden behind the Masquerade.
Cosa attacked Doran in 1713, and for years their mortal followers clashed. Cosa had Bienville removed from office and a servant of Cosa's own, Antoine Cadillac, made governor.
Life-extension work let leading Technocrats live for centuries; Reginald Proctor, extended in 1715, was the only one lost before the Anomaly, by suicide in 1914.
A Brujah of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1736 by Katherine Wiese, who released Edgardo early in the nineteenth century.
Early in a long war with the Brujah Simon de Cosa, Doran made the governor, Bienville, a ghoul. In 1743 Bienville broke free with a mage's help and returned to Europe.
Werewolves followed their Cajun kinfolk to the bayous after 1755 and fought the Uktena already there over a caern. In the end the vampires and the Uktena together pushed Cosa into the western swamps.
In 1756 more than a hundred Native American Dreamspeakers left Horizon over bias against tribal and shamanic magic.
Robin was a silversmith's apprentice in colonial America, Embraced in 1757 during the French and English war for the continent and then abandoned by the sire.
Idealist elders in Spain who hoped to settle in Louisiana had France cede the territory to Spain in 1763. Doran's servants lost their offices, and Cosa rose again and drove the Ventrue from the city.
A Ravnos of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1764 by Vasily Vasilevich, born to a noble family.
The Inner Circle founded the order at its 1764 gathering, when the Hellfire Clubs were in fashion; rumour credits Meerlinda with the name.
When Louis XVI took the throne in 1774, the Toreador of the French court backed the status quo against reform.
Gumagan live in the deserts, Arnhem Land, New Guinea and the Torres Strait Islands; none have been left in southern Australia since the war that began in 1788.
A Toreador of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1790 by Émeric de Sauveterre, at home on the Côte d'Azur among the very rich; Villon sees a former Anarch self in Laurette.
Luther Gazes-Inward, the first Stargazer in Australia, landed at Sydney Town in 1790, and the tribe hoped to learn from the Aboriginal peoples and the Bunyip, who would not speak with them.
They took the name of the first Genji, vampires who had driven out the Bishamon centuries before, and their power grew with Japan's rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
Its power grew through the 1800s as it infiltrated groups, among them the first mixed Tradition Chantries, and it became the Technocracy's internal police.
In the 1800s they joined others around the computer to become the Difference Engineers, finally finding a place in the Union.
A Turkish Cypriot born under Ottoman rule in the 1800s and among the best-known vampires of the modern era.

appr.t: Bone Gnawer Kin in Other Lines
appr.x: By the late 1800s the tribe had Kin among Irish and Scottish families, and descendants who earned glory were often taken in by the Fianna, so many Garou carry a Bone Gnawer ancestor they would rather hide.
The western Brujah are younger than most clans of the Camarilla; those Embraced in the 1800s barely know the old tragedies of their line.
Born a slave on a Georgia cotton plantation and taken into the house as manservant to Jackson Mills; Embraced in 1807 by Monica San Valentin, Ventrue of the 8th Generation.
Lasombra of the 5th Generation, Embraced in 1812 by one known as Mary; when one Esperanza Lucifer falls, a new one takes up the fearsome role.
The Seers of Chronos became the Sahajiya in 1825, then the Cultists of Bacchus, then the Cult of Ecstasy.
Don Sebastian was a Californio landowner who sheltered the survivors of the brig Danube, wrecked in San Pedro Bay on Christmas Day 1828.
It broke free some time in the 1830s, as caern after caern fell to the European Garou, and the Garou needed decades even to learn its name.
In the 1830s the Europeans’ seizure of too many Uktena and Wendigo caerns weakened the seals, and the Bane slipped out and began feeding again.
Babbage and Lovelace's work in 1834 gave rise to the Difference Engineers, who became the Virtual Adepts around 1880; the Natural Philosophers renamed themselves Electrodyne Engineers in 1866.
Princes cite the Nuremberg affair of 1836, when a Sabbat spy became seneschal and passed what was learned to the sect.

name: The Age of Steam and Shadow

items.x: Victoria becomes queen of Britain at eighteen and gives the coming age its name.
Cooke and Wheatstone patent an electric telegraph; within a generation news crosses a continent in minutes.
Salic law bars a queen in Hanover, so the crown passes to Ernest Augustus and the union with Britain ends.

items.t: The Ventrue and the new reign
items.x: London's Ventrue court marks the new queen as an omen of stability; the house reading puts Mithras's influence at its height.
Brunel's steamship crosses the Atlantic in fifteen days, and the sailing packets begin to lose the mails.
A British army marches on Kabul to put a friendly emir on the throne, beginning a war that ends in catastrophe.
The Emperor Ferdinand Northern Railway opens its branch to Brno, and the wool town is tied to Vienna by rail.
Soldiers march the Cherokee west at bayonet point; about a quarter die on the way.
A Boer wagon fort beats off Dingane's regiments on the Ncome.
China's commissioner Lin Zexu destroys British opium at Canton, and Britain sends gunboats to force the trade open.
The Rose Chamber edict promises Ottoman subjects of every faith security of life, honour and property.
Daguerre's photographic process is given to the world, and faces can be fixed on silvered plates.
The Rothschilds' Vitkovice ironworks and the new pits turn the Ostrava basin into the black country of the empire.
Britain's penny post starts with the first adhesive stamp, and letter writing becomes ordinary.
Photographers in London whisper about sitters who leave no image; the house reading makes the camera a quiet hunter's tool.
The sultan of Oman makes Zanzibar the seat of the realm.
Maori chiefs and the British crown sign a treaty whose two texts say different things.
British marines land on Hong Kong island, which China cedes the next year.
The northern line reaches Olomouc, and the fortress town begins to grow beyond its walls.
The British army leaving Kabul in winter is cut down in the passes; almost none of the sixteen thousand reach Jalalabad.
China opens five ports, pays an indemnity and gives up Hong Kong, the first of the unequal treaties.
A fire burns for four days and destroys a third of the old city.
A British army returns to Kabul, blows up its great bazaar and leaves again.
Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol, three spirits and a miser's change of heart.
Charles Napier defeats the emirs of Sindh at Miani and takes the province for the Company.
A young merchant of Shiraz declares the gate to a coming prophet, and the Babi movement spreads across Persia.
Starving handloom weavers in Silesia smash the houses of the merchants, and Prussian troops shoot them down.
Daniel O'Connell is jailed for conspiracy after the monster meetings for repeal of the union with Britain.
Blight rots Ireland's potato crop; over the next five years a million die and another million leave.
The house reading has Fianna caerns in the west cry out as the famine dead crowd the Shadowlands of Ireland.
Two Royal Navy ships seek the Northwest Passage and vanish; searches over decades find bones and tales of cannibalism.
Blight takes the Irish potato from 1845; a million die and a million leave. The Fianna lose Kinfolk to the ships. Fits: Fits the Bone Gnawer Kin card on Irish families.
items.ref: Real history (1845 to 1849); the Fianna are a house reading.

items.x: Peel ends the tariffs on grain and splits his party; cheap bread wins over the landlords.
A Polish noble rising in Galicia is turned when peasants kill hundreds of their lords, and Austria swallows Krakow.
Galle finds the planet Neptune where mathematics said it would be.
The Company fights the Sikh kingdom of the Punjab and takes its eastern lands.
The house reading has Silent Striders carry word west that the Company's wars have broken caerns along the Indus.
The United States goes to war with Mexico over Texas and takes half its territory in two years.
The Bronte sisters publish Jane Eyre, Wuthering Heights and Agnes Grey within months.
Semmelweis shows that doctors washing their hands save mothers, and the profession mocks the idea.
The emir of Algeria surrenders to France after fifteen years of war.
The settlers of Liberia declare a republic.
Paris overthrows Louis Philippe and declares a republic; revolution spreads across Europe within weeks.
Vienna rises in March, and the old chancellor flees to England in a laundry cart.
The Austrian imperial parliament meets in the archbishop's palace at Kromeriz and drafts a liberal constitution.
Czech students and workers rise in Prague; Windischgratz shells the city and ends the Slav Congress.
Hungary declares its laws its own under Kossuth and fights Vienna for a year.
Marx and Engels publish their manifesto: a spectre is haunting Europe.
The house reading has mediums across London drawing real ghosts to their tables, and the Hierarchy watches every seance.
The house reading puts young Brujah at the Paris barricades, hoping the republic of 1848 can be the one that lasts.
The imperial parliament abolishes the labour dues of the peasants, and Moravian villages are free of the robot.
Gold is found on the American River days before California passes to the United States; the world rushes in.
Revolution breaks out in Paris in February 1848 and spreads to Vienna, Berlin, Milan and Budapest. Most of it is put down within a year. Fits: Round 1 has the Moravian side.
items.ref: Real history (1848).

items.x: Soldiers close the Kromeriz parliament and the young emperor imposes a constitution from above.
With Russian help, Austria crushes Hungary; the Hungarian army lays down its arms at Vilagos and thirteen generals are hanged.
French troops end Mazzini's Roman Republic and restore the pope; Garibaldi escapes.
The second Sikh war ends with the Punjab annexed and the Koh-i-Noor sent to the queen.
Hong Xiuquan, who believes himself Christ's younger brother, raises the Taiping; the war kills twenty million or more.

items.t: The Taiping and the Middle Kingdom
items.x: The house reading has the Kuei-jin courts of the south shaken as the Taiping burn temples and shrines across their lands.
The Bab is executed by firing squad at Tabriz; the first volley leaves the prisoner unhurt, and the faith grows.
Brno is made a statutory city and swallows its suburbs.
Northern officials and bystanders are bound by law to help return people who have escaped from slavery.
The Crystal Palace in Hyde Park shows the world's machines, and six million people come to see.
Louis Napoleon closes the assembly and makes himself master of France; within a year he is emperor.
Gold is found in New South Wales and Victoria, and the population of the colonies trebles in ten years.
An American medium holds paid seances in London, and table rapping becomes the fashion of the drawing rooms.
Napoleon III is proclaimed emperor of the French.
Commodore Perry's steamships anchor off Edo and demand that Japan open its ports.
Russia destroys an Ottoman squadron at Sinope with shell guns, and Britain and France move toward war.
The house reading has the Kindred who held the Spilberk prison as a feeding ground leave when it closes as a jail.
Britain and France land in the Crimea to besiege Sevastopol.
A misread order sends British light cavalry into the Russian guns at Balaclava.
Florence Nightingale's nurses reach the barracks hospital, where disease kills far more than Russian shot.
John Snow maps cholera deaths in Soho to a single pump and has its handle taken off.
Christian socialists open a college in London for working men.
Soldiers storm a stockade of gold diggers who had sworn by a flag of the Southern Cross.
After eleven months the Russians leave Sevastopol in flames.
Nicholas I dies; the new tsar Alexander II will free the serfs.
Paris answers London with its own Universal Exposition.
A former bandit is crowned Tewodros the Second and sets out to reunite Ethiopia.
David Livingstone is shown the great falls of the Zambezi and names them for the queen.
The Crimean War ends; the Black Sea is closed to warships.
Britain and France fight China again over a seized ship, the Second Opium War.
The sultan promises full equality to Christians and Jews, and the Muslim notables resent it.
A young prophetess tells the Xhosa to kill their cattle so that the ancestors will rise; tens of thousands starve.
Sepoys at Meerut mutiny over cartridges and march on Delhi; north India rises against Company rule.
British women and children held at Kanpur are killed; British vengeance across the north is terrible.
The house reading has the Ventrue of Calcutta and the Kuei-jin of the Ganges both feeding on the war while blaming each other.
Flaubert is tried for offending public morals with Madame Bovary and acquitted.
The emperor orders the old walls of Vienna pulled down for a grand boulevard.
The last Mughal emperor is tried and exiled to Rangoon, and the crown takes India from the Company.
A miller's daughter sees a lady in a grotto at Lourdes; the spring becomes a place of pilgrimage.
A hot summer makes the sewage in the Thames unbearable, and Parliament funds Bazalgette's sewers.
Darwin publishes the theory of natural selection and sets science against Genesis.
The house reading has the Union's men of science seize on Darwin as proof that the world runs by law, not spirit.
France and Piedmont beat Austria in a bloody day; a Swiss witness, Henri Dunant, will found the Red Cross.
A great solar storm sets telegraph lines sparking and lights auroras as far south as the Caribbean.
Ferdinand de Lesseps breaks ground on a canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
An abolitionist seizes a federal armoury to arm the enslaved and is hanged for it.
Garibaldi lands in Sicily with a thousand volunteers and conquers the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
Druze and Christian fighting in Mount Lebanon spreads to Damascus, where thousands of Christians die.
British and French troops loot and burn the Qing emperor's Summer Palace.
The house reading has the Inquisition's Society of Leopold shrunk to a few priests in Rome, keeping files no bishop reads.
A disputed land sale begins twelve years of war between the crown and Maori.
Victor Emmanuel becomes king of Italy.
Alexander II frees twenty-three million serfs, though they must buy their land in debt.
The prince consort dies of typhoid, and the queen wears black for the rest of her life.
Southern batteries fire on a federal fort, and four years of civil war begin.
Two explorers cross Australia from south to north and starve on the way back beside a river where the Yandruwandha live well.
Bismarck becomes minister-president of Prussia and promises iron and blood.
Victor Hugo publishes Les Miserables from exile.
Tyrs and Fugner found the Sokol gymnastic movement, and halls rise in every Czech and Moravian town.
Starving Dakota rise along the Minnesota River; thirty-eight are hanged in one day, the largest execution in American history.
A Mexican army beats a French one at Puebla; the French take Mexico City the next year and crown an Austrian archduke.
Poland rises against Russia again and fights for over a year in the forests.
The first underground railway opens between Paddington and Farringdon.
The house reading has London's Nosferatu furious as the Underground cuts through warrens they have held since the Romans.
A British squadron shells Kagoshima after a Satsuma samurai kills an English merchant.
Lincoln declares the enslaved of the rebel states free on New Year's Day, and in July the rebel invasion of the north is broken.
Ships begin bringing Pacific islanders to Queensland's cane fields, many by trickery or force.
An imperial army crosses into the lands of the Maori king, and millions of acres are confiscated.
Prussia and Austria take Schleswig and Holstein from Denmark.
Twelve states agree to protect the wounded and those who care for them.
Workers' leaders found the International Workingmen's Association in London.
Qing armies take the Taiping capital and kill over a hundred thousand; Hong Xiuquan is already dead.
Russia ends its war in the Caucasus by driving hundreds of thousands of Circassians to Ottoman lands; many die on the shore.
Colorado volunteers kill some hundred and fifty Cheyenne and Arapaho, mostly women and children, camped under a flag of truce.

items.t: The war of the Triple Alliance
items.x: Paraguay goes to war with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay and in six years loses most of its men.
Gregor Mendel reads the laws of heredity to the Brno natural history society; no one understands them for thirty-five years.
The house reading has a Technocrat visitor to the Brno monastery mark Mendel's work as a future paradigm and leave it unknown.
Russian troops take Tashkent and the conquest of Central Asia begins.
The main rebel army surrenders, the president is shot five days later, and slavery is ended by amendment at the end of the year.
A protest by black Jamaicans is put down with hundreds of hangings, and Britain argues for years over the governor's guilt.
Prussia crushes Austria in Bohemia in a single day, and the German question is settled.
Prussian troops occupy Brno after the Bohemian defeat; cholera follows the armies.
Austria and Prussia sign the preliminary peace at Mikulov castle; Austria is shut out of Germany.
The Austrian fleet rams and sinks Italian ironclads off Lissa in the Adriatic.
Crete rises against the Ottomans; the monks of Arkadi blow up their monastery rather than surrender.
The compromise makes the Habsburg lands a dual monarchy; Hungary rules itself and the Czechs get nothing.
The first volume of Marx's Capital is published.
The last Tokugawa shogun returns power to the emperor.
Paris holds another world fair, with Japanese prints that change European art.
The house reading has Irish Kithain hoping the Fenians win; a few eshu carry their letters across the sea.
Four British colonies join as the Dominion of Canada.
The republic of Benito Juarez shoots the emperor the French left behind.
A child finds a diamond near the Orange River, and the rush that follows remakes southern Africa.
The emperor's government defeats the shogun's last loyalists and moves to Edo, renamed Tokyo.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Japan split over the Meiji reforms; some court the new ministries, others retreat to the mountains.
Foundation stones from Czech mountains, Radhost among them, are laid for the National Theatre in Prague.
The last shogunate loyalists hold out at Hakodate under their Republic of Ezo and surrender the next spring.
A British expedition storms Tewodros's mountain fortress to free hostages, and the emperor shoots himself.

In the Meiji Restoration of 1868 the emperor moves to Edo, now Tokyo. Hakari, oldest of the undead in Japan, keeps court in the Imperial Palace from then on. Fits: Fits House Genji's rise with Japan in the late 1800s.
items.ref: Real history (1868); Hakari from Encyclopaedia Vampirica p. 89; the timing is a house reading.

items.x: The canal opens to shipping and the route to India is shortened by weeks.
The bishops meet in Rome and declare the pope infallible on faith and morals.
Mendeleev arranges the elements in a table that predicts ones not yet found.
The emir of Bukhara accepts Russian protection after defeat.
Rails laid largely by Chinese and Irish workers join the two coasts of the United States.
The French emperor surrenders at Sedan with his army, and the Second Empire falls.
The Prussians ring Paris; the city eats its horses, its rats and the zoo animals.

items.t: The Toreador starve with the city
items.x: The house reading has the Toreador of Paris feeding thin as the siege drags on and blood grows as scarce as bread.
Italian troops break into Rome through the Porta Pia, and the Papal States end.
The king of Prussia is proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
Paris rules itself for ten weeks; in the bloody week of May the army kills thousands of Communards.
The house reading has the Camarilla let the Commune burn to purge Brujah radicals, then blame the Sabbat for the fires.
Italy makes Rome its capital, and the pope shuts himself in the Vatican as a prisoner.
Bismarck fights the Catholic Church over schools and priests.
A fire burns for two days and leaves a third of Chicago homeless.
A newspaper's correspondent finds the missing missionary on Lake Tanganyika.
Sheridan Le Fanu publishes Carmilla, a vampire tale of a countess and a lonely girl in Styria.
The exiled Algerian emir, who saved thousands of Christians in 1860, lives on as a scholar in Damascus.
The Vienna stock exchange collapses days after the World's Fair opens, and a long depression follows.
Cholera kills thousands in Vienna during the exhibition, and visitors stay away.
Russia takes the khanate of Khiva and frees its slaves.
Under the guns of the British navy the sultan closes the slave market of Zanzibar; a cathedral is built on the site.
Painters refused by the Salon show their work together, and a critic mocks it as impressions.
A British expedition burns the Asante capital.
Cakobau cedes Fiji to Britain; measles brought home from a state visit to Sydney kills about a third of the Fijians the next year.
Blavatsky and Olcott found the Theosophical Society, and Eastern wisdom becomes a fashion in Europe.
The house reading has the Cult of Ecstasy and the Chakravanti watching the Theosophists closely, for some of what they teach is true.
Christian peasants rise against Ottoman tax collectors, and the Great Eastern Crisis begins.
Ottoman irregulars crush a Bulgarian rising and kill thousands at Batak; Gladstone writes of Bulgarian horrors.
The Ottomans proclaim a constitution and a parliament, which the sultan suspends within two years.
Wagner's whole Ring cycle opens in a theatre built to stage it.
Leos Janacek becomes a teacher and choirmaster in Brno; the town's music will carry Moravian folk song to the world.
Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors destroy Custer's command on the Little Bighorn.
The woman the colonists call the last Tasmanian dies in Hobart; her people's descendants live on.
The Ottomans hold Plevna against the Russians for five months before hunger breaks them.
Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India at a great durbar while famine kills millions in the south.
Saigo Takamori leads the last samurai rising against the new Japan and dies at Shiroyama.
Drought and grain exports kill five million or more in south and west India.
The house reading has the Stygian Hierarchy struggle to collect the souls from Plevna, and Renegades take many.
The powers redraw the Balkans: Serbia, Montenegro and Romania are free and Austria takes Bosnia to govern.
Austro-Hungarian troops occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina against fierce resistance.
Drought across north China kills nine million or more.
The house reading has Tzimisce of the Balkans see the Austrian occupation as a chance to push Camarilla influence south.
Swan and Edison light carbon filament lamps; the night changes.
The house reading has the night shrinking for the Kindred as electric light spreads, and the Weaver grows stronger in every lit street.
The British envoy at Kabul is murdered, and British troops occupy the city again.
Chile fights Peru and Bolivia for the nitrate desert, and Bolivia loses its coast.
The Zulu army destroys a British column at Isandlwana; the kingdom is broken by the end of the year.
An Afghan army wins at Maiwand, and Roberts marches three hundred miles to relieve Kandahar.
Brno opens horse trams, among the first in the Czech lands.
The bushranger who fought the police in home-made armour is hanged in Melbourne.
Revolutionaries of the People's Will kill the tsar with bombs on the Catherine Canal.
After the tsar's murder, mobs attack Jewish towns across the south of the empire, and emigration to America begins.
The new National Theatre in Prague burns before its formal opening; the nation pays to rebuild it in two years.
France occupies Tunisia.
A Sudanese holy man proclaims himself the Mahdi and raises the country against Egyptian rule.
The Royal Navy shells Alexandria, and a British army defeats Urabi at Tel el-Kebir.
The house reading has Egypt's mummies watching as British collectors empty tombs, and some go to London after their own bodies.
Prague's university is split into Czech and German halves.
Scholars found a society to test mediums, ghosts and thought transference.
The volcano blows apart, the sound is heard across the Indian Ocean, and sunsets turn red worldwide.
Some four hundred people die when the Ringtheater burns in Vienna during an opera.
France fights China and the Black Flags for northern Vietnam.
The European powers meet to share out Africa among themselves.
An international conference fixes the prime meridian at Greenwich and the world's time zones follow.
Germany takes the north-east of New Guinea and Britain the south-east.
Britain takes Mandalay in weeks and annexes Upper Burma.
Pasteur saves a boy bitten by a rabid dog with a new vaccine.
The house reading places the founding of the Arcanum in London, scholars sworn to study the hidden world without becoming part of it.
Serbia attacks Bulgaria and is beaten at Slivnitsa within two weeks.
The Mahdi's army storms Khartoum after a ten-month siege, and Gordon is killed two days before relief.
The Metis and their Cree allies rise on the Saskatchewan; Louis Riel is hanged for treason.
The powers recognise the king of the Belgians as the private owner of the Congo; millions die in the rubber terror that follows.
The house reading has every hidden power of Europe follow the flags into Africa and find the continent already held: by its own shapeshifters, its own undead and its own dead.
Stevenson publishes The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.
Ludwig II of Bavaria is declared insane and found dead in Lake Starnberg with the doctor who certified him.
Masaryk and others show that the medieval Czech manuscripts of Dvur Kralove and Zelena Hora are forgeries.
The last Apache band at war gives itself up and is sent to prison in Florida.
The richest goldfield in the world is found on the Witwatersrand.
Victoria marks fifty years on the throne, and kings come to London.
The Yellow River breaks its dykes and floods the plain; perhaps a million die.
The house reading has a mummy unwrapped before a London audience wake that night; the house rule notes the Reborn remember such things.
Three Freemasons found the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn in London.

items.t: The Golden Dawn and the Order
items.x: The house reading has the Order of Hermes recruit from the Golden Dawn, and a few of its members Awaken.
An unknown killer murders at least five women in Whitechapel, and the press calls the killer Jack the Ripper.
The house reading has London's Kindred fear a Masquerade breach in Whitechapel; the prince sends hounds after the killer.
Wilhelm I dies, Frederick III reigns ninety-nine days, and Wilhelm II takes the German throne.
The house reading has an Arcanum scholar keep notes on the Ripper that point away from the Kindred and toward a mortal doctor.
Brazil, the last country in the Americas to keep slavery, abolishes it; the empire falls the next year.
Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria and Mary Vetsera are found dead at the hunting lodge of Mayerling.
The tower is finished for the World's Fair, the tallest structure on earth.
Japan becomes a constitutional monarchy with a parliament on the Prussian model.
An influenza pandemic spreads by rail from Russia and kills about a million.
The young emperor drops the old chancellor.
Oscar Wilde publishes the tale of a portrait that ages while its sitter does not.
Japan's schools are bound to loyalty to the emperor.
Soldiers kill some three hundred Lakota, many of them Ghost Dancers, on Wounded Knee Creek.
The house reading has the Pure Ones' Garou among the dancers, and the dead of the plains answer the dance in the Shadowlands though the living cannot see them.
Prague holds a great exhibition and builds the Petrin lookout tower and a funicular.
Work begins on a railway across Siberia to the Pacific.
A great earthquake in central Japan kills seven thousand.
Persians stop smoking when the shah sells the tobacco trade to a British company; the shah backs down.
Unfiltered water spreads cholera through Hamburg and kills eight thousand, while Altona next door is spared.
The house reading has a Brno doctor's notes on a patient with no pulse who walks at night; the Arcanum buys them.
The Indian Councils Act lets Indians sit on the legislative councils.
A canal cut through rock opens across the isthmus of Corinth.
Young Czech radicals are tried and jailed, and Prague is placed under emergency law.
Dvorak writes his symphony From the New World far from home.
A chartered company's column with machine guns takes the Ndebele capital.
New Zealand is the first self-governing country where women vote for parliament.
Planters backed by American marines depose Queen Liliuokalani; the islands are annexed five years later.
A Jewish army captain is falsely convicted of spying and sent to Devil's Island; France splits for twelve years.
Japan defeats China in Korea and at sea, and takes Taiwan.
The sultan's irregulars kill Armenians in eastern Anatolia; over two years perhaps two hundred thousand die.
Bubonic plague reaches Hong Kong; Yersin finds its bacillus, and the disease spreads by ship to every continent.
The house reading has the fae of Brittany and Ireland feed on the poets of the Celtic revival, and the Dreaming grows brighter there.
The Lumiere brothers show moving pictures to a paying audience in a Paris cafe.
Rontgen finds rays that pass through flesh and show the bones.
Oscar Wilde is sentenced to two years' hard labour for gross indecency.
Prague shows peasant life from every Czech land, Moravian Wallachia and Slovacko among them.
Japanese agents murder Queen Min in the palace at Seoul and burn the body.
The Olympic Games return in Athens.
Becquerel finds that uranium salts fog photographic plates in the dark.
A tsunami strikes the coast of northern Japan and kills over twenty thousand.
Plague reaches Bombay and kills millions across India over the next two decades.

items.t: The Akashic Brotherhood shut the doors
items.x: The house reading has the Akashics close Tibetan monasteries to Western seekers after Theosophists come asking.
Gold is found on a creek in the Yukon, and a hundred thousand people set out for it.
The army of Menelik the Second destroys an Italian army at Adwa, and Ethiopia stays free.
British ships shell the sultan's palace at Zanzibar; the war lasts under an hour.
Victoria celebrates sixty years with troops from every corner of the empire.
Bram Stoker publishes Dracula: a Transylvanian count, his voyage to Whitby and the hunters who stop him.
The house reading has the Tzimisce furious at the book, the Tremere amused, and every hunter in England reading it twice.
The house reading follows Mage canon: the Order of Reason takes the name Technocratic Union at its 1897 convocation.
Herzl gathers the first Zionist Congress in Basel.
Vienna orders officials in Bohemia and Moravia to know Czech; German riots force the minister out.
One of the strongest earthquakes recorded strikes Assam and Shillong.
Greece fights the Ottomans over Crete and loses in a month.
The Brazilian army destroys a holy man's settlement in the backlands and kills nearly all its people.
A British expedition burns Benin City and carries off thousands of its brasses and ivories.
An anarchist stabs the empress of Austria with a file by the lake at Geneva.
The Guangxu emperor orders sweeping reforms; the empress dowager stops them and holds the emperor prisoner.
Kitchener's machine guns destroy the Mahdist army outside Omdurman.
Wilhelm II rides into Jerusalem through a gap cut in the wall.
Alfons Mucha of Ivancice, in Moravia, is the rage of Paris for his posters of Sarah Bernhardt.
An American battleship blows up in Havana harbour; within the year Spain loses Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines.
A Jewish vagrant is convicted of ritual murder at Polna; Masaryk defends Hilsner and is called a traitor.
The Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists attacks missionaries and Chinese Christians in Shandong.
The powers agree rules of war and found a court of arbitration.
Freud publishes the book that founds psychoanalysis.
The house reading has the Dreamspeakers and the fae both uneasy as Freud teaches the waking world to pick dreams apart.
The house reading has the Toreador of Vienna patron the Secession painters while the Ventrue fund their critics.
The Boer republics go to war with Britain; farms are burned and families held in camps, where tens of thousands die.
Germany and the United States divide Samoa between them.

Don Cerro brings the childe Theo Bell to Victorian London to learn to read Kindred society. In London Bell meets Angus Abranson, a friendship that lasts a century. Fits: The book has them meet about a hundred years before the late 1990s.
items.ref: Clan Novel Trilogy: Brujah 1, Slave Ring p. 35, and Brujah 2, The Overseer; the year is a house reading.

items.x: The Boxers and Qing troops besiege the foreign legations in Beijing for fifty-five days until an eight-nation army arrives.
The relief armies loot Beijing and punish the north China countryside; the court flees to Xi'an.
The house reading has some Kuei-jin courts feed the Boxer fury against foreign Kindred, and pay when the foreign armies arrive.
Paris holds the century's greatest fair, with moving walkways and the first Metro line.
Three botanists find Mendel's forgotten paper from Brno within months of each other.
Trade unions and socialists form a committee to send workers to Parliament.
Max Planck proposes that energy comes in small packets, and physics begins to change.
The Golden Dawn tears itself apart over Mathers and Crowley, and rival temples form.
The house reading has a Technocrat in Brno quietly delighted as Mendel's laws return; the Progenitors claim them.
A hurricane drowns at least six thousand people on the Texas coast.

items.t: The war of the Golden Stool
items.x: A British governor demands to sit on the Golden Stool, and the queen mother Yaa Asantewaa leads the Asante to war.
The queen dies at Osborne after sixty-three years, and Edward VII takes the throne.
Marconi receives a radio signal sent from Cornwall across the Atlantic.
Persia grants a British prospector the right to drill for oil across most of the country.
The Czech technical university opens in Brno.
Six colonies federate; among the first laws is one to keep the country white.
Britain ends its splendid isolation in an alliance with Japan.
The bell tower of St Mark's in Venice collapses into a heap of rubble.
King Chulalongkorn's reforms keep Siam independent between British and French empires.
A cloud of burning gas from the volcano kills nearly thirty thousand people in Saint-Pierre, Martinique, in minutes.
Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union: deeds, not words.
Officers murder King Alexander and Queen Draga of Serbia and throw their bodies from a window.
A mob kills forty-nine Jews over two days in Bessarabia while police watch.
Macedonian revolutionaries rise against the Ottomans and are crushed with village burnings.
Russian socialists split at their London congress, and Lenin's faction calls itself the majority.
Panama breaks from Colombia with American warships offshore and grants the canal zone within weeks.
